After the Singapore Major, we can expect new weapon skins to arrive with the upcoming CS2 updates. They can be perfect finishes to decorate with the stickers you earn from the Pick’Ems.
FAQs about CS2 Singapore Major Pick’Ems
When is the Singapore Major Pick’Em Challenge active in Counter-Strike 2?
Starting Nov. 18, you can place your predictions for Stage 1 of the Singapore Major. The Pick’Em challenges unlock the next prediction phases after each previous stage concludes. Stage 2 starts on Nov. 28. Stage 3 begins on Dec. 2. The Playoffs Pick’Em are available on Dec. 6.
How can I participate in the Pick’Em Challenge?
You need to purchase the Singapore 2026 Viewer Pass in-game. It grants full access to the Pick’Ems.
What can I earn from the CS2 Singapore Major Pick’Ems?
By submitting your predictions and making correct guesses, you upgrade your tournament coin and earn 300 tokens per tier upgrade. Up to 900 tokens are possible. You can spend these tokens in the in-game shop for event, team, and player autograph stickers — or use them to craft custom Souvenir weapons.
Is it possible to win all 900 tokens from the Pick’Em Challenges?
It is very difficult to achieve, as earning the full 900 tokens requires completing all 11 challenges for a flawless Diamond Coin run. Major predictions are notoriously chaotic and frequently ruined by miraculous underdog runs or favorites fails.
Is it financially profitable to invest in the Viewer Pass and Pick’Ems?
It can be profitable if you earn enough tokens and redeem them for high-demand team or player stickers. They can grow afterwards. It requires a lot of luck, though. For most players, purchasing the Viewer Pass is an investment in fun activities during the Major and in commemorative stickers from the tournament.

items.title: G2 Esports x Umbro: Every Piece in the New Football Streetwear Collection and What It Costs
items.content:
G2 Esports has teamed up with Umbro on a limited-edition football streetwear collection, and the five-piece set went on sale on 18 November. The joint announcement from Berlin describes it as the start of a longer partnership, with more news planned for early 2027. Prices on G2’s store run from €30 for the beanie to €110 for the hooded track jacket, and the full set costs €360.
The collection pairs Umbro’s football terrace heritage with G2’s branding in a deep forest green, finished with chequered tartan details and woven patches. It is sold through the G2 shop and on Umbro’s UK site. G2 teased the drop on X a day earlier with the line “Your new Fall uniform”, before confirming it was available on launch day.
Every piece in the G2 x Umbro collection and what it costs
There are five items in the range, and G2’s store gives each one its own product page with a short description. Prices below are from G2’s store in euros, with the US price in brackets, and other regions see their own currency. The Hooded Track Jacket is the most expensive piece, and buying all five at the listed prices comes to €360, or $538 in the US.
Hooded Track Jacket, €110 ($164): a relaxed track cut in deep forest green with off-white contrast piping and co-branded chest crests.
Long Sleeve Polo, €90 ($134): a 90s terrace design with Pine Grove and Bistro Green panels, a classic polo collar and high-density embroidery.
Track Pants, €80 ($120): relaxed wide-leg trousers in 235 GSM fabric, blacked out with forest green side panels.
Iconic T-Shirt, €50 ($75): heavyweight interlock cotton with raglan sleeves and co-branded chest detailing.
Beanie, €30 ($45): a cuffed jacquard knit in Bistro Green and Pine Grove.
The jacket and track pants are designed as a matching terrace set, and G2’s product pages point buyers from one to the other. The polo’s product page opens with the line “EST. 2015. STILL RUNNING THE PITCH.”, while the jacket’s page promises “terrace heritage” and a “villain mentality”. Every piece is co-branded, so this is a shared product line instead of a G2 kit with a sponsor logo added. The clothing is listed in sizes starting from XS, while the beanie comes in a single size.
What G2 and Umbro said about the partnership
Both companies framed the drop as more than a logo swap. “It is really special to partner with a deeply authentic brand like Umbro,” said Sabrina Ratih, chief operating officer of G2 Esports, in the announcement. “We wanted to do more than put two logos on a collection,” she added, describing team identity as something fans wear every day.
Markus Ley of Umbro Germany pointed to the overlap between the two audiences. “We are excited to bring Umbro’s rich sporting DNA into gaming and connect with a new generation of fans,” he said. Ley also said football and esports fans share the same passion, energy and sense of community, which is the idea the whole collection is built around. The announcement does not say who designed the pieces or where they are made, unlike G2’s own jerseys.
Umbro brings a long history to the deal. The brand was founded in 1924 by Harold Humphreys, and the announcement says more than 120 teams around the world wear its kit. Those range from club sides in England, Scotland, Argentina, Brazil, Spain and Portugal to several national teams. G2, for its part, says its fanbase is now more than 40 million people. It fields teams in League of Legends, Counter-Strike 2, VALORANT and Rainbow Six Siege, and its store also stocks a Rainbow Six Siege collaboration alongside the new range.
G2’s growing list of fashion collaborations
Umbro is not G2’s first big crossover this year. The organisation launched a G2 x One Piece streetwear collection in June, and its store is also selling its 2026 jerseys, which G2 says are made in Portugal. G2 has also been busy in mobile esports, and it ran a PUBG MOBILE community challenge this month, which Sky Esports won.
Brand deals and merchandise are a major source of income for esports organisations, and some partnerships become part of a team’s identity. FURIA’s long-running link with Hellmann’s, which we covered in our piece on the CS2 mayonnaise team, shows how far those partnerships can go. On the competitive side, G2 is still working through its 2027 League of Legends rebuild.
The G2 x Umbro range is listed as a limited edition, but neither company has said how many pieces were made or how long the drop will stay on sale. Both say this is only the first release of the partnership, and the next announcements are due in early 2027. Neither has said whether future drops will include a full football kit or anything made for G2’s players to wear on stage. The cheapest way into the set is the €30 beanie on the G2 store.

items.title: Intel reclaims desktop CPU market share from AMD in Q3 2026
items.content:
Intel reclaimed a significant chunk of desktop CPU market share from AMD during Q3 2026, according to new figures from Mercury Research. Intel's x86 desktop CPU shipment share rose from 65.1% in Q2 to 70.1% in Q3, while AMD's share fell from 34.9% to 29.9%, marking a five-percentage-point swing between the two chipmakers.
AMD spent much of the Ryzen era steadily gaining desktop market share from Intel. Q3 2026 moved in the opposite direction, with Intel gaining five percentage points while AMD lost the same amount.
The wider PC market remained challenging throughout the quarter. Separate figures from Jon Peddie Research (JPR) show that global client CPU shipments declined by 3.4% quarter-on-quarter and 6.5% year-on-year, falling to 60.8 million units. Desktop processor shipments were down 13% compared to the same period last year, while notebook CPU shipments declined by 4%.
The reasons behind Intel's desktop market share gain are not entirely clear. Mercury Research (via PCGamer) believes improved CPU availability may have contributed to the shift, while Intel's own financial results pointed to ongoing pressure across the client PC market due to higher component and memory costs. Regardless of the cause, Q3 was a positive quarter for Intel's desktop business after several years of AMD steadily chipping away at its market share.

items.title: Epic Takes Legal Action Against a Rocket League Cheat Seller, Bans Them From Every Epic Game
items.content:
Epic Games says it has taken legal action against a seller of Rocket League cheats, and the seller is now permanently banned from every Epic game. According to the publisher, they published a note, under the “Update on our fight against cheating”, alongside a short apology video from the seller. Epic’s post was blunt about the reason, stating that selling cheats is against its rules.
The video, titled “An Apology to the Rocket League Community” and hosted on YouTube, is a plain text statement on a black background. “I sold cheats for Rocket League and that wasn’t fair,” the seller says in it, adding that cheating ruins matches for everyone. The statement ends by confirming they have stopped selling cheats and are banned from Rocket League and all other Epic Games products.
What Epic said about the Rocket League cheat seller
Epic has not said what form the legal action took. Its post does not mention a lawsuit, a court, a settlement or any payment, and it does not say how long the seller had been operating. What it does confirm is the outcome: the cheats are no longer for sale, the seller has apologised publicly, and the ban covers Epic’s whole catalogue instead of Rocket League alone.
That last point matters, because a ban across Epic Games products cuts the seller off from Fortnite, Rocket League, Fall Guys and anything else tied to an Epic account. Epic’s community rules tell players not to cheat, grief or exploit bugs, and not to promote or advertise known cheats. Selling them goes a step further, which is why Epic chose legal action in this case.
We are not naming the seller or the product here. TalkEsport does not publish the names of cheat sellers or cheat tools, even in enforcement stories, so readers are not pointed towards them. Epic named the seller in its own post on X, and the apology video is public on YouTube.
Epic’s pattern of legal action and public apologies
This is not the first time Epic has paired legal action with a public message. In July 2025, the Newsroom account said Epic had taken legal action against two people, one who sold and used cheats and another who carried out DDoS attacks on creators while they were livestreaming. Both were ordered to stop and banned from Epic’s games.
Public apology videos have also become part of Epic’s approach. In February 2025, Fortnite Competitive announced that a player who broke tournament rules in a 2023 event had received a lifetime ban, given up their winnings and paid a fine that Epic donated to charity. That player also had to post a short apology video on YouTube, much like the one shared today.
The approach turns each case into a warning for others. Instead of quietly banning accounts, Epic is showing the community that cheat sellers face legal consequences and will be made to admit what they did in public. Riot Games has also taken a hard line on cheating this month, after it disqualified Team BONK for cheating in a VCT EMEA qualifier.
Why cheat sellers are Epic’s target in Rocket League
Rocket League is developed by Psyonix, which Epic bought in 2019, and the game went free to play in September 2020. Its ranked ladder and esports scene rely on fair matches, from the Rocket League Championship Series run by Psyonix to national team play. The game is also one of the 16 titles at the Esports Nations Cup. Going after the people who sell cheats targets the supply, instead of chasing each player who buys them.
The update landed on a busy day for Epic. Earlier on 18 November, Fortnite Status confirmed that island publishing through the Creator Portal was blocked by a backend error, and leakers pointed to a second Fortnite x Overwatch wave later this week. Epic has not linked the cheating update to either story, and its post on X focused only on the Rocket League case and the seller’s apology.
Epic has not said whether more cases are coming, though it framed the post as an update on an ongoing fight against cheating. The company’s enforcement updates appear on the same Newsroom account, which links to Epic’s news site. In the July 2025 case, both people were also ordered to stop and banned from its games.
The post Epic Takes Legal Action Against a Rocket League Cheat Seller, Bans Them From Every Epic Game appeared first on TalkEsport.

Krafton’s AI Horror Game MIMESIS Wins at the Korea Game Awards and Passes 2.4 Million Sales
items.content:
Krafton’s AI horror game MIMESIS has won an Excellence Award at the 2026 Korea Game Awards, and the publisher says the game has now sold more than 2.4 million copies worldwide. The co-op title from ReLU Games, a creative studio inside the BGMI and PUBG maker, picked up the prize at the ceremony at BEXCO in Busan on 18 November. Krafton’s announcement said judges rewarded the way the game builds artificial intelligence into its core design.
The Korea Game Awards are hosted by South Korea’s Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and organised by the Korea Association of Game Industry. Winners are judged on artistry, technology and popularity, with an expert panel counting for half of the score and public and media votes for a quarter each. MIMESIS shared the Excellence Award tier with Supercat’s Dokkaebi’s World and Com2uS’s MMORPG Zeus, while all four technical and creative awards went to Crimson Desert.
The night belonged to Pearl Abyss, whose Crimson Desert took the Grand Prize as part of the record eight-award haul we covered earlier. Crimson Desert has sold more than 6 million copies since its March release, according to the ministry. NC’s Aion 2 won the Prime Minister’s Award, while Nimble Neuron, the developer of Eternal Return, received the Esports Development Award. Culture minister Choi Hwi-young also used the evening to back a tax credit for game development.
How MIMESIS uses AI to turn friends against each other
MIMESIS is a four-player co-op horror game built around monsters that copy the people playing it. According to Krafton, the AI-driven enemies imitate a player’s appearance, actions and voice, so the person standing next to you might not be your teammate at all. The AI also reads its surroundings and reacts to what players do, which keeps the group guessing about who is real.
Krafton describes it as an “AI-native game”, meaning the AI is the main source of the experience instead of a background system. That design is what the Korea Game Awards judges singled out, according to the publisher. It also fits Krafton’s wider bet on AI, which in India includes a $250 million commitment to AI and deep tech startups announced in September.
ReLU Games has kept updating the monsters since launch. In October, to mark a year in Early Access, the studio released its second major update, called OFF THE RAILS. It added a feature that copies players’ habits and a new Paranoia system, both aimed at making the imitations harder to spot.
From CEDEC in Japan to 2.4 million sales
The Busan award is not the game’s first. In June, MIMESIS won an Excellence Award in the game design category at Japan’s CEDEC Awards 2026, which are handed out at the Computer Entertainment Developers Conference, Japan’s biggest event for game developers. Krafton says the win made it the first Korean game to take that prize in the category. It also took the multiplayer horror prize at the Japan Horror Game Awards.
Sales have grown alongside the awards since the game’s launch last year. MIMESIS launched in Early Access on Steam in October 2025 and passed one million copies within 50 days, according to Krafton. It crossed 2.4 million copies this month, and the publisher says its Steam user rating remains at Very Positive.
Those numbers make MIMESIS one of the clearest wins yet for Krafton’s creative studio model. ReLU Games is led by chief executive Kim Min-jung, and Krafton itself is run by chief executive Kim Chang-han. The publisher said the run of awards at home and abroad shows that an original IP built in-house can compete globally.
Why the award matters for Krafton beyond PUBG
Krafton’s revenue still leans heavily on PUBG: Battlegrounds and its mobile versions, including BGMI in India, where the BGMI 4.7 update rolled out this week. Krafton posted record revenue in 2025, driven largely by growth in BGMI and PUBG. A government award for a new IP gives the company another success story to point to as it tries to show it can build hits outside battle royale.
Krafton’s announcement does not mention a date for a full release, and the game is still sold through Steam’s Early Access programme. More details are on Krafton’s corporate site and the game’s Steam page. MIMESIS reached 2.4 million copies sold in November 2026, 13 months after it first went on sale.
The post Krafton’s AI Horror Game MIMESIS Wins at the Korea Game Awards and Passes 2.4 Million Sales appeared first on TalkEsport.

Esports Nations Cup 2027: Qualified Nations Keep Their Places, but No Player Is Safe
items.content:
Every country and territory that qualified for the Esports Nations Cup in 2026 will keep its place at the rescheduled Finals in November 2027. The Esports Foundation confirmed the decision on 18 November in its roadmap for the 2027 edition, which also adds bigger national rosters, a new ranking system and one last qualifying route for nations that missed out. For India, which had secured places in BGMI, chess, VALORANT and Trackmania, those places are safe, though the players who fill them are not guaranteed a trip to Riyadh.
The inaugural tournament was meant to run in Riyadh in November 2026 before the foundation postponed it by a year in August, citing its ongoing assessment of the wider regional situation. The Finals will now take place over four weeks in November 2027, still in Riyadh. Our report on the postponement covered how far India’s preparations had already gone at that point.
The decision protects a large 2026 qualifying season. According to the foundation’s figures, 189,105 players took part across 210 qualifiers, and 1,847 players from 123 countries and territories earned places at the Finals. “Representing your nation is one of the proudest moments in any athlete’s career,” said Ralf Reichert, chief executive of the Esports Foundation, in the official announcement.
How the Esports Nations Cup 2027 roster rules work
In team games, the players who qualified in 2026 become the core of each national squad and cannot be removed while rosters grow. Coaches can add eligible players to that pool until 15 January 2027, and keeping last year’s substitutes is optional. The expansion is meant to help teams react to changes in the game, club rules and player eligibility over the extra year.
The protection ends when the Finals squad is picked, though. Coaches choose their final line-up from the full expanded pool by 31 May 2027, and at that stage no player is guaranteed a spot. A player who helped a nation qualify in 2026 could be left out in favour of someone added this winter.
Solo titles work differently, because the place belongs to both the nation and the player who earned it. If that player withdraws, the spot passes to the next invited or qualified player and nation in line. Chess and Trackmania, two of India’s four titles, fall under this rule, so those places stay with the players who won them.
A second chance to qualify, except in CS2
Nations that missed out in 2026 get one more chance through regional online tournaments, which begin on 26 February 2027 and run for five weeks. The winners of seven regions then go to a global LAN qualifier in each title, joined by one nation invited through the foundation’s solidarity programme. Game-specific dates and the LAN details have not been announced yet.
Counter-Strike 2 is the one exception to the new qualifying route. The foundation said CS2 already filled every slot through the 2026 qualifiers, so there will be no new route into that event. Every other title will hold the extra regional tournaments, which include games with active Indian scenes such as EA FC and PUBG on PC.
A new ENC Ranking will also shape the Finals. Points are awarded to individual players for results in national team events and in club competitions, from international events to regional and national leagues, and they decay over a rolling 24-month window. The ranking will decide seeding for the Finals and help determine direct invites to future editions, with the full list of counting tournaments due early in 2027.
What the changes mean for India’s national teams
India’s National Team Partner is NODWIN Gaming, with Akhil Kavuturu listed as the national team manager on the official ENC site. NODWIN now has until 15 January 2027 to add players to India’s squads, and until the end of December 2026 to pitch events of its own. The foundation says partner-led events can include friendly matches, community events and multi-nation invitationals, supported by the ENC Development Fund.
The biggest call will come in BGMI, where India’s roster was announced in July 2026 for the PUBG Mobile event. That competition was set to feature 32 teams and 128 athletes with a $1,320,000 prize pool, according to the official event page. With the final line-up no longer protected, the squad that represents India in 2027 could look quite different from the one named last summer.
CS2 is the clear loss for India under the new rules. The country played the 2026 CS2 qualifiers, but CS2 was not among its four confirmed titles, and with no new CS2 route, India will not be in that event at the 2027 Finals. India can still chase places through the regional tournaments starting in February, and the foundation says partner events will stay inside the existing two-week Club Release window, adding no extra availability demands on players.
The wider calendar for national team esports is busy as well. The Asian Esports and Mind Sports Games are also set for 2027 in Kuwait, and the foundation previously launched its rankings and Team Builder platform in May. The inaugural Esports Nations Cup Finals are now scheduled to begin in November 2027 in Riyadh, a full year after their original date.
The post Esports Nations Cup 2027: Qualified Nations Keep Their Places, but No Player Is Safe appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Acer launches 34-inch 5K ultrawide gaming monitors with dual-mode refresh rates
items.content:
Acer has launched two new 34-inch ultrawide gaming monitors that can switch between a full 5K ultrawide resolution and a lower-resolution high-refresh mode. The new Nitro ED340CKR Pbmiipx and ED340CKR Jbmiipx are built around 1500R VA panels with a native 5120×2160 resolution.
According to DisplaySpecifications, the two monitors differ primarily in refresh rates. The ED340CKR Pbmiipx reaches up to 180Hz at 5120×2160 or 360Hz when switched to 2560×1080, while the ED340CKR Jbmiipx tops out at 120Hz and 240Hz respectively. Both displays also support AMD FreeSync Premium, 1ms response times, Black Boost and Acer's GameView presets.
Both monitors offer 90% DCI-P3 colour coverage, 8-bit + FRC colour depth and a matte anti-glare finish. Acer rates brightness at 250 nits and includes its VisionCare suite with BlueLightShield and Flicker-less technologies.
Connectivity includes two HDMI 2.1 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4 connection and a headphone jack. Both monitors also include integrated speakers and a tilt-adjustable stand. Currently, the displays are only available in Japan, where the ED340CKR Jbmiipx is priced at ¥69,800 (£333), while the higher-end ED340CKR Pbmiipx sells for ¥99,980 (£476).

items.title: GTA 6 includes advanced ray tracing even on base consoles
items.content:
Today has been a huge day for Rockstar, with GTA 6 earning over 100 perfect review scores ahead of its release at midnight tonight. However, the most interesting review around comes from Digital Foundry, whose technical analysis gives us a much clearer look at graphical features and performance across Xbox and PlayStation consoles. Most notably, the team confirmed the presence of ray-traced global illumination (RTGI) and ray-traced reflections across all console versions of the game.
A few weeks ago, Rockstar was still being fairly cagey about the game's graphical feature set, only confirming ray-traced shadows as a PS5 Pro enhancement. Based on that information, I speculated that the standard consoles may not feature ray tracing at all. The logic was straightforward enough – RT shadows are one of the least taxing forms of ray tracing to run, so if that was being reserved for PS5 Pro, it seemed unlikely to me that more expensive features like RTGI would be running on the base consoles.
As it turns out, that assessment was wrong. Digital Foundry's analysis confirms that Rockstar has included RTGI and ray-traced reflections across the entire console lineup, with PS5 Pro receiving additional ray-traced shadow enhancements on top.
So the game looks amazing, as expected, but how does it run? Well, that is where some cracks start to show. According to Digital Foundry, the PS5 Pro holds a rock-solid 30FPS target during normal gameplay, with frame-rate drops only appearing during extreme stress-test scenarios involving large numbers of explosions and physics interactions. The standard PS5 is less stable, with frame-rate dips occurring more frequently during ordinary gameplay situations like driving through the city.
The Xbox Series X has a very similar performance profile to the standard PS5, while Xbox Series S struggles most often, as should be expected given its weaker GPU. Despite that, Rockstar has still managed to preserve much of GTA 6's visual identity on the entry-level console. That should be encouraging news for PC players, suggesting Rockstar's renderer is capable of scaling across a fairly broad range of hardware configurations ahead of the inevitable PC release.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches tomorrow, November 19
items.content:
Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive.
Grand Theft Auto VI arrives on PlayStation 5 Thursday, November 19, available at PlayStation Store.
When the sun fades and the neon glows, everyone has something to gain — and more to lose
The game is set in the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond in the biggest, most immersive evolution of the series yet.
Jason Duval
Jason grew up around grifters and crooks. After a stint in the Army trying to shake off his troubled teens, he found himself in the Keys doing what he knows best, working for local drug runners. Meeting Lucia could be the best or worst thing to ever happen to him. Jason knows how he’d like it to turn out but right now, it’s hard to tell.
Lucia Caminos
Lucia’s father taught her to fight as soon as she could walk, and life has been coming at her swinging ever since. Fighting for her family landed her in the Leonida Penitentiary. Sheer luck got her out but now more than anything, Lucia wants the good life her mom has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City. Instead of half-baked fantasies, Lucia is prepared to take matters into her own hands.
The sprawling state of Leonida
Leonida is made up of six regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga. Here’s a closer look at what makes each region unique.
Vice City
The glamour, hustle, and greed of America captured in a single city. Each neighborhood has something to offer, from the pastel art deco hotels and bright white sands of Ocean Beach, to the bustling panaderías of Little Cuba and the bootleg brands of the Tisha-Wocka flea market, out to the VC Port, the cruise ship capital of the world. We’re a long way from the ’80s, but Vice City is still the sun and fun capital of America
Leonida Keys
Life in this tropical archipelago isn’t flashy but it’s easy. Get your buzz on and pull up a deck chair but look out — you are right on the doorstep of some of the most beautiful and dangerous waters in all of America.
Grassrivers
You never know what lies beneath the surface of this primordial expanse. The gators may be the most famous attraction, but there are far deadlier predators and weirder discoveries among the mangroves.
Port Gellhorn
Cheap motels, shut-down attractions, and empty strip malls won’t bring the tourists back, but there’s a new economy in this once-popular vacation spot. It’s fueled by malt liquor, painkillers, and truck stop energy drinks.
Ambrosia
In the heart of Leonida, American industry and old school values still reign supreme — whatever the cost. The Allied Crystal sugar refinery provides the jobs, while the local biker gang provides almost everything else.
Mount Kalaga
A national landmark up against the state’s northern border, Mount Kalaga offers prime hunting, fishing, and off-road trails. In the lush surrounding backwoods, hillbilly mystics and paranoid radicals live far from the prying eyes of the government.
Broadcasting live across Leonida
Spanning stations including Classic Rock, Modern Hip-Hop, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latin, ‘80s, Electronic, Blues, Ballads, Talk Radio, and much more, Grand Theft Auto VI features the biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet.
Plus, for the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto VI introduces a series of on-demand podcasts for Jason and Lucia to experience beyond Leonida’s terrestrial radio, with both radio and podcasts available to listen to in vehicles and on foot through newly introduced headphones and earbuds connected to their smartphones.
Grand Theft Auto VI
Available November 19

How to play GTA 6 early: New Zealand trick for PS5 and Xbox
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) just became available in New Zealand today on Nov. 18. How are people playing GTA 6 early, and can players in the United States access it before the official release? Here’s our guide on the New Zealand trick for GTA 6.
Key takeaways
GTA 6 became playable in New Zealand on November 19 due to the time zone difference.
The GTA 6 New Zealand trick involves changing your console’s region to New Zealand to access the game early if you live elsewhere.
Xbox Series X|S players can change their location by going into “Settings,” “System,” and “Language & location” before restarting their console.
PlayStation 5 owners need a new New Zealand account and must get GTA 6 again using New Zealand’s currency.
Table of contents
Is GTA 6 out in New Zealand?
GTA 6 countdown
How to play GTA 6 early
How to play GTA 6 early on Xbox
How to play GTA 6 early on PS5

GTA 6 FAQs
Is GTA 6 out in New Zealand?
Yes, GTA 6 is now playable in New Zealand since it’s already Nov. 19 there due to the time zone difference. This means folks in North America must wait until Nov. 19 midnight to play the game. No matter where you’re located, GTA 6 launches locally for you at midnight.
GTA 6 COUNTDOWN
GTA 6 countdown
Here is our live countdown to GTA’s release date and time for those in the Pacific Daylight Time (PDT) time zone.
Lucia and Jason in GTA 6 (Image credit: Rockstar Games)
How to play GTA 6 early
The New Zealand trick involves changing your console’s location to New Zealand to make the game become available ahead of time.
Do note that the following methods for Xbox Series X|S and the PlayStation 5 are not officially guaranteed by Rockstar Games. Regional restrictions and purchasing requirements may still affect access.
GTA 6 screenshot (Image credit: Rockstar Games)
How to play GTA 6 early on Xbox
Go into the “Settings” option
Select the “System” tab
Choose the “Language & location” option
Go into the “Location” option
Change your location to New Zealand
Press the “Restart now” button
To play GTA 6 early on Xbox Series X|S, go into your “Settings,” select “System,” and choose “Language & location.” Next, select the “Location” option and change it to New Zealand. Finally, press the “Restart now” button on the screen.
Cal Hampton in GTA 6 (Image credit: Rockstar Games)
How to play GTA 6 early on PS5
If you’re on the PlayStation 5, then you must create a new account on your console and set your region to New Zealand. However, the catch is that you must get GTA 6 again using New Zealand’s currency.
Vice City (Image credit: Rockstar Games)
Is GTA 6 on PC?
No, at the time of writing and publishing this guide, GTA 6 is not available on PC. However, according to a GamesBeat report, the game will launch on PC sometime in Q1 of 2027.

Yes, GTA 6 became playable in New Zealand on Nov. 19 because of the time zone difference. Players in other regions must wait until their local midnight release time.
How are people playing GTA 6 early?
Players are using the New Zealand trick to play GTA 6 early, which involves changing their console’s location or account region to New Zealand.
How do I play GTA 6 early on Xbox Series X|S?
To play GTA 6 ahead of time on Xbox Series X|S, go into “Settings,” “System,” “Language & location,” and change your region to New Zealand. Then, select “Restart now.”
How do I play GTA 6 early on PS5?
PlayStation 5 owners need to create a new PlayStation account with New Zealand as its region. However, they must purchase GTA 6 again using New Zealand’s currency.
Is the GTA 6 New Zealand trick officially supported by Rockstar Games?
No, Rockstar Games has not officially guaranteed that the New Zealand trick will work. Regional restrictions and purchasing requirements may still affect access.
Is GTA 6 available on PC?
No, GTA 6 is not available on PC at launch. According to a report, a PC release is expected sometime in Q1 of 2027.

items.title: Sam Houser Breaks His Silence on GTA 6 Launch Week: ‘We Hope You Have Fun’
items.content:
Rockstar Games co-founder Sam Houser has spoken publicly about Grand Theft Auto VI on the eve of its release, which is something he almost never does. In a statement given to GamesRadar+ on 18 November, Houser said Rockstar is “incredibly grateful” as the game finally reaches players. He also set out what the studio was trying to build with its first new Grand Theft Auto in 13 years.
The statement arrives hours before GTA VI unlocks worldwide on 19 November, on PS5 and Xbox Series X and S. It also lands in the middle of Rockstar’s biggest launch week, with record review scores, a jump in Take-Two shares and a Miami festival all in the same few days. At the time of writing, the statement had not been posted on Rockstar’s own X account or website.
What Sam Houser said about GTA VI and Vice City
Houser opened by going back to the studio’s founding idea. He said Rockstar “was founded on the belief that games could achieve the same distinction as all other forms of storytelling” and could become part of modern culture. “This week, Grand Theft Auto returns to Leonida and modern-day Vice City,” he wrote, before adding that one thing still holds true despite how much time has passed.
He then described the team’s goal in plain terms. Rockstar has “tried to create an experience that will exceed your expectations while showing what this medium is capable of”, Houser said, and he addressed both long-time fans and players who are new to the series. He called the game a story set in a world of possibilities, where it is up to the player “to shape how it ultimately feels, and concludes.”
The rest of the statement was aimed at players directly. Houser said Rockstar hopes the game feels both familiar and entirely new, and that above all it hopes players have fun. He closed by saying Rockstar looks forward to “many more years of sharing these experiences with you”, the only hint in the statement about Rockstar’s plans beyond launch day.
Why a Sam Houser statement is so rare
Sam Houser co-founded Rockstar in 1998 and holds an executive producer credit on every mainline Grand Theft Auto game. His brother Dan Houser, who co-wrote the series for years, left Rockstar in 2020. Sam rarely gives interviews, which is why a launch-week statement under his own name stands out.
The last time he spoke this directly about GTA VI was the reveal in December 2023. In the announcement released by Rockstar, Houser said the game would “push the limits of what’s possible in highly immersive, story-driven open-world experiences”. That release promised a 2025 launch, and the game was later delayed twice, first to 26 May 2026 and then to 19 November 2026.
Those delays are part of why this week’s statement leans so heavily on gratitude. Rockstar’s parent company Take-Two Interactive is guiding for $8.0 billion to $8.2 billion in net bookings this financial year, with GTA VI at the centre of that forecast. Fans, meanwhile, spent almost three years between the first trailer and release day. Houser’s message reads as a thank you for that patience as much as a pitch for the game.
GTA VI’s launch week in numbers
The early numbers suggest the wait paid off. As of 3 hours after launch, GTA VI held a 99 Metascore from 147 critics and a 98 on OpenCritic, with every critic recommending it, as our GTA 6 reviews roundup tracks. Take-Two shares were up about 6% at $216.17 at the same time, after bouncing on the first reviews.
Rockstar is also marking the launch with a party in Miami. GTA VI: The Festival takes over Mana Wynwood on 21 November with Travis Scott, Cardi B and Metro Boomin, and Rockstar’s festival page says the event is presented with PlayStation. In a post on X, Rockstar said all proceeds from ticket sales will go to local Miami charities.
Players who are already in the game can follow every unlock, server update and record on our GTA 6 launch live blog. Those who finish the story can also use the 61 cheat codes it unlocks. Grand Theft Auto V first released on 17 September 2013, which makes GTA VI’s launch on 19 November the longest gap between mainline games in the series.

items.title: Fortnite Creators Portal Error: Can’t Publish Islands Update
items.content:
Fortnite creators cannot publish islands through the Live Creator Portal right now, and Epic Games has confirmed the problem is on its side. Epic Games confirmed on 18 November that publishing was “blocked due to backend dependency returning an unexpected error”. They said it is looking into a fix, but it has not shared a time for when publishing will work again.
The wording points to a service the Creator Portal relies on failing, not to the portal itself being offline.
What Epic has confirmed about the Creator Portal error
The Creator Portal is where Fortnite developers manage their islands, submit builds for review and push approved versions live. When publishing is blocked, a creator who has finished a new island or a patch for an existing one cannot release it to players. Epic’s post only covers publishing, and it has not reported any problem with playing islands that are already live.
Every new island and every update has to pass Epic’s review before it can go live, which is why rejection notes also sit inside the portal. The error does not appear to affect work in Unreal Editor for Fortnite, where creators build islands and run private test sessions before they submit. That means teams can keep building today, but nothing they finish can reach players until Epic clears the fault.
Epic’s public status page showed no open incident when we checked shortly after the post, with its UEFN and publishing components still marked as operational. That leaves the post on X as Epic’s only public word on the error so far. The same page logged a short Easy Anti-Cheat incident on 14 November, which Epic marked as resolved once service returned to normal.
Epic has been changing the portal recently as well. On 2 November, the Fortnite Developers account said rejection notes in the Creator Portal can now include gameplay video, flagged image previews, audio files and the reviewed thumbnail. Epic has not linked today’s error to that update or to any other change.
Why a publishing outage hits Fortnite creators’ payouts
Publishing delays matter because Fortnite pays creators by engagement. Epic’s engagement payout documentation says 40% of eligible net revenue from the Item Shop goes into a pool shared between islands. That pool is split using a formula built on playtime, retention and new players, and engagement is measured across each calendar month.
An island that misses a planned update loses the chance to pull players back during that window. Creators also have a second income stream this year, because Epic opened in-island item sales in January and is paying developers 100% of the V-Bucks value until 31 January 2027, according to its official announcement. Any update that adds new items to sell is stuck until publishing comes back.
The timing is awkward for the whole Fortnite ecosystem. Grand Theft Auto VI launches worldwide on 19 November, and our GTA 6 launch live blog is already tracking Twitch viewership for Rockstar’s game. Fortnite is also in its Treasure Hunters mini season, which began on 1 November with update v43.00 and bridges Chapter 7 Season 4 and Chapter 8.
A busy week for Fortnite Status
The publishing error follows several other fixes and clarifications from the same account this week. On 17 November, Fortnite Status said a chest-opening animation plays wrongly when a player finds a reward they already own but a party member does not, and Epic is working on a visual fix.
The token is still a sore point with the community. At least one reply to today’s outage post ignored the Creator Portal entirely and demanded better token odds, a week after the #ReleaseTheOdds campaign asked Epic to publish them. Epic has still not shared those odds with players.
The account also linked a support article on 17 November for players stuck on a “processing Reboot” screen and unable to respawn. All of this comes less than a week after AWS’s US-EAST-1 region went down again on 15 November. Epic’s latest post on the Creator Portal error, at 8:28pm Indian time, still listed the issue as under investigation.
The post Fortnite Creators Portal Error: Can’t Publish Islands Update appeared first on TalkEsport.

Kiriko and Widowmaker Are Coming to Fortnite on November 20, Leakers Say
items.content:
Kiriko and Widowmaker are the next Overwatch heroes heading to Fortnite, and leakers say both land in the Item Shop on Friday, 20 November. The leaker Jorge_Most posted the wave 2 list on 18 November, naming two outfits, two back blings, two pickaxes, an emote, a pair of kicks and a wrap. HYPEX and ShiinaBR shared the same set within the hour, and ShiinaBR added that an in-game reveal should follow within 24 hours.
KIRIKO & WIDOWMAKER FORTNITE SKINS DROP ON FRIDAY
– 2 Skins, 2 Back Blings, 2 Pickaxes, 1 Emote, 1 Kicks, 1 Wrap
– In-Game Reveal in 24 HOURS pic.twitter.com/hR7A6m4uPw
— Shiina (@ShiinaBR) November 18, 2026
ShiinaBR’s 18 November post listing the Kiriko and Widowmaker bundle
Neither Epic Games nor Blizzard has confirmed the drop yet. The official Fortnite account has spent the past few days promoting Cap’n Hatsune Miku and Kasane Teto, while Overwatch’s channels were busy with the OWCS World Finals Cheer Rally. The same leakers did call wave 2 early, with Jorge_Most reporting on 13 November that Overwatch sneakers had been decrypted and the second wave was coming this month.
Every Kiriko and Widowmaker cosmetic in the leak
The leaked bundle follows the shape of the first Overwatch drop, with a full set for each hero instead of a lone skin. Most of the detail comes from HYPEX’s 13 November breakdown of the encrypted files, which had passed 850,000 views on X by 18 November. That post confirmed Kiriko and listed a second, unnamed female hero as either Juno or Widowmaker, and this week’s lists settle it as Widowmaker.
Kiriko outfit: glowing body and head effects, flowing clothes with physics, a custom lobby animation and a LEGO Style.
Widowmaker outfit: a glowing body, a glowing head accessory, hair physics, a custom lobby animation and a LEGO Style.
Two back blings: Kiriko’s glows, and Widowmaker’s animated pickaxe may also be wearable on the back.
Two pickaxes: Widowmaker’s has its own ready sound and trail.
One emote: it uses a prop and plays a special version when Kiriko performs it.
One pair of kicks: Kiriko-themed sneakers that leave footprints and a small trail.
One wrap: a spray also appeared in the 13 November files but is missing from this week’s lists.
Both outfits carry LEGO Styles, so they should also work in LEGO Fortnite and other LEGO islands, as the wave 1 heroes do. Kiriko’s set looks the more complete of the two, with her own kicks and an emote that changes when she performs it. ShiinaBR has already shared a short gameplay clip of those kicks from the 13 November files.
Kiriko is a support hero who joined the game when Overwatch 2 launched in October 2022. Blizzard’s Kiriko hero page describes her as a shrine maiden from Kanezaka in Japan who heals with ofuda and fights with kunai. Widowmaker is a damage sharpshooter from the original 2016 roster, the French assassin Amélie Lacroix, so wave 2 pairs one of the newer stars with one of the oldest.
Epic has not listed V-Bucks prices, and none of the leakers has posted them. Players who found a Pirate Shop Token during Treasure Hunters could still claim the set for free during an active 14-day window. That only works if Epic sells the items for V-Bucks, because the token excludes Packs sold for real money.
Kiriko and Widowmaker Fortnite release time in India and the US
Jorge_Most and ShiinaBR both give the date as 20 November, which falls on a Friday. Fortnite’s Item Shop resets at 00:00 UTC, so a US release on 20 November usually means 7pm ET that evening. Portuguese and German-language leak accounts have converted the drop to 9pm Brasília time on 20 November and 1am Central European time on 21 November, which is the same reset.
In India, that reset falls at 5:30am on Saturday, 21 November, Indian time. In the UK it is midnight going into Saturday, and on the US West Coast it is 4pm on Friday afternoon. Our guide to when the Fortnite Item Shop changes has the reset in every other time zone.
Epic has not confirmed a time, so the bundle could still move by a shop cycle in either direction. One Portuguese-language leak account added that the item files should unlock on 19 November, a day before the listed release. That lines up with ShiinaBR’s note that an in-game reveal is due within 24 hours of the leak.
How wave 2 follows the first Fortnite x Overwatch drop
Epic confirmed the first wave on 12 May with a teaser that read “Answer the Call 5.14”, and D.Va, Genji, Tracer and Mercy arrived on 14 May in Act III of Chapter 7 Season 2. Epic’s official news post listed all four outfits with matching accessories and LEGO Styles. It also added an Overwatch Porsche Cayenne EV bundle and a Payload at King’s Row Tower that rewarded everyone who escorted it home.
All four of those heroes came from Overwatch’s 2016 launch roster, which makes Kiriko the first post-launch Overwatch hero to make the jump. Fortnite is now in the Treasure Hunters mini season, which began with update v43.00 on 1 November and bridges Chapter 7 Season 4 and Chapter 8. That season has already brought One Piece items, including Zoro’s Three Sword Style, so the Overwatch pair lands in a crowded shop.
Overwatch itself is in the final weeks of Season 5, which runs until 7 December. Blizzard has already confirmed a four-week 6v6 Role Queue test for the start of Season 6, and the OWCS World Finals Cheer Rally starts on 24 November. If the leaks hold, Kiriko and Widowmaker take Fortnite’s Overwatch roster to six heroes, just over six months after the first four arrived on 14 May.

items.title: Tomb Raider studio hit with yet another round of layoffs
items.content:
Crystal Dynamics has confirmed yet another round of layoffs, marking the fifth time the studio has reduced headcount in less than two years. While only eight employees are affected this time, the latest cuts bring the total number of jobs lost during that period to roughly 70.
In a statement provided to PC Gamer, Crystal Dynamics described the decision as a “necessary business” move and insisted that no ongoing projects would be impacted. The latest cuts also come just eight months after the studio's previous round of redundancies, bringing the total number of employees lost over the past two years to roughly 70.
Crystal Dynamics is currently developing two major Tomb Raider projects, with Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis now targeting a 2027 release and Tomb Raider: Catalyst planned for 2028. While the studio continues to insist that development remains unaffected, the latest cuts come just eight months after the previous round of layoffs and mark the fifth reduction in staff at the studio in less than two years.
Crystal Dynamics spent several years co-developing the Perfect Dark reboot before Microsoft cancelled the project and closed The Initiative in 2025. Since then, the company has undergone multiple rounds of restructuring while simultaneously navigating delays across its two announced Tomb Raider titles. Taken individually, the loss of eight employees is not particularly significant. The latest cuts bring Crystal Dynamics to five rounds of layoffs in less than two years, despite the studio currently working on multiple Tomb Raider projects.
KitGuru says: Hopefully Crystal Dynamics is being truthful when it says Tomb Raider is unaffected. We'll know for sure pretty soon, as Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis is due out in just a couple of months.

GTA 6 hits 6.38 million viewers and counting
On Nov. 18, GTA 6 reached more than 6.38 million concurrent viewers just hours after its launch in New Zealand. According to preliminary data from Streams Charts, this marked a new livestreaming record, surpassing VALORANT’s 2020 closed beta peak of 1.74 million viewers.

items.title: Take-Two Shares Bounce on GTA 6 Reviews After a 10% Pre-Launch Sell-Off
items.content:
Take-Two Interactive’s shares jumped on Wednesday as the first GTA VI reviews pushed the game to a 99 Metascore, but the rebound has not yet erased a sharp slide in the days before launch. The stock opened at $212.64 and was trading at $218.46 at 9:39am New York time, or 8:09pm in India, up 7.1% on Tuesday’s close, according to Yahoo Finance. That put it well ahead of the Nasdaq Composite, which was up only 0.3% at the same point.
The early gain recovers about 60% of a two-day drop that took the shares from $227.82 on Friday to $203.93 on Tuesday, a fall of 10.5%. Take-Two is still below where it finished last week and well short of its 52-week high of $265.65. With a market value of about $40.4 billion shortly after the open, every one percent move now shifts the company’s value by roughly $400 million.
Take-Two shares through GTA VI launch weekDaily closing price in US dollars, 3 to 17 November 2026, plus early trading on 18 November$190$200$210$220$230$240-10.5% in two days3 Nov4 Nov5 Nov6 Nov9 Nov10 Nov11 Nov12 Nov13 Nov16 Nov17 Nov18 Nov*$231.31$203.93$218.46Q2 resultsReviews land*18 November price at 9:39am New York time (8:09pm Indian time). Source: Yahoo Finance.
How Take-Two stock moved before GTA 6 launched
The run-up to launch has been anything but smooth for Take-Two investors. Shares jumped 8.3% on 10 November, the day after the company reported second-quarter results in which net bookings fell 18% to $1.60 billion. Take-Two kept its forecast of $8.0 billion to $8.2 billion in net bookings for the year, and chief executive Strauss Zelnick said GTA VI pre-orders were “continuing to reach unprecedented levels”.
The stock peaked at $231.31 on 11 November, then gave back almost all of that gain in two sessions this week. It fell 6.3% on Monday and another 4.5% on Tuesday, on roughly double the trading volume of the previous Thursday and Friday. Financial site TipRanks linked the slide mainly to a wider sell-off in technology stocks.
The index figures only explain part of that move, however. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.5% on Monday and 0.7% on Tuesday, a fraction of Take-Two’s drop, and Quiver Quantitative suggested traders were locking in gains before the launch. Trefis went further and asked whether a GTA VI that merely met guidance could hurt the shares, which made Wednesday’s reviews the first real test of the launch.
The price levels around Take-Two’s GTA 6 rebound
On the chart, Wednesday’s session opened with a gap of about 4.3% above Tuesday’s close, and the shares touched $221.00 in early trading. The obvious reference points above are last week’s closing prices between $227 and $231, where the stock topped out before the sell-off. Below, Tuesday’s low of $201.66 marks the bottom of the pre-launch slide that Wednesday’s rebound has moved away from.
Trading was busy from the opening bell on Wednesday. About 1.7 million shares had changed hands by 9:37am New York time, already more than half the full-day volume of last Thursday or Friday. Whether that pace holds through the session will show how much of the early jump reflects lasting conviction rather than short-term positioning.
Analysts were already upbeat before the reviews arrived. TipRanks counts 17 Buy ratings over the past three months and an average price target of $290.50, about a third above Wednesday’s early price. It also noted that the shares were down about 17% for the year before this week’s rebound, and this article is for information only rather than investment advice.
The GTA 6 numbers Take-Two investors are waiting for
Reviews are only the first data point for the market. In its second-quarter results release, Take-Two guided for $3.35 billion to $3.5 billion in net bookings for the October to December quarter, which includes the launch. That forecast is more than double the $1.60 billion it booked from July to September. Sensor Tower estimated before release that GTA VI pre-orders had already generated $1.18 billion, as we reported in our story on GTA 6’s pre-order revenue.
The critical reception could hardly be stronger for the company’s biggest release. GTA VI holds a Metascore of 99 from 147 reviews on Metacritic, the same score as The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, as our GTA 6 review roundup covers. Launch-day viewing has already broken streaming records, which we are tracking in our GTA 6 launch live blog.
The game unlocks at midnight local time on 19 November in each region, reaching India at 12am and the US East Coast at 10:30am Indian time. Take-Two’s investor relations site has not yet given a date for its first sales update on GTA VI. The company’s next scheduled earnings report covers the October to December quarter.

GTA VI’s money cheat will stand out for long-time fans, because GTA V never had a cheat that simply handed players cash. Single-player cheats are also separate from cheating in online modes, which Rockstar’s policy on posting its material does not allow creators to promote.

Cobblestone Returns to CS2: How to Play the Iconic Map
items.content:
One of the most popular maps of Counter-Strike has returned to the game with the latest update, and fans are dying to get back into it. With the map’s official release in the game, players are no longer required to rely on community servers or Workshop versions to experience the map. In this article, we will explain how you can use the legendary map.
Cobblestone has been a fan favorite ever since its release in CS:GO. Unlike traditional maps like Mirage and Dust2, Cobble offered a layered structure that kept the map balanced while being tactically demanding. Having witnessed historic moments from Counter-Strike esports, the map has been etched into the hearts of the fans.
Something we've cobbled together: https://t.co/bQbe8WQh0S
— CS2 (@CounterStrike) November 17, 2026
While the map is not a part of Active Duty at the time of writing, players can enjoy it in alternate game modes through the official matchmaking system.
How to play Cobblestone in CS2?
The official release has limited the map to certain game modes. To experience the map in CS2, follow the steps below:
Launch Counter-Strike 2 through Steam.
Navigate to the Play menu.
Select Competitive, Wingman, Casual, Deathmatch, or Retake.
Open the map selection menu.
Select Cobblestone and start matchmaking.
When will Cobblestone come to Active Duty?
Valve has not hinted at the map’s official return to the Active Duty map pool, but given the circumstances of its release, we can take an educated guess. Given that the map has been reintroduced weeks before the Major, Valve would likely wait for the current competitive season to conclude before making such a tectonic shift to the map pool.
If historical map changes are anything to go by, we might see the map return to the game as soon as the PGL Singapore Major concludes or by the end of December, after all the tier-1 tournaments for the season have wrapped up.
Cobble’s addition will be a highly welcome and refreshing change to a map pool that many believe has stagnated since the release of CS2. A new map comes with its own set of bugs and glitches, and whether Valve decides to bring it to Active Duty is a debate of its own. As of now, we can only enjoy the map in game modes other than Premier and hope it doesn’t go the route of Train.

You Can’t Replay Story Missions in GTA 6, Unlike GTA 5
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto VI does not include a mission replay option, so players cannot return to a completed story mission from the pause menu. The only way to play a mission again is to load a manual save made before it, and the game offers 15 manual save slots for that purpose.
The change breaks from GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, which both let players revisit any finished story mission at any time. For players chasing gold medals, trophies or a favourite heist, it means saves now have to be planned in advance.
GTA 6 has no mission replay menu
In GTA 5, players can open the pause menu, go to the Game tab and pick Replay Mission to restart any completed story mission. A replay does not overwrite the main save, so players can retry a mission for a better medal and return to free roam where they left off.
GTA 6 removes that option entirely. Once a story mission ends and the game autosaves, the mission is locked behind the player’s progress. The game’s 93 story missions, listed in our GTA 6 chapters and missions guide, can only be played once per save file unless players keep older saves.
How to go back to a GTA 6 mission with manual saves
GTA 6 gives players 15 manual save slots, the same number as GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2. Loading a manual save made before a mission is the only way to replay it. The game also keeps its own autosave, but that slot updates as the story moves forward, so it cannot be used to go back.
Players who want to replay key moments should create a manual save before each major mission, especially heists such as Sinfrontera National Bank and The Cartel Heist. A save at the start and end of each of the five chapters also keeps the full story available later. With only 15 slots, older saves will need to be overwritten as the campaign moves on.
Why GTA 6 handles missions differently
Rockstar has changed how the story is paced in GTA 6. The game adds gaps between some story missions, and Jason and Lucia sometimes need to earn money through activities such as robberies or car thefts before the next job unlocks. Story missions also allow more freedom, with players able to ignore suggested escape routes during police chases.
Rockstar has not explained why it left out the replay feature. It is not clear whether a replay option could arrive in a later update, and the studio has made no announcement about post launch changes to the save system.
What this means for GTA 6 trophies and gold medals
Missing a mission objective in GTA 6 cannot be fixed by replaying the mission later, unless an earlier manual save exists. Players going for a full completion run should save before each mission and check the GTA 6 trophies and achievements list before starting a new chapter. Our guide to how long GTA 6 takes to beat covers the length of the main story and a completionist run.
More launch day details are in our GTA 6 launch live blog. Rockstar lists the game’s platforms and editions on its official Grand Theft Auto VI page.

MSI unveils EdgeMesa N AI+ RTX Spark mini PC
items.content:
MSI has unveiled the EdgeMesa N AI+, an RTX Spark-equipped mini PC. The system combines NVIDIA Grace CPU cores with a Blackwell-based RTX GPU, and up to 128GB of unified memory in a compact 1.3-litre chassis.
Cooling comes courtesy of MSI's AI Pulse Cooling System, which combines a vapour chamber with dual turbo fans to sustain the system's 140W TDP. According to MSI, the cooling system is designed for continuous operation and 24/7 workloads, so there should be minimal downtime for any local AI agents.
The system is built around NVIDIA's RTX Spark N1X, which combines a Blackwell GPU featuring up to 6,144 CUDA cores with a 20-core Grace CPU. Like other RTX Spark systems, it can deliver up to 1 petaflop of FP4 AI performance, while up to 128GB of LPDDR5X unified memory allows users to run larger AI models locally rather than in the cloud.
MSI also includes 10GbE networking, WiFi 7 and Bluetooth 5.4, alongside four 20Gbps USB Type-C ports, HDMI 2.1 and support for up to four displays. Storage comes via a single M.2 NVMe slot, while NVIDIA's Personal AI Router (PAIR) technology allows compatible systems to be linked together in a local AI inference cluster.
The MSI EdgeMesa N AI+ will ship in two variants, one with 64GB of RAM at £4099, and another with 128GB of RAM at £6999.

Native Windows on Arm applications from Adobe, the NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction feature in Blender and local generation workflows in ComfyUI expand what creators and developers can do on RTX Spark — all on one Windows PC.
A Windows PC Built for Local AI
As workflows expand to include local AI models and agents, more work can continue beyond an active editing session — from generating assets to processing long renders or scheduled tasks.
RTX Spark compact desktops give developers, creators and AI enthusiasts a dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents. They bring together image and video generation, model fine-tuning, creative applications and development tools in one compact system.
Running supported models locally keeps locally processed code and files on the PC and avoids per-token cloud application programming interface (API) charges for those tasks.
RTX Spark compact desktops like the ASUS ProArt GR1X mini PC are built to run personal AI agents 24/7.
RTX Spark desktops are equipped with a 20-core NVIDIA Grace CPU, an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU with 6,144 CUDA cores and up to 128GB of unified memory, delivering up to 1 petaflop of AI performance. Ten-gigabit Ethernet connectivity enables fast transfers of large datasets, model files and creative assets between RTX Spark compact desktops and networked storage.
This advanced hardware unlocks incredible capabilities for creators, developers and AI enthusiasts, including:
Running massive 120-billion-parameter large language models locally
Rendering 90GB+ 3D scenes in real time
Smoothly editing 4:2:2 video in real time
The MSI EdgeMesa N AI+ Series RTX Spark compact desktop.
New compact desktops are available for purchase from ASUS, Dell and MSI, joining the RTX Spark family of laptops available today. Mini PCs from Acer, GIGABYTE and HP are coming soon, along with the Microsoft Surface RTX Spark Dev Box.
From Local Agents to AI Creation
Native CUDA support and Linux development tools through Windows Subsystem for Linux give developers a foundation for building and running local AI workflows. Developers can set up agents with Hermes Agent or NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints and fine-tune supported models using Unsloth.
RTX Spark can run creative agents that connect familiar applications and local AI tools, helping creators move from an idea to finished work with natural-language instructions.
NVIDIA Switchyard, now available in Hermes, automatically routes agent tasks between local and cloud models. Everyday tasks can run on device, while advanced reasoning draws on cloud models, helping manage cloud costs across creative workflows.
These capabilities come together in creative workflows that connect Photoshop and ComfyUI through Hermes Agent. Using natural-language instructions, creators can turn sketches into rendered images and animations, or animate an image entirely on device by isolating a subject and defining its motion.
NVIDIA brought these workflows to life at Adobe MAX, where attendees used natural-language instructions to turn sketches into rendered images and generate video for a shared digital Miami landscape.
The RTX Video Frame Generation and RTX Video HDR features, already available in ComfyUI, extend the pipeline: a generated clip can be expanded to 60 frames per second and converted to high dynamic range for color grading, all within a single ComfyUI workflow on RTX Spark.
Adobe Accelerates the Full Creative Stack for RTX Spark
NVIDIA and Adobe are expanding native Windows on Arm support and RTX acceleration across Adobe’s creative applications, helping video editors, photographers, designers and 3D artists work more efficiently on RTX Spark.
Adobe Premiere accelerates a range of AI-powered editing features through NVIDIA TensorRT-RTX, including Enhance Speech, Object Mask, Scene Edit Detection and Auto Reframe — so editors spend less time waiting and more time cutting.
GPU acceleration also extends to Film Impact transition and effects plug-ins. The update improves support for professional video formats, including Canon RAW, Red RAW, ARRI RAW, ARRICORE, ARRI HDE, H.264 and HEVC in MXF, ProRes RAW and long-GOP video. This lets editors realize more than 50% quicker turnaround on everyday H.264 video deliverables.
Adobe Photoshop adds TensorRT-RTX acceleration for the Remove Tool and ArmRTX Spark-native Camera Raw support, helping photographers remove unwanted objects faster and work with RAW images without relying on emulation. At Adobe MAX, Adobe previewed a next-generation image processing engine with extensive GPU acceleration, including interactive Gaussian blur and Light Leaks filters.
Adobe Substance 3D Painter 12.2 is now optimized for RTX Spark with native support on Arm for the first time in public beta. Artists in games, visual effects and visualization can run Substance Painter natively on RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops, with no compatibility layer required.
Adobe Illustrator and InDesign now offer native Windows on Arm versions optimized for RTX Spark. Adobe Illustrator delivers up to 30% higher performance than its emulated version, helping accelerate illustration, graphic design and page-layout workflows on RTX Spark.
Blender 5.3 Adds DLSS Ray Reconstruction to the Viewport
Blender 5.3 integrates DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction into the Cycles viewport, helping artists evaluate lighting and materials with near-final-quality ray-traced previews as they work.
The practical difference is immediate: instead of navigating a noisy, resolving preview, Ray Reconstruction delivers near-final-quality lighting, reflections and materials in the interactive viewport in real time.
DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction support requires Blender 5.3 and the latest NVIDIA Game Ready Driver or NVIDIA Studio Driver. Download the NVIDIA App to get automatic notifications when the latest drivers are available, optimize games and applications from a unified GPU control center, and discover the latest NVIDIA tools and software.
Windows Server 2028 Coming to DGX Station for Windows
Announced at Microsoft Ignite, Windows Server is evolving for organizations that need to run AI closer to their enterprise applications and data.
Microsoft is expanding hardware choice through support for the latest AI silicon, helping customers take advantage of accelerated inference and increasingly capable models in their own environments. NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows platform powered by the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip is expanding to include support for Windows Server 2028.
New accelerator platforms and the breadth of the Windows silicon ecosystem provide customers options at different capability levels and price points for advanced AI development, local inference, and agent workloads at scale.
Windows ML Updates Give Developers More Options
Also announced at Microsoft Ignite, developers can now bring any GGUF model from Hugging Face and run it within Windows ML using the llama.cpp backend.
The DxCGC backend, now available as an experimental release, is an integration for game developers that compiles and runs machine learning models through DirectX 12, allowing them to execute AI workloads alongside graphics.
Windows APIs let applications integrate platform-provided AI capabilities adding GPU support for AION Instruct and VSR.
Developers can also build high-performance AI models for Windows ML using the command line interface.
#ICYMI: The Latest NVIDIA Local AI Updates
llama.cpp v1.0.0 marks a major milestone for building local AI apps. The open source inference engine introduces API versioning updates, alongside expanded model support and CUDA optimizations for NVFP4 inference. Learn more.
Ricursive Intelligence introduced its first open model: Ripple-65B Preview. The full-stack AI lab builds self-improving systems by co-optimizing hardware, software and models. Ripple-65B Preview was trained on NVIDIA B300 GPUs, refined using NVIDIA Nemotron post-training datasets and runs locally on DGX Spark. Download the NVFP4 checkpoint from Hugging Face.
Runway’s Praxis-1 is a newly released 27-billion-parameter world action model that predicts video and actions together. Developers can run it locally on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, DGX Spark and DGX Station, and adapt it to their own robots, cameras and tasks with LoRA fine-tuning. Download the NVFP4 checkpoint from Hugging Face.
NVIDIA TensorRT Edge-LLM helps run AI models locally on DGX Spark with just a few commands. Read the technical blog, which walks through downloading Nemotron-3.5 Lightning, setting up optimized inference, testing prompts and serving the model through a local OpenAI-compatible API.
Subscribe to the NVIDIA Local AI newsletter. Follow NVIDIA RTX Spark on X, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook.

The Gentlemen Ransomware Group Claims Nvidia Attack, Sets Leak Timer Under 10 Days
items.content:
The Gentlemen ransomware group listed Nvidia as a victim on its dark web leak site on 18 November and threatened to publish data it claims to have taken from the chipmaker. A countdown timer on the listing gives Nvidia less than 10 days before the alleged leak goes live.
The group has not shared any sample files or a list of stolen data to support the claim. Nvidia has not confirmed a breach or responded publicly to the listing.
What The Gentlemen’s Nvidia listing shows
The post names Nvidia alongside its company revenue and its stock ticker, NVDA. A section for data details reads “DATA INFO – SOON”, which means the group has not yet said what it took or how much. The listing also includes a Tox messaging ID that the group offers for ransom negotiation.
Ransomware tracker Ransomware.live recorded the Nvidia listing on 18 November and logged the estimated attack date as the same day. When the timer was first spotted, it showed around 234 hours remaining.
Without samples, it is unclear whether the claim relates to Nvidia’s own systems, a supplier or partner, or older data. Ransomware gangs sometimes list large companies before any proof exists, in an effort to pressure them into talks. Security researchers treat such posts as unverified until data or a company statement appears.
Who is The Gentlemen ransomware group?
The Gentlemen surfaced in 2025 and operates as a ransomware as a service group, renting its tools to affiliates who carry out attacks. It has since become one of the most active gangs tracked by researchers, with hundreds of claimed victims on its leak site.
Security firm NCC Group said earlier this year that the group usually gains access through vulnerable internet facing services or stolen credentials. Once inside, its affiliates have been seen taking over privileged accounts, changing Group Policy settings and switching off antivirus tools across a network. The group encrypts Windows, Linux and VMware ESXi systems and steals data before encryption, so it can threaten a leak as well as a lockout.
In October, security firm CloudSEK identified a Russian speaking affiliate of the group using AI tooling to run commands during live intrusions. The Gentlemen has also listed several other high profile companies this month.
Nvidia faces the claim during a turbulent month
The listing comes during one of the most difficult periods in Nvidia’s recent history. The company’s board rejected Jensen Huang’s offer to return as CEO this month, weeks after his departure following reports of a third relationship with an Nvidia employee. The board has also created a national security committee as Washington increases scrutiny of chip exports.
Nvidia was the target of a confirmed cyberattack in February 2022, when the Lapsus$ extortion group stole employee credentials and internal data and later leaked part of it. The chip industry has seen other security incidents this year, including TSMC’s confirmed employee data leak through a cloud provider. The Gentlemen’s timer is due to run out in late November.
