JioBLAST’s VCT South Asia Qualifier Goes BO3, Then BO1, Then BO3 Again, and Admins Say Riot Approved It
items.content:
Day two of JioBLAST’s VCT 2027 Kickoff Open Qualifiers for South Asia has brought a new complaint, this time about how long matches last. Indian Valorant coach Abhishek “GodspeedxD” Bajaj said on 18 November that after a best-of-three round of 128 the day before, teams would play the next two rounds as best-of-ones before switching back to best-of-threes. He added that the admins had told teams they had Riot’s approval for running the bracket this way.
PSA: Kickoff South Asian OQs will feature a probable first-in-history bracket featuring a bo3 ro128 bracket and then subsequent rounds with bo1s before returning to bo3s.
Making teams play best-of-1s in the slot deciding qualifiers is a new low, and we havent yet truly started…
— GodspeedxD (@GodspeedxD) November 18, 2026
Abhishek “GodspeedxD” Bajaj’s post on X about the qualifier format, 18 November 2026.
Bajaj did not hold back in his criticism of the decision. “Making teams play best-of-1s in the slot deciding qualifiers is a new low, and we havent yet truly started the season,” he wrote in his post on X. He called it “probably the first time in the history of esports” that earlier rounds were best-of-threes while later ones were best-of-ones, and said it was “just the tip of the iceberg”.
Neither JioBLAST nor Riot had responded publicly by Wednesday afternoon. The organiser’s X account has not posted about the qualifier since its reminder on 16 November, and TalkEsport has not seen the revised bracket published on any official channel. Without a published bracket, teams are relying on Discord updates and posts like Bajaj’s to follow the changes.
What the BO1 switch means for South Asian teams
The difference between the two formats is bigger than it sounds. In a best-of-three, a team has to win two maps, so one bad veto, one hot opponent or one technical problem rarely ends its run. In a best-of-one, a single map decides the tie, which is why rounds that decide qualification are usually played as best-of-threes or longer.
The format also seems to have moved away from the one JioBLAST announced. As our guide to the South Asia Open Qualifiers explained, the 3 November announcement described a Swiss stage from 17 to 20 November, followed by a double-elimination playoff for the top eight. Bajaj and other community voices are describing numbered knockout rounds instead, including a round of 128.
The first day of the qualifier had already shown the cracks. As we reported, a Maldivian player said teams were told on Discord, an hour before their matches, that a new schedule and bracket had been released, and that his team now faced a best-of-three. Bajaj’s account fits that timeline, with best-of-three matches in the round of 128 on day one.
Players caught between the qualifier and other events
Scheduling is causing problems for players who compete in more than one event. Rishi “RvK” Vijayakumar, who is part of GodLike’s reported return roster, asked his followers to “find me another rvk” on Wednesday. He explained on X that he had two best-of-threes at 8pm, one against Kryon in a separate competition and one in the Open Qualifier.
Clashes like that are harder to manage when the format keeps changing. Teams plan practice and veto preparation around the schedule they are given, and South Asian teams are already working across several countries and time zones. A late switch between best-of-one and best-of-three changes how many maps a team must prepare and how long its players need to be available.
Bajaj, who describes himself on X as a Valorant coach currently looking for a team, said he was holding back “other details out of respect”. He warned that the way the qualifier was being run would “set the region back so much further”. His post had been viewed a few hundred times within its first hour, but it echoed complaints that spread widely on day one.
Why the South Asia qualifier matters for VCT 2027
The stakes are high for a region with few routes into the Pacific circuit. Under Riot’s VCT 2027 system, the two South Asian qualifiers join a Kickoff Last Chance Qualifier with Oceania’s playoff winner and Southeast Asia’s runner-up. The winner of that event takes the final Open place at VCT Pacific Kickoff in Bangkok.
South Asia’s tournament organisation has drawn complaints before, including the ARISE Esports allegations about a banned player in VCSA 2026 under the previous organiser. This is JioBLAST’s first VCT event, and the organiser took over the region’s qualifiers only this month. Riot’s VALORANT Esports India and South Asia account has not addressed the format change on X.
The Open Qualifier stage was scheduled to run until 20 November, with the double-elimination playoffs due to begin on 23 November. Two teams will come out of those playoffs and represent South Asia at Kickoff APAC. The playoffs are set to be broadcast on the JioBLAST and VALORANT YouTube channels and on JioTV.
The post JioBLAST’s VCT South Asia Qualifier Goes BO3, Then BO1, Then BO3 Again, and Admins Say Riot Approved It appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: We Got a GTA 6 Game of the Year Nominee Before GTA 6
items.content:
For years, “we got X before GTA 6” was the internet’s favourite way of saying something would take forever. On 17 November, The Game Awards delivered the final version of the joke. Grand Theft Auto VI was named one of six Game of the Year nominees and picked up eight nominations in total, two days before the game goes on sale.
The reaction on social media was instant and loud. Under The Game Awards’ own post on X asking fans for the most surprising nomination, the top replies pointed at the game that “isn’t even playable yet”, and some called the show rigged. Our view is simpler: GTA VI broke no rule to get here, but the rules now produce a result that looks bad, and The Game Awards should fix that before next year.
Why GTA 6 is eligible for The Game Awards before release
The eligibility rule is a sales date, not a nominations date. According to The Game Awards’ FAQ, as quoted by Make Tech Easier, games had to be “commercially available to customers on or before Friday, November 20, 2026”, with a cut-off of 9pm Pacific time. GTA VI launches on 19 November on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, which puts it inside the window with a day to spare.
That release date was not chosen to suit the show either. As our GTA 6 guide sets out, Rockstar first targeted 2025, then moved the game to 26 May 2026 and finally to 19 November. Had the last delay pushed it a few days further, GTA VI would have been a 2027 contender instead.
Nominated first, released secondKey dates for GTA VI and The Game Awards 202617 NovNominations announcedGTA VI gets eight, including Game of the Year18 NovCritic reviews reportedly dueDate reported by Insider Gaming, not confirmed by Rockstar19 NovGTA VI launchesPlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S20 NovEligibility cut-offGames must be on sale by 9pm PT9 DecFan voting closesFans make up 10% of the result10 DecThe Game Awards ceremonyPeacock Theater, Los Angeles2daysSources: The Game Awards, Rockstar Games, Insider Gaming. Graphic: TalkEsport
The selection process is also harder to rig than the replies suggest. A jury of media and creator outlets, which our full list of The Game Awards 2026 nominees put at more than 160, submits unranked ballots, and the most-named games become nominees. The jury then decides 90% of each result, with the fan vote worth 10%, and the FAQ states that host Geoff Keighley does not vote.
Why the GTA 6 nomination still looks biased
The problem is timing, and it is hard to explain away. The shortlist went out on 17 November, while critic reviews are reportedly due on 18 November, a date Insider Gaming says it verified but Rockstar has not confirmed. That means the public saw GTA VI named a Game of the Year nominee before it could read a single published review.
Many of the jurors may well have played it already. Rockstar reportedly began sending review code to outlets at the end of October, which would have given voting outlets time to form a view before the jury’s ballots were due. The Game Awards does not say which jurors had access, however, so fans are being asked to trust a process they cannot see.
The fan vote has the same issue in reverse. Voting is already open on The Game Awards website, so millions of people can back GTA VI before the game is in their hands. Rockstar’s marketing has reached as far as a Weather Channel forecast for Leonida, and that hype runs both ways. A 6.5 user score from five ratings briefly appeared on GTA VI’s Metacritic page on 16 November, before anyone could have played it, and then vanished.
We also looked at how close previous Game of the Year nominees came to the wire. Among recent late launches, God of War Ragnarök arrived five days before its nomination in 2022, Death Stranding 11 days before in 2019 and Alan Wake 2 17 days before in 2023. TalkEsport could not find an earlier Game of the Year nominee that was still unreleased when the shortlist was announced.
The latest Game of the Year launchesDays between a nominee’s launch and the nominations announcementNominations daylaunched beforelaunched afterAlan Wake 2202317 daysDeath Stranding201911 daysGod of War Ragnarök20225 daysGrand Theft Auto VI20262 daysSources: The Game Awards, publisher release dates. Graphic: TalkEsport
The cost of that falls on other games. Crimson Desert fans say their game was ignored, although it is in fact nominated for Best Community Support. The Blood of Dawnwalker made Best Narrative and Best Role Playing Game but missed the top six. When a game wins eight slots on reputation and pre-release access, the games people have already finished are the ones squeezed out.
What The Game Awards should change before 2027
The fix is mostly a matter of the calendar. The Game Awards’ cut-off has recently landed after nominations day, with 18 November against 14 November in 2022, 17 November against 13 November in 2023 and 20 November against 17 November this year. In 2019, by contrast, the cut-off of 15 November came four days before the nominations were announced on 19 November.
Going back to that order would mean every nominee is on sale when it is named. The show could also ask jurors to confirm that they played each game they nominate, and open fan voting for a title only once it has launched. None of these changes would stop GTA VI from winning, but each would make a win easier to defend.
Pushing GTA VI into 2027 would have been the worse option, because a game released in November should compete with the games of its own year. Rockstar’s title was always going to dominate this season’s conversation, and the joke landed because it was true. The awards can live with the meme, but they should not have to defend the calendar again.
GTA VI’s eight nominations are the most of any game this year, two more than CONTROL Resonant and Resident Evil Requiem. Fans have until 9 December to vote, and the winners will be revealed on 10 December at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. In India, the show runs in the early hours of 11 December, as our The Game Awards 2026 date and time guide explains.
The post We Got a GTA 6 Game of the Year Nominee Before GTA 6 appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: South Korea Moves Closer to a Tax Credit for Game Development After Minister’s Pledge
items.content:
South Korea’s culture minister has promised to keep pushing the rest of the government for a tax break on game production costs. Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism Choi Hwi-young made the case at the 2026 Korea Game Awards in Busan on 18 November. He said his ministry would consult and persuade “relevant ministries” to introduce a tax credit for game content production. Korean media reported that it was his first appearance at the awards since 2023.
The pledge matters because games are still left out of the production tax credit that South Korea already gives film, broadcast and webtoon content. Choi has made similar promises before, and the finance ministry has so far left games out of its tax plans. This time, though, the chair of the National Assembly committee that handles tax law was on the same stage.
What Choi Hwi-young promised at the Korea Game Awards
The ceremony was hosted by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and run by the Korea Game Industry Association at BEXCO, the day before G-Star opens at the same venue. In his congratulatory address, Choi called games a representative Korean industry “where culture and technology converge” and a core driver of the country’s content exports. He said the government would support the industry so it can lead what he called the “K-culture 400 trillion won era”.
He then listed the support that the ministry has already planned. Help for indie game planning and production will expand significantly, and a new programme for large-scale games aimed at global markets will start next year. The game internship scheme for young people will grow to 500 places, according to Korean media reports of the speech.
Choi also pointed to new funds aimed at games and other content. A 120 billion won intellectual property fund created this year is investing mainly in games. Next year, the government plans a 1.5 trillion won content fund alongside 600 billion won in loans for the content sector. Those plans build on the 2027 budget proposals we covered when the culture ministry outlined its gaming support in October.
Two senior lawmakers backed him up from the same stage. Lee Jae-jeong, the Democratic Party chair of the National Assembly’s culture committee, promised legislative support for the industry. Cho Seung-rae, the Democratic Party chair of the Finance, Economy and Planning Committee, said the game content tax credit was already on his committee’s agenda and pledged active support.
Why games are left out of South Korea’s content tax credit
South Korea’s video content production tax credit sits in the Restriction of Special Taxation Act. According to Korean outlet Inven, it gives small and medium-sized companies a basic credit of 15%, with 10% for mid-sized and large companies. An extra credit at the same rate applies when at least 80% of production costs are spent in Korea. Webtoons receive the same basic rate, but games have no equivalent provision.
The finance ministry has been the main obstacle. Its tax reform plan of 3 August did not include a game production credit, and instead added a step-down rate of 12.5% for three years for video and webtoon companies that outgrow small-business status. The ministry has been cautious because games already receive research and development tax credits, and it worries about the two overlapping.
Choi’s own position on the credit has also moved over the past year. In August 2025 he told the National Assembly’s culture committee that he would try to include the credit in the government’s policy agenda. At an advisory meeting on 20 October this year, however, he said it seemed important to build public debate and a favourable social mood first, which Korean games media read as a step back.
A bill to change the law is already in the National Assembly. People Power Party lawmakers Jung Yeon-wook and Park Sung-hoon have sponsored an amendment to the Restriction of Special Taxation Act that would add game production. With Cho’s committee now saying the issue is on its table, the proposal has a clearer route through the National Assembly than it did a month ago.
A tax push as Korea’s biggest publishers skip G-Star
The timing of the pledge says a lot about the industry’s mood. G-Star 2026 runs at BEXCO from 19 to 22 November, but Korean media report that Nexon, Netmarble, NCSoft, Krafton and Kakao Games are not exhibiting in its consumer hall. Organisers have said the industry’s move from mobile to longer PC and console projects means studios have fewer new titles ready to show each year.
Production costs are part of that story, and the Korea Game Awards shortlist showed both sides of it. Pearl Abyss’ Crimson Desert, which Business Post calls the first AAA open-world game from a Korean developer, passed 6 million copies 83 days after its March launch. It and NCSoft’s AION 2, an online role-playing game whose latest update arrived earlier this month, were the favourites for the presidential Grand Prize, due to be named at the end of the ceremony.
Crimson Desert’s international profile has grown well beyond Korea too. It picked up a nomination for Best Community Support at The Game Awards 2026. Korean publishers have also been adding policy expertise, as when KRAFTON hired a former finance ministry official as an adviser this month.
Choi did not give a timeline for the tax credit or say which ministries he would approach first. Any change would need to pass the National Assembly as an amendment to the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, the same law that already covers film, broadcast and webtoon production. Until then, Korean game studios will keep relying on research and development credits rather than the production credit their film and webtoon peers receive.
The post South Korea Moves Closer to a Tax Credit for Game Development After Minister’s Pledge appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: GTA 6’s Jason Missed Out on a Game Awards Nomination, and Rockstar Still Hasn’t Said Who Plays Him
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto VI picked up eight nominations at The Game Awards 2026, but only one of its two leads made the shortlist. Manni L. Perez was named among the five Best Performance nominees on 17 November, which fans took as confirmation that she plays Lucia Caminos. The actor behind Jason Duval was not nominated, and Rockstar has still not said who he is.
That has left GTA fans in an odd position two days before launch, with two playable leads who, as our GTA 6 guide explains, share the story as a criminal couple. The awards have answered one of the series’ longest-running casting questions while making the other look like a snub. It has also started an argument over whether Jason simply made less of an impression in the footage Rockstar has shown so far.
How The Game Awards confirmed GTA 6’s Lucia actor
Rockstar has never published a cast list for GTA VI, and its official character pages do not name the performers. The Game Awards’ list names only the performer and the game, not the role, so Perez’s nomination for Grand Theft Auto VI was as close to an announcement as fans have had. She had been linked to Lucia for years, and IBTimes UK noted that the specific casting still rests on reporting rather than a Rockstar statement.
Perez trained at NYU’s Tisch School of the Arts and has television credits including Chicago P.D., The Blacklist and Jessica Jones. In 2020, she won an Imagen Award for her role as Esperanza Morales in Law & Order: Special Victims Unit. Fans greeted the news by sharing clips of Lucia’s lines from the trailers, and one clip posted on X had passed 470,000 views by Wednesday.
She now faces Angela Sant’Albano for Resident Evil Requiem, Liam McIntyre for Marvel’s Wolverine, Patrick Gibson for 007 First Light and Rahul Kohli for Saros. The full shortlist, alongside GTA VI’s other seven nominations, is in our list of The Game Awards 2026 nominees. Three of the five performances come from Game of the Year nominees, with Resident Evil Requiem and 007 First Light joining GTA VI.
Why Jason’s actor missed out on Best Performance
Some fans expected both leads to be named together. The YouTube channel GameRoll wrote on X before the announcement that if either actor received a nomination, they would “HAVE to be named”, and it hoped both would be revealed. Fan speculation has long linked Dylan Rourke to Jason, but neither Rockstar nor Rourke has confirmed it.
The rules do not stop two actors from the same game being nominated. According to The Game Awards’ FAQ, each outlet on the jury submits one unranked ballot, and the performances named most often become the nominees. Last year, three Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 performers made Best Performance, with Jennifer English winning as Maelle ahead of Charlie Cox and Ben Starr.
The Last of Us Part II did the same in 2020, when Laura Bailey won for Abby and Ashley Johnson was nominated for Ellie. Jason’s absence reflects how this year’s jurors voted, rather than any limit on a single game. Those ballots were cast before GTA VI’s critic reviews, which are reportedly due on 18 November, so most jurors were judging the trailers and whatever pre-release access they had.
That footage has leaned towards Lucia from the start. Rockstar’s first trailer in December 2023 opened on her in a prison interview, before Jason appeared alongside her. Not everyone sees the snub as a verdict on Jason, however, and the fan site iGrandTheftAuto.com said the omission “doesn’t take anything away from what we’ve seen of his character so far”.
Rockstar’s history with Best Performance at The Game Awards
Rockstar’s last big release went through something similar. In 2018, Roger Clark won Best Performance for Arthur Morgan in Red Dead Redemption 2, but he was the game’s only nominee in the category. The rest of its large cast, including the actors behind Dutch van der Linde and John Marston, missed out on the shortlist.
Clark’s win showed that one standout lead can carry a Rockstar game through this category. Perez now has the same chance, and the result will come after millions of players have heard both protagonists for themselves. GTA VI launches on 19 November, and Indian players can start at midnight, as our GTA 6 release time guide explains.
Fan voting on The Game Awards website counts for 10% of each result and closes on 9 December. GTA VI is also up for Game of the Year, Best Narrative and Best Score and Music. The winners will be announced on 10 December at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, which falls in the early hours of 11 December in India.
The post GTA 6’s Jason Missed Out on a Game Awards Nomination, and Rockstar Still Hasn’t Said Who Plays Him appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Is CarryMinati Joining GodLike Esports? Here’s What We Know
items.content:
GodLike Esports has been in the spotlight recently after co-owner Chetan “Kronten” Chandgude spoke publicly about why Jonathan left the organization. Now, the organization has drawn attention for a completely different reason. A rumour suggesting that renowned YouTuber CarryMinati could join GodLike Esports has been circulating online since 17th Nov. Here’s everything that has emerged so far.
Why Are Fans Linking CarryMinati With GodLike Esports?
The speculation began with the same message that Kronten sent on his Instagram broadcast which started the unveiling of the GodLike vs JONATHAN controversy. In the end of the message, Kronten mentioned that there’s “a BIG announcement coming soon.”
Following this, Amar Chandgude, GodLike Esports’ co-owner, posted a picture of Kronten and Kammaljeet, the general manager of the organization, with a bouquet, accompanied by the message, “Announcement soon.”
Neither of these teasers bring CarryMinati into the picture. What sparked the rumour was a user posting on X that CarryMinati has started following Kronten on Instagram.
Following this, Kammaljeet posted an old group picture, which included himself, CarryMinati, and two other individuals. This picture, given the timing, further fueled the speculation.
AnkiiiBOT Responds to CarryMinati Joining GodLike Esports Rumours
As the speculations mounted, fans were impatient to find out whether CarryMinati was indeed the mystery creator joining GodLike Esport. To verify the rumour, fans flooded the livestream chat of Ankit “AnkiiiBOT” Pandey, GodLike Esports’ content creator. Addressing these messages, AnkiiiBOT mentioned that he was unaware of the rumour and could not verify or deny it. “I have no idea about this, guys. I don’t know anything about it. The person I have an idea about is someone else.”
Subsequently, AnkiiiBOT shed some light on who the mystery creator is. He stated that the creator who is joining GodLike Esports is not someone from an esports background or does not livestreams, but creates content around vlogging.
However, he refrained from revealing the name of the creator. “I can’t reveal the name, guys. I can’t give you any hints… You guys tell me. If this is such a huge announcement, it wouldn’t make any sense for me to drop hints about it.”
Before moving on from the topic, AnkiiiBOT clarified that this isn’t some forced hype. “It’s actually going to be a very crazy announcement. That’s all I’m saying. Let’s wait and see what the announcement turns out to be.”
Although the rumours suggest that CarryMinati could be the mystery creator joining GodLike Esports, AnkiiiBOT’s comments seem to suggest otherwise. With the creator reportedly belonging to a vlogging background, it will be interesting to be seen whether CarryMinati is indeed the one behind the upcoming announcement.

items.title: Nvidia Board Rejects Jensen Huang’s Offer to Return as CEO, but Some Directors Reportedly Still Want Him Back
items.content:
Jensen Huang offered to come back as Nvidia’s chief executive on 17 November, and the company’s board turned him down within hours. In a statement on X, the co-founder admitted “serious mistakes” in his personal life and said he would be “honored” to return if the board wanted him. That afternoon, on Nvidia’s third-quarter earnings call, board chair Harvey Jones said the board “unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO”, according to NPR.
Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.
I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an…
— Jensen Huang (@JensenHuang) November 17, 2026
Jensen Huang’s statement on X, posted on 17 November 2026.
The rejection landed on the same night Nvidia posted a record quarter. Revenue for the three months to 25 October reached $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier, and the company forecast $130 billion for the current quarter. Nvidia shares closed 0.48% lower at $155.39 on Tuesday but rose nearly 5% in after-hours trading, according to The National.
What Jensen Huang said in his statement
Huang posted his statement at 9:48 pm Indian time on 17 November, which was Tuesday morning in the US. “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life,” he wrote. He added that he had “created problems for the Board” that he deeply regretted, and said he was committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.
Most of the statement, however, was an offer. Huang said he had seen “an outpouring of calls” from employees, investors, business partners and customers asking him to return. If the board decided his return was in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company and America, he wrote that he “would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO”. By Wednesday morning in India, the post had passed 43 million views on X.
Those calls had been building all week, from inside and outside the company. A “Stand With Jensen” petition passed 175,000 signatures, and Altimeter Capital’s Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management’s Gavin Baker publicly asked the board to keep his possible return open. The Financial Times also reported that Huang was considering a comeback, with an ally reportedly assembling a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby the board.
How Nvidia’s board closed the door on Huang’s return
Washington, however, had been pulling the board the other way. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had said Nvidia needed “a dramatic shakeup” and should look outside the company for its next chief executive, as we reported when he demanded answers from the board within 10 days. On the call, Jones called the change “an unexpected transition”, but he gave Huang’s supporters no opening at all.
Jones also made clear that Colette Kress keeps the job for now. “We have every confidence in Colette’s leadership, integrity and ability to deliver as interim CEO,” he said, according to Yahoo Finance. He confirmed that the board has hired the executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent chief executive, but said Nvidia would not take questions about the nature of Huang’s resignation or the investigation.
Kress said Nvidia wants its next chief executive in place “as quickly as possible, but we won’t expedite the CEO before finding exactly the right person”, according to The National. The board had already set up a national security and export control committee earlier that day. Huang resigned on 12 November as president, chief executive and director, ending 33 years in charge of the company he co-founded.
The board may not be as settled as Jones suggested, however. Semafor reported late on Tuesday, US time, citing people familiar with the matter, that a minority of directors are still pushing for Huang’s return while others have begun narrowing the search for a successor. According to the report, Huang met several tech executives and discussed a comeback with at least one board member before the results and his statement were released. Neither Nvidia nor Huang’s representatives commented on the report, and TalkEsport has not independently confirmed it.
His legal and political problems are not over either. NPR reported that Huang will appear behind closed doors before House committees on 1 December, with general counsel Tim Teter following on 2 December. The board’s own investigation has no public end date.
The record quarter Huang left behind
The quarter itself ran entirely under Huang, and the results beat Wall Street’s forecasts comfortably. Revenue of $115.8 billion compared with an LSEG consensus of $109.15 billion, according to The National. Data Center revenue came in at $107.6 billion, up 110% from a year earlier, against expectations of $101.85 billion, while GAAP net income reached $65.3 billion.
Kress, who is also Nvidia’s chief financial officer, said in the release that “our momentum is real” and that Vera Rubin “is off to an explosive start”. Nvidia said its Vera Rubin NVL72 racks had shipped in the fastest product ramp in its history, with systems running at CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Non-GAAP earnings of $2.68 per share also beat the $2.47 that analysts expected, according to The National.
The outlook for the current quarter was stronger still. Nvidia guided for revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, in a fourth quarter that includes an extra week, compared with forecasts of $125.5 billion. It said it is not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China, which has been at the centre of the export questions surrounding Megaspeed and Alice Huang.
Shareholders also have a large buyback behind them. The board approved a $150 billion increase to Nvidia’s share repurchase programme in September, and the company returned $28.1 billion to shareholders during the quarter, leaving about $227.3 billion still available. Gamers got a mention too, with the release listing DLSS 5 in NBA 2K27 and Hogwarts Legacy among the quarter’s highlights.
For the people who wanted Huang back, the numbers cut both ways. They show the company he built is still growing at a pace few others can match, and they show the board believes it can keep that going without him. The next quarterly dividend of $0.25 per share is due on 23 December, to shareholders on record on 2 December.
The post Nvidia Board Rejects Jensen Huang’s Offer to Return as CEO, but Some Directors Reportedly Still Want Him Back appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Cobblestone Is Back in CS2 With a Winter Makeover, and Valve Changes How Singapore Major Stickers Are Sold
items.content:
Cobblestone is back in Counter-Strike 2, and it has arrived in the snow. Valve’s latest update, released on 17 November in the US and early on 18 November in India, adds a winter version of the classic map to official Casual, Competitive, Wingman, Retakes and Deathmatch matchmaking. It landed hours after Valve’s “‘Tis the season” teaser, which we covered in our first look at winter Cobblestone, and the same update opened the PGL Major Singapore 2026 shop and added eight Monstercat music kits.
Something we've cobbled together: https://t.co/bQbe8WQh0S
— CS2 (@CounterStrike) November 17, 2026
Counter-Strike’s post announcing the update on X.
In its blog post announcing the update, Valve said veterans “will feel at home in familiar locations like drop, chicken coop, and stables”. It added that the map “has undergone changes and features new pathways and locations for players to master”, before warning players to “watch your crunchy footsteps as you trudge through the snow to the bombsites”. The post ended with a simple instruction for players: “Now put on a jacket and get out there.”
What has changed on winter Cobblestone
Cobblestone sits in Competitive and Wingman, and in its own map group in Casual, Deathmatch and Retakes. It has not been added to Premier, and the update makes no change to the Active Duty pool, so the map will not be played at the Singapore Major. To make room, Valve’s patch notes also removed Boulder, Fachwerk and Shelter from the official matchmaking pool.
The snow is more than a texture swap. According to the notes, fire effects now get custom processing on ground materials, so they can harden metal surfaces and melt snow. The notes do not mention the frost effect that dataminers found in last week’s update files, which made players, weapons and even chickens freeze when they stayed outside.
Cobblestone has not been an official Counter-Strike map since a March 2019 CS:GO update removed it, and Valve’s teaser alone had passed 5.8 million views on X by Wednesday. The map also gave the game its most famous skin, because the AWP Dragon Lore came from the Cobblestone Collection. For many older fans, the update is as much about those memories as it is about the new layout.
Former professionals noticed the news straight away on social media. Kenny “kennyS” Schrub wrote on X that he “might unretire” because the “best map in the game” was coming back, in a post that had passed 760,000 views by Wednesday. According to career figures shared by a Counter-Strike news account on X, the French AWPer played 158 maps of Cobblestone with a 1.15 rating.
How Valve changed Singapore Major stickers
The update also opened the Major Shop for the PGL Major Singapore 2026, with Viewer Passes and Team and Player Autograph stickers now on sale. Valve repeated that “50% of the proceeds go to the players, teams and tournament organizer”, with revenue shared based on a team’s initial seed and final placement. The split is the same one that came under fire in our report on what Major sticker money now means for legacy organisations.
Autograph stickers in the Singapore Major Shop now come in Paper, Foil, Holo and Gold at fixed prices. Image: Valve
What Valve has changed is how fans buy the items. “We’ve heard your feedback and made some adjustments,” it wrote, explaining that Team and Player Autograph stickers in Paper, Foil, Holo and Gold finishes now have a fixed price and can be bought directly. Souvenirs can also be crafted for a fixed price, depending on the rarity of the weapon a player chooses.
A Singapore 2026 Viewer Pass gives an immediate Bronze Singapore Challenge Coin, Steam.tv chat flair and unlimited team graffiti for the event. Players upgrade the coin through the Pick’Em Challenge, and every upgrade earns 300 tokens to spend on stickers or souvenirs. The Major itself starts on 24 November, and our PGL Major Singapore guide has the full schedule.
The Singapore 2026 Viewer Pass and Challenge Coin. Image: Valve
The eight Monstercat music kits in the CS2 update
The final part of the update is musical. Valve and Monstercat, the Canadian independent label, released eight kits featuring ALLEYCVT and Level Up, Arcando and Pirapus, DJ Diesel and Hairitage, FOOL, Noisestorm, Pegboard Nerds, Tristam and Braken, and Vicetone with Cozi Zuehlsdorff. DJ Diesel is the music alias of basketball great Shaquille O’Neal, which makes him one of the more unexpected names to appear on a Counter-Strike music kit.
The eight Monstercat music kits added to CS2. Image: Valve
Valve described the set as ranging from “a classic Monstercat release from Tristam & Braken” to “an April Fool’s joke gone viral from Noisestorm”. That second line points to Crab Rave, the 2018 track whose artwork appears on Noisestorm’s kit. The update also adds an MVP Anthem preview button when inspecting music kits in the in-game store, so players can hear each kit before they buy it.
Cobblestone is live now in Competitive and Wingman, while the Singapore stickers, souvenirs and Viewer Passes are on sale in the in-game Major Shop. Monstercat has also confirmed the kits are in the CS2 store now. Results and brackets for the tournament will be on the TalkEsport wiki once play begins on 24 November.
The post Cobblestone Is Back in CS2 With a Winter Makeover, and Valve Changes How Singapore Major Stickers Are Sold appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: No Indian Winners at Esports Awards 2026 as S8UL’s Four-Year Reign Ends and Thug, Snax Miss Out
items.content:
India left the 2026 Esports Awards without a single trophy. At the ceremony at the Adrienne Arsht Center in Miami on 17 November, French organisation Gentle Mates won Esports Content Group of the Year, ending S8UL Esports’ run of four straight wins in the category. S8UL co-founder Animesh “Thug” Agarwal lost Esports Personality of the Year to Marc “Caedrel” Lamont, while Raj “Snax Gaming” Varma lost Streamer of the Year to iShowSpeed.
It is a sharp turn from last year, when India won twice in one night. S8UL took its fourth straight Content Group of the Year in 2025, and Thug became the first Indian to win Personality of the Year, beating Caedrel among others. This year’s ceremony handed out awards across 23 categories, according to the official winners list.
How S8UL’s Content Group of the Year streak ended
S8UL had owned this category since 2022, and it went into Miami as the four-time defending champion. The field was crowded, though, with 12 finalists including 100 Thieves, G2 Esports, OpTic Gaming, T1, Team Vitality and a second Indian organisation, GodLike Esports. Karmine Corp, NRG, Team Spirit and Rocket Baguette completed the shortlist, as our full list of Esports Awards 2026 nominees showed.
Gentle Mates, the French organisation co-founded by content creators Gotaga, Squeezie and Brawks, took the award. The club was also a finalist for Esports Team of the Year with its Rocket League roster and for Esports Organisation of the Year, which went to Team Vitality. That gave French clubs both of the night’s awards for organisations.
The way the category is judged matters here. According to the Esports Awards’ FAQ, most awards combine a public vote worth 25 per cent with an expert panel vote worth 75 per cent. Content Group of the Year is one of five exceptions decided entirely by the community, so S8UL’s streak ended on fan votes alone.
Why Thug and Snax lost in fan-voted categories
Personality of the Year and Streamer of the Year are on that same fan-voted list, along with Content Creator of the Year, so S8UL, GodLike, Thug and Snax all lost in categories decided entirely by the public. S8UL fan accounts on X had urged followers to back S8UL, Thug and Snax before voting closed on 10 November, during a final Turbo Week in which every vote counted double.
That support was not enough against Caedrel, the British League of Legends streamer and caster whom Thug beat a year ago. Caedrel was a finalist in three categories this year, Personality, Streamer and Content Creator, and Personality was the one he won. Content Creator of the Year went to Jynxzi, who was also on the Personality and Streamer shortlists.
Snax faced an even tougher field in Streamer of the Year, alongside names such as Kai Cenat, CaseOh, Jynxzi and Caedrel. The Hyderabad streamer has had a strong few weeks at home, recently becoming the most watched BGMI streamer over 30 days. The problem was that iShowSpeed had won a third straight Streamer of the Year at The Streamer Awards only days earlier.
Snax still had a moment on the Miami stage during the ceremony. Photos shared by Indian esports community accounts on X show him presenting Esports Mobile Game of the Year alongside RdJavi, with the award going to Mobile Legends: Bang Bang. Snax streams BGMI on his YouTube channel, and the Miami trip put him in front of a global industry audience.
India’s other near misses at the 2026 Esports Awards
The Mobile Game of the Year result was a miss for India’s biggest esports titles as well. Mobile Legends: Bang Bang beat Free Fire and PUBG Mobile, the global versions of the two games that drive most of India’s mobile esports scene. BGMI, the India-only version of PUBG Mobile, was not on the shortlist.
There was also an Indian link in the business categories. The phone brand iQOO, a familiar sponsor in Indian mobile esports, was a finalist for Esports Commercial Partner of the Year, but the award went to Razer. Meanwhile, GodLike Esports missed out alongside S8UL in the Content Group category, so neither Indian organisation took a trophy home.
Elsewhere, South Asia’s best chance came in Controller Player of the Year, where Pakistan’s Tekken stars Arslan Ash and Muhammad Zubair were both finalists, and Zubair was also up for Breakthrough Player. Neither won, with Brandon “Dashy” Otell taking Controller Player of the Year and Jaime “Craime” Bustos named Breakthrough Player of the Year. Caedrel, who also streams regularly on Twitch, now joins a list of Personality winners that included Thug only a year ago.
The night’s other headline awards went to Counter-Strike 2 as Esports Game of the Year, Team Vitality as Organisation of the Year and Mathieu “ZywOo” Herbaut as PC Player of the Year. Faker won the EWC Player’s Choice Award, and Gabriel “FalleN” Toledo was named in the Lifetime Achievement class of 2026. He was joined in that class by Damon “Karma” Barlow and Juan “Hungrybox” DeBiedma, among others.

items.title: 66 Years Later, William Shatner's Forgotten 'Twilight Zone' Is Still a Haunting Masterpiece
items.content: “Nightmare at 20,000 Feet” is one of the all-time great episodes of The Twilight Zone. Starring William Shatner, the story is about a man who is taking his first flight after having had a nervous breakdown. During the flight, he looks out the window and sees a creature, called a gremlin, on the wing that taunts him and tears apart pieces of the plane. No one can see the gremlin but him, and even his own wife attributes it to his fragile mental state. The story is a brilliant commentary on paranoia and Shatner was captivating in the role. It was so good that it sometimes overshadows Shatner’s other great episode of The Twilight Zone, which premiered 66 years ago today.

items.title: Guide: GTA 6 Release Times: When Can You Start Playing?
How to Get Ready for November 19
items.content:
November 19, 2026, has long been circled on your calendar. Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your XBOX console. We can hardly believe it’s almost here, either. Once midnight strikes, you want to be locked in the action, so to help you prepare, we created a checklist to ensure distractions are put to bed so you can settle in for a season of gaming like nothing you’ve ever experienced before.
Make Some Hard (Drive) Choices
2026 has been full of some absolute bangers: Gears of War E-Day, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Forza Horizon 6, Halo: Campaign Evolved, Minecraft Dungeons II, Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred, Control Resonant, Mixtape, Pragmata, The Blood of Dawnwalker, Star Wars: Galactic Racer, 007 First Light, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve… seriously, all these games came out this year. That also means you might have a hard drive that is nearing capacity. And you will be faced with some hard choices to free up approximately 212GB of space on your XBOX Series X|S before November 19.
You could always upgrade the capacity of your console to keep all your games at the ready, using the storage expansion slot on the back of the console. Otherwise, you’ll have a hard choice to make which we do not envy. But know that you’re in good company – we had to find a way to make room too.
Connect to the Cloud
XBOX Cloud Gaming means that you don’t need to own an XBOX Series X|S console to experience the latest games (or use up that hard drive space) – you can stream directly from the cloud to your XBOX One console. Game Pass subscribers receive an allotment of hours per month as part of their plans, but you can also purchase blocks of time. Certain upcoming major releases have been confirmed as cloud-ready on day one, so even if you don’t own a current gen console, your latest obsession isn’t out of reach.
Ready Your Console
You never want to settle in for a long gaming session only to immediately get hit with an update download. If you haven’t used your XBOX Series X|S or XBOX One in a minute, be sure to power up and connect to the internet beforehand and make sure you’re all set with the latest system updates. You can also install any upcoming releases you may have pre-ordered, while you’re at it.
Call in Sick
If you’re feeling a gaming flu coming on (and there’s a lot of that going around right now), then take a sick day, rather than risk infecting your coworkers or classmates. Sometimes you just need to listen to your body’s needs, relax, and let the fever run its course. Miami’s own DJ Khaled, aka Dr. XBOX will write you a personalized note to help explain the situation. If this thing is really serious, you may even need the whole week to recover – it’s the responsible thing to do.
Hire a Dog Walker
We all have responsibilities. Some of them come with four legs and a suspect bladder. Don’t let Rufus ruin your gaming fun. Get ahold of a local dog walker to take them outside so you can enjoy the big day uninterrupted. Or drop them off at doggie daycare for a day (or week) to get them out of your hair.
Reconsider Placement of Your XBOX
Is your XBOX in an area of the house that is easily accessible to younger players? Consider the steps you need to take to get it out of younger sightlines, like running an extension cable out to the shed in the backyard or huddling up in your at-home office. Even if you do find yourself bouncing between rooms, your save files reside in the Cloud, allowing you to pick up your session wherever you last plugged your console in.
Update Your Playlist
We’re always on the hunt for new tunes and one of the things we’re most looking forward to on November 19 is discovering a whole bunch of new tracks that are sure to make our listening playlist pop throughout the year. You can get started here on Spotify.
Create a New XBOX Wireless Controller to Commemorate the Day
XBOX Design Lab lets you create your own next-gen XBOX Wireless Controller. Choose from a combination of colors, patterns, textured grips, and more. You could even pick up some specially themed versions of controllers styled in hot pink and pastels – this one is particularly striking.
Charge Your Controller
Speaking of controllers, if you expect long gaming sessions in your near future, make sure that it’s plugged in so it has a full charge when you need it, or stock up on AA batteries. Maybe even get a backup controller ready so you can hot-swap them in and minimize interruptions.
Prepare for a Tale of Two Tragic Lovers in Crime
Looking for something to add to your queue? Check out the 1967 classic, “Bonnie and Clyde,” featuring Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway to get you in the mood for an epic story about two tragic lovers who fall into a life of crime. We’ll have to wait and see if the outcome is any different this time around starting on November 19.
Watch Out for Gators
No seriously, we saw one recently.
The post How to Get Ready for November 19 appeared first on XBOX Wire.

items.title: Millions of Butt Slaps: Last Pirates Sails into XBOX Game Preview
items.content:
Summary
Online co-op comedy horror game for up to four players.
Out now in XBOX Game Preview with Steam crossplay.
The story of how it got here and what’s next.
Ahoy, pirates! We’re RetroStyle Games, a team from Kyiv, Ukraine, and our online co-op horror game Last Pirates: Die Together is out today in XBOX Game Preview on XBOX Series X|S and PC. It has crossplay with Steam! So, a lobby can be half on console and half on PC and still lose their butts together.
Up to four pirates land on a cursed island, grab treasure with stretchy arms and drag it back to the ship before the captain’s quota runs out. In practice monsters flip the cart, a monkey begs for coins (bro, we’re broke too), and somebody always wants to tear off a friend’s booty and slap it.
Honestly, we had no idea what to write here. We’ve never done anything like this before. Making a game is a thousand small stories, and they won’t fit into 1,000 words. We could just write “butt” a thousand times, but we’d rather share a few favorites, so you get to know the crew behind the booty.
Story 1: The Game Jam that Got out of Hand
After Ocean Keeper, our pretty serious roguelike, we wanted something much lighter, so in January, 2026 we ran a game jam inside the studio. Once the pirate prototype was playable, the office never got quiet again. Why pirates? Yarr, who doesn’t love pirates?!
Loot first, questions later. Every coin counts toward the captain’s quota.
Story 2: The Playtest Where the Butt Came off
We wanted our pirates to be breakable, so at zero health they snap in half. In one playtest everybody kept trying to stick the bottom half back on, so we coded it, and the revive worked better than anything we had planned. Now monsters bite butts off, crewmates steal them, and a downed pirate comes back when a friend slaps a spare booty onto them.
For Steam Next Fest in June we put a giant butt on the beach and asked players to slap it a million times to unlock an update. An average pirate lands about 1,000 slaps in five hours, so we expected it to take a while. But(t)… one crew of four did it alone in seven hours. We were not prepared.
Our crew, showing off their best side.
Story 3: The Mimic Learns to Talk
For a long time the Mimic was our most boring monster: it only copied how a player looked, and we could spot it every time. Then streamers walked straight up to it, sure it was their buddy. Okay, the Mimic works. Time to make it worse. Now each Mimic picks any player in the lobby, copies their skin and borrows short shouts from their voice chat. Two Mimics on the map? Two pirates in the crew have evil twins. Today it’s our favorite monster (not counting the muscle-mice, they’re number one).
When the lights go out, hide. Then hide better.
Story 4: Our Favorite Bug, and Other Things Players Found that we Never Made
Every streamer we’ve played with does the same two things on their first spawn: slaps a butt, then climbs into the cauldron and flies off the map, thanks to a bug they all find within seconds. Maybe we were all witches in a past life. The cauldron still flies, and we’re keeping it.
Then a group on YouTube snuck up behind our monster who only moves when nobody’s looking (we call him Misha, short for Man In Shdows), sniffed his butt, and he vanished. Pure coincidence, but they were sure it was a secret mechanic and kept sniffing him for the rest of the video. It “worked” two times out of three. There’s no such mechanic, and it was so funny to watch.
Misha only moves when nobody’s looking. Sniff at your own risk.
Story 5: A Bowling Prophecy
We also dreamed of a certain YouTuber playing it, the one the internet pictures as a bag of milk in a propeller hat. One night the marketing team went bowling and made a bet: if each of us rolled a strike in a row, we’d email him. We all did. The email with the subject line “Bowling prophecy” went out, he answered, and he actually played Last Pirates. We’re still not over it.
Story 6: Kyiv
Some days the meeting moves to the shelter, or a playtest runs on the generator during blackouts. One morning a strike hit across the road, bent our windows inward and injured one of our teammates. That’s the scary reality for everyone who lives in Ukraine. It doesn’t stop us: this team and this silly pirate game keep us sane, and we want to bring a little joy. If people get scared, let it be of Misha or a jump scare and nothing else. We are so grateful to everyone who makes it possible for us to keep making games in Kyiv.
Current Port: XBOX, and We’re Not Stopping
On XBOX the game gets the same updates as Steam at the same time, and crews can mix both platforms. A new event is coming this winter, and after that, the full release.
One crew, any platform: XBOX Series X|S, XBOX on PC and Steam.
What’s in XBOX Game Preview
• Online co-op for one to four players, with Steam crossplay.
• Optimized for XBOX Series X|S.
• XBOX Play Anywhere: buy once, play on XBOX Series X|S and PC.
• In-game voice chat (the Mimic says thanks).
• A lobby browser to find a crew.
• Meta-progression: weapons, items and a wardrobe full of skins.
• Regular updates in sync with Steam.
See you on the Islands
Last Pirates: Die Together is out now in XBOX Game Preview. Grab friends, slap booty, set sail and let us know what you think! Thank you from the bottom of our hearts.
P.S. Butt, butt, butt. It would be a sin not to use this chance, hehe.

Last Pirates: Die Together is a comedic online co-op adventure for up to 4 players. You and your crew use wobbly, stretchy arms to haul as much treasure as possible back to your captain. Break down doors, snatch every coin in sight, and survive the monsters, the traps, and each other's terrible decisions along the way.
Every run drops you onto a mysterious island full of cursed loot and lurking creatures. Team up, make a plan, and shout over voice chat. Just make sure at least one of you makes it back to the ship with the gold. Be a hero, hide like a coward, or "accidentally" volunteer a teammate as a distraction. They will be fine. Probably.
Expect chaotic physics and voice-morphing mayhem. And the butts do more than revive your crew: each one grants its own buff that shakes up how you play. It is loud, it is messy, and it is best played with friends.
Round up your crew. Grab the treasure. Make it a story worthy of a shanty.
Full details on the latest status of the game, how you can give feedback and report issues can be found at https://discord.gg/YywWVj4jJK

Nekochuofficial interview: Finding a hero through Soldier: 76
items.content:
When Overwatch launched in 2016, players were introduced to 21 heroes. One of these heroes was none other than Soldier: 76, and even after 10 years, he remains a fan favorite. Esports.gg sat down with Soldier: 76 connoisseur Nekochuofficial to learn about what makes the hero so compelling even after all these years.
Soldier: 76 in Overwatch (Image credit: esports.gg)
Nekochuofficial interview: Discovering Overwatch
In his interview with esports.gg, Nekochuofficial shared that he first discovered Overwatch through his sister before finding a personal connection with Soldier: 76. Back in 2016, his sister started playing the game and showed him many of the cinematics.
Interestingly, however, she didn’t show him the “Hero” one featuring Soldier: 76. It was in 2021 when Nekochuofficial’s best friend introduced him to more of the Overwatch roster. This led him to duking it out as Reaper and learning more about his story before discovering his eventual favorite. Nekochuofficial really liked the Soldier: 24 skin that belonged to Reaper back then and even now.
“My best friend was showing me Overwatch characters around mid-to-late 2021,” he said. “I actually used to be a Reaper main before I became a Soldier: 76 main. I’ve been playing since before the Overwatch 2 stuff got around, but that’s where I think I really started.”
Soldier: 76’s Strike Commander Morrison skin and Reaper’s Soldier: 24 skin (Image credit: esports.gg)
Why Soldier: 76 is Nekochuofficial’s favorite Overwatch hero
Speaking of Reaper, it was a piece of Reaper76 fanart that sparked Nekochuofficial’s interest in Soldier: 76. The artwork showed the characters in their younger days as Gabriel Reyes and Jack Morrison, and Nekochuofficial became a fan of the handsome Strike Commander.
Reading the “Bastet,” “Future’s Past,” and “Lucky Man” short stories then helped him appreciate Soldier: 76 beyond his appearance.
Ana looking at an old photo of Jack and Vincent (Image credit: Blizzard Entertainment)
“I got to see like a little bit of his personality,” Nekochuofficial said. “Like how he’s gruff, the Soldier Enhancement Program’s effects on him, how sheepish he can be sometimes with Ana, and how determined he is. And he’s gay? That’s so cool.”
He continued, “I think that’s the first time I’ve seen something like that. I didn’t really play FPS games at all. So I think that was kind of like the first time I’ve seen someone be openly in the LGBTQ+ space in an AAA shooter.”
Soldier: 76 is among Overwatch’s canon LGBTQ+ heroes (Image credit: Blizzard Entertainment)
When Blizzard Entertainment introduced Soldier: 76’s older Overwatch 2 appearance, complete with a beard, it changed how Nekochuofficial viewed the hero once again.
“It’s kind of that point on where it went from, ‘Oh, he’s cute. I kind of like this character’ to ‘Oh my gosh, he feels paternal,’ if that makes sense,” he said. “He’s really like that dad figure.”
On my soul this was my first ever Tactical Paws art I made pic.twitter.com/rd3b9AAYEi
— Nekochuofficial 🐾 The Soldier: 76 Connoisseur 💙 (@nekochuofficial) August 2, 2026
Tactical Paws: Of comfort, healing, and family
Nekochuofficial then told esports.gg how Soldier: 76 soon became a comforting character, sharing that drawing the hero alongside his fursona helped him come to terms with his complicated relationship with his late father. He described Soldier: 76 and Neko artwork as “familial yumeshipping.”
“It’s what people call a familial yumeship — where it’s kind of like instead of you seeing them as their partner, you see them as a familiar figure like your parent or your sibling,” Nekochuofficial explained. “I call it Tactical Paws.”
Changed my watch face to be more tactical paws, I am NOT keeping it on at work though pic.twitter.com/OjtVdIgwgX
— Nekochuofficial 🐾 The Soldier: 76 Connoisseur 💙 (@nekochuofficial) October 20, 2026
Why Overwatch players ship Reaper76
Overwatch fanfiction also became a source of comfort for Nekochuofficial. He said that he particularly enjoys soft, fluffy stories featuring Soldier: 76. He’s especially fond of the Reaper76 fanfics that show the tough Strike Commander in a more vulnerable state with Gabriel Reyes stepping in to take care of him.
According to Nekochuofficial, Reaper and Soldier: 76’s relationship has the potential to develop further in canon as well, but he understands that it depends on Blizzard Entertainment. He said that he’d love to see a Reaper 76 renaissance with more fanart and perhaps even recognition from the official Overwatch account on social media.
“I like it because of the potential. I think more people should ship it,” he said, noting how both characters have complicated romantic pasts.
Nekochuofficial then gave a shoutout to Reaper76 artist Scaryspookycoin.
Warm up sketch :'D#reaper76 #soldier76 #reaperow pic.twitter.com/y6glqLbUqF
— Scaryspookycoin🍉 (@scaryspookycoin) September 29, 2021
“Bones heal, pain is temporary, and scars look good.”
In terms of what Nekochuofficial would like to see for Soldier: 76 moving forward, he told esports.gg that he hopes the Overwatch team continues its push for more lore. He would love to learn more about the Conspiracy, see the hero interact with Sierra, and get more skins featuring Soldier: 76’s older appearance.
“One thing I will say that I want to see more of in the future is more of Soldier: 76’s perspective of things,” Nekochuofficial said. “How is his goal of finding the Conspiracy going? Is Illari going to come back? Is he finally going to confront Moira?”
He continued, “I want to see more skins of him with his Overwatch 2 hair, his Overwatch 2 beard. I know we have Colder: 76, but that’s kind of like the closest thing I have to it. I want to see more visorless Soldier: 76 where he’s old with scars and everything. I think that would make me really happy. It also would be really cute to see him in a Soldier: 76 casual skin like how Hanzo has one. We can maybe do a leather jacket.”
The Colder: 76 skin in Overwatch (Image credit: esports.gg)
That’s all for now. Stick around on esports.gg for more Overwatch interviews, news, guides, and updates!

items.title: World of Fallout Exhibit at the Las Vegas Atomic Museum Expands – and It’s Full of Easter Eggs for Fans
items.content:
This past weekend, the National Atomic Testing Museum in Las Vegas, Nevada (aka, “Old Vegas”) doubled the size of its “World of Fallout” exhibit, which has been open to the public since November 2025. The exhibit juxtaposes recreated objects from the Fallout universe with the real-life artifacts from the nuclear era that inspired the game’s design. Playfully dark satire of Atomic Age retrofuturism and Cold War paranoia has always been a central pillar of the Fallout franchise, making the Atomic Museum a uniquely fitting place to explore the relationship between the games, and now the Prime Video series, and the real-world history that inspired them. One year after its launch, the exhibit has now doubled its footprint with two new galleries, featuring an interactive Overseer’s Desk, a fan-made, full-size Mister Handy robot, on-camera costumes from Season 2 of Prime Video’s “Fallout,” and more.
Below are some tips for what to check out in the newly expanded exhibit, and some of our favorite easter eggs tying together the Fallout universe with real-world history.
Always Be Scavenging
Just like playing a Fallout game, the best way to experience the exhibit is to take your time and pay attention to the little things. Even before reaching the World of Fallout galleries, you can take part in a Fallout Finds, an interactive scavenger hunt throughout the museum that encourages you to track down Fallout-themed items and scan their QR codes. Once you’re in the World of Fallout, be sure to keep scavenging, hidden historical artifacts and supply caches to be found tucked away in certain drawers and cabinets.
The Perks of Being a Hacker
Again, just like in the games, there are terminals to hack at the new Overseer’s Desk. Succeed, and you’ll get to read strange and spooky real-life anecdotes from the long history of the Nevada Test Site. Even if you’re a Fallout hacking master and have no trouble cracking the code, be sure to fail deliberately … you’ll want to see the warning that pops up
Signed Work
The exhibit features replicas of the in-game signs for New Vegas and the Lucky 38 casino, complete with classic Vegas neon. These were created in partnership with the University of Nevada, Las Vegas by students and staff in its Entertainment, Engineering, and Design program, providing what was no doubt a fun and valuable hands-on learning experience.
Fact or Fiction
One of the exhibit’s main elements juxtaposes real historical objects, like posters and pulp books, with their fictional Fallout equivalents. You might be surprised at how little Fallout exaggerates some parts of ’50s material culture.
Hands Off Mister Handy
Visitors to the exhibit are greeted by a life-size Mister Handy robot replica, created by fan fabricator, Dragonfoot3D, who also made the Deathclaw and terminal replicas.. Unlike some other parts of the exhibit, this unique museum piece is not to be touched, and his eyes will react threateningly if you get too close, to underline the point.
Photo Bombers
Pay particular attention to photos around the exhibit for some fun cameos. The Vault features an autographed photo of Edward Teller, father of the hydrogen bomb (memorably played by Benny Safdie in “Oppenheimer”), given to Troy Wade, one of the museum founders and a key employee at the Nevada Test Site. There is also a discreetly tucked-away photo of some Bethesda staff who helped make this exhibit possible.
Audio Log
Actor/crooner Perry Como’s music hasn’t graced the games themselves yet, but it sits right in their midcentury musical wheelhouse, as evidenced by songs being prominently featured in the Season 1 opening and Season 2 finale of Prime Video’s “Fallout.” There’s another real-world connection too; Como was born in Canonsburg, Pennsylvania, which hosted important nuclear material processing facilities in the ’40s and ’50s. Hidden in the exhibit, you’ll find Perry Como sheet music alongside a vial that once held radium paint produced in Canonsburg.
Gary
High-Perception fans may notice “GARY” spelled out in a stack of blocks. It’s a nod to Vault 108 in Fallout 3, where a cloning experiment left the vault overrun by hostile copies of the same unfortunate dweller, all named Gary, and all only able to say one thing …“Gary.”
The expanded World of Fallout exhibit is open now at the National Atomic Testing Museum in Las Vegas, Nevada. Find out more and how to visit on the official website.

items.title: Ice Cream Simulator: Why We Gave Our Customers Infinite Patience
items.content:
In Ice Cream Simulator, you can leave a customer waiting, go away for an hour, and come back to find them still standing there, ready to order.
They have nowhere more important to be. They have chosen ice cream.
We respect that.
Their infinite patience is one of our most deliberate design decisions. We wanted to capture the pleasure of running your own ice cream shop while giving you time to enjoy it. Real life already supplies plenty of deadlines. We didn’t feel the need to put another one on a cone.
It Started with a Scoop
Our inspiration was simple: we love ice cream.
We also hadn’t seen many games explore running an ice cream shop in the way we imagined. We wanted to create something cozy and hands-on, where you could turn your love of dessert into a business of your own.
The design challenge was giving that simple idea enough depth to keep you interested, while protecting the relaxed atmosphere that made us want to build it.
Hold the Stress
We built the shop around a daily rhythm. During the day, you serve ice cream with different toppings and sauces, along with milkshakes. At night, you prepare for the days ahead.
That rhythm gives you both sides of the experience: the satisfaction of serving an order and the preparation that makes tomorrow’s orders possible.
But serving customers can easily become a game about speed. We wanted you to settle into the routine, so we gave customers unlimited patience. Take your time with an order. Step away if you need to. Your customer will remain impressively committed to dessert.
For us, this was a way to put the emphasis on decisions about the business. You have time to think about what you are building, which leads to the question at the heart of the game: what kind of shop do you want to run?
Three Customers, Three Priorities
We designed three customer groups to give that question a meaningful answer.
Elite customers want the best ice cream and don’t care about the price. They are here for quality, and your ingredient budget is about to hear about it.
Office customers look for a balance between price and quality. They appreciate good ice cream, but they would also appreciate the numbers making sense.
Casual customers care most about affordability. Premium ingredients are not the selling point for them. A reasonably priced ice cream is.
Those differences are why we wanted you to choose between cheaper and more premium ingredients. Keeping costs low can support a shop aimed at casual customers. Spending more on quality can support one designed to attract elite customers.
We wanted both approaches to have a purpose. Buying the most expensive ingredients should be a decision that fits your business, rather than an automatic answer to every problem.
Your Shop, Your Style
Once you start thinking about your audience, the walls become surprisingly relevant.
Our attractiveness attribute connects the appearance of your shop with the customers it attracts. Renovating the floors, walls, and ceiling becomes part of your business strategy. This means staring at flooring options counts as a business meeting. You’re the owner. You make the rules.
With renovation choices ranging up to premium options, you can shape the surroundings alongside the menu. We wanted decorating to feel connected to the shop you are building and the people you hope will visit.
Seating adds another small but meaningful interaction: customers can sit, enjoy their ice cream, and leave a tip. Seeing someone spend time in a space you have put together helps make it feel like a little shop with a life of its own.
A Change in the Weather
We wanted variety to come from the world around the shop, too.
There are four weather conditions, changing every two in-game days. Each affects the visuals and the number of customers visiting, bringing a different atmosphere and pace to familiar surroundings. Apparently, our customers can wait forever, but they still have opinions about the weather.
These choices all grew from the same goal: creating a cozy business that gives you room to make it your own. Your ingredients, prices, and surroundings help define the shop you want to run. Our love of ice cream started the project. The interesting part was turning that love into decisions players could enjoy making for themselves.
We can’t wait to see what kind of shop you create in Ice Cream Simulator. Whether you’re serving affordable scoops or building a premium ice cream destination, we hope you enjoy making it your own.
See you behind the counter. Take your time—we’ve already told the customers.
Ice Cream Simulator

Get it now
Have you ever dreamed of running your very own ice cream shop? In Ice Cream Simulator, you can create your dream shop, prepare delicious ice cream, serve customers, and grow your own business. It’s a relaxing simulation game where creativity and good management go hand in hand.
Start by preparing ice cream and serving your first customers. Experiment with different ingredients, create new flavors, and try to meet the expectations of your visitors. Every customer can have different preferences, so preparing the right orders will be the key to success.
Running an ice cream shop is about much more than simply selling ice cream. You’ll also need to manage the entire business – take care of its growth, hire staff, organize the work, and gradually upgrade your shop. As your business grows, new opportunities will become available, allowing you to build an even bigger and more unique ice cream shop.
Customization also plays an important role. You can furnish and decorate your ice cream shop however you want, creating a cozy place that customers will enjoy coming back to. It’s up to you to decide how your shop looks and how it operates.
The changing weather also has an impact on the gameplay. Different weather conditions can affect the atmosphere in your shop, as well as the behavior and needs of your customers, making each day a little different. Keep an eye on your surroundings, react to changing situations, and adapt your business to the current conditions.
Ice Cream Simulator focuses primarily on relaxing gameplay and the enjoyment of running your own business. If you enjoy simulation games, management, decorating your own spaces, and laid-back gameplay, this might be the perfect game for you.

items.title: Valve Teases CS2 Winter Cobblestone With 30-Second Snow Clip
items.content:
Counter-Strike’s Cobblestone has received an official teaser from Valve. The company posted a 30-second clip of a snow-covered Cobblestone on the official Counter-Strike account on November 17, 2026. The post reads “’Tis the season,” and the clip ends on a “Cobble” seal. Valve has not shared a release date or said which layout will return. Cobblestone has not been officially in Counter-Strike since the March 19, 2019 CS:GO update.
Below, you can read what the teaser shows, the commentary used in the clip, the map’s history, earlier leaks, and what remains unknown.
CS2 Winter Cobblestone Teaser
Valve posted the teaser on Tuesday, November 17. The clip walks through a snowy version of Cobblestone at dusk.
'Tis the season. pic.twitter.com/qRLYkRHAmL
— CS2 (@CounterStrike) November 17, 2026
The castle towers, red banners, and walls look the same as in CS:GO. A pink and purple winter sky lights the scene. Snow covers the ground and the rooftops. The lighting is darker than on most current CS2 maps.
The clip ends on a red wax seal that reads “Cobble.” Valve gave no other details in the post.
Sadokist Commentary Features Snax’s Famous Clutch
The teaser uses a voiceover from Matthew “Sadokist” Trivett. He comments on Janusz “snax” Pogorzelski’s 1v4 pistol clutch on Cobblestone.
Snax made the play for Virtus.Pro against NAVI at ESL One New York 2016. The moment remains one of the best-known plays on the map.
Cobblestone CS2 Release Date
Valve has not announced a release date. It has also not said which version of the layout is coming back.
The company usually lets updates speak for themselves, so details should arrive with the patch notes. It is also not known whether Cobblestone will join the competitive map pool or arrive as a seasonal addition for the colder months.
Cobblestone went through several versions in CS:GO. One player wrote that they hope the layout follows an older version, not the most recent one from CS:GO.
The table shows that Valve has confirmed only the teaser. Every gameplay detail is still open.
Cobblestone History in Counter-Strike
Valve removed Cobblestone from the Active Duty map pool on April 20, 2018. Dust2 replaced it. The map left the game entirely with the March 19, 2019 CS:GO update.
Players have asked for Cobblestone to return for years. The same is true of Cache, which Valve has since added to CS2.
Earlier Leaks Pointed to Snowy Cobblestone
The teaser follows a long trail of leaks. Dataminer Gabe Follower first found snow-themed assets in the game files in 2023. Other dataminers later backed up the find.
More snowy Cobblestone files appeared during 2026. A November update then revealed commands for a frost system. The commands cover frost building up on weapons, players, and chickens.
Valve had not announced the frost mechanic at the time. Read more in our CS2 frost mechanic report.
Why the Timing Matters for CS2
CS:GO received temporary festive changes each year from 2012 to 2022. Since CS2 launched, Valve has not released a traditional December holiday update. A winter Cobblestone would be the first seasonal winter update in CS2.
The teaser also arrives after CS2 lost players for eight months in a row. That drop came even after Valve added Cache and a new 3v3 mode.
The post Valve Teases CS2 Winter Cobblestone With 30-Second Snow Clip appeared first on TalkEsport.

The Game Awards 2026 Nominees: Full List of Every Category
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto VI leads The Game Awards 2026 nominees with eight nominations, including Game of the Year, after Geoff Keighley revealed the shortlist across all categories in a livestream on 17 November. Rockstar Games’ open world title earned its place two days before its own launch, with its release landing inside this year’s eligibility window by a single day.
CONTROL Resonant and Resident Evil Requiem follow with six nominations each, while Phantom Blade Zero has five. The ceremony takes place on 10 December 2026 at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, with Keighley hosting for the thirteenth time. A jury drawn from more than 160 media and creator outlets picked the nominees, and fans can vote now through the official The Game Awards website.
The Game Awards 2026 Game of the Year nominees
Six games are competing for the top prize this year. The shortlist mixes new releases, a returning Remedy franchise and Nintendo’s remake of one of the most celebrated games ever made.
Grand Theft Auto VI appears in Game of the Year, Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, Best Score and Music, Best Audio Design, Best Performance, Best Art Direction and Best Action/Adventure Game. The game will not be in players’ hands when voting opens, as millions prepare for GTA 6 launch day streams later this week. Games released on or before 20 November qualified this year, while Players’ Voice entries have until 30 November.
Nominees for craft and performance awards
Capcom holds two of the five Best Game Direction slots through Pragmata and Resident Evil Requiem. The Blood of Dawnwalker, the debut game from Rebel Wolves and Bandai Namco, is the only Best Narrative nominee absent from the Game of the Year list. Rahul Kohli earns a Best Performance nomination for Saros, alongside Manni L. Perez for Grand Theft Auto VI.
