GTA 6 New Zealand Release Time Revealed: Check Here
items.content:
GTA 6 New Zealand release time is 12:00 AM NZDT on Thursday, November 19, 2026. Rockstar Games confirmed a rolling midnight launch, so New Zealand gets Grand Theft Auto VI first on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. That moment equals 11:00 UTC on November 18, which is 4:30 PM IST in India. Players in other countries unlock the game at their own local midnight.
Below, you will find the New Zealand unlock time in major time zones, how the rolling launch works, and the GTA 6 preload details.
GTA 6 New Zealand Release Time and Date
The launch begins at 12:00 AM NZDT in New Zealand and moves across the globe as each country reaches midnight on November 19. The game releases on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
The New Zealand PlayStation Store lists the unlock as November 18 at 11:00 AM UTC, which is midnight in Auckland on November 19. New Zealand Daylight Time is UTC+13.
For most of the world, the first unlock happens on November 18. Players elsewhere still wait for their own local midnight.
New Zealand Unlock Time in Other Time Zones
This table shows the New Zealand unlock converted to other time zones. It does not show when players in those regions can start playing.
Indian players reach their own midnight on November 19, later than New Zealand. The 4:30 PM IST time marks only the moment New Zealand unlocks.
How the GTA 6 Rolling Midnight Launch Works
GTA 6 does not unlock at one moment worldwide. Each country gets the game at 12:00 AM local time on November 19. Rockstar applies this rule to both PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
Regional store listings show Mexico and Central America unlocking last, at 6:00 UTC on November 19. That is about 19 hours after New Zealand.
GTA 6 Preload Details
The GTA 6 preload is already live. On PS5, digital preload began at midnight local time on November 10, 2026. On Xbox Series X|S, it began globally at 12 AM GMT on November 10. Rockstar first announced November 12 as the preload date and later moved it to November 10.
The game is a download of over 200GB. Players who preloaded can launch the game once their region unlocks.
What About the New Zealand Trick?
Some guides describe a “New Zealand trick” that involves changing a console’s region and time to New Zealand to play early. Neither Rockstar nor PlayStation has announced that it works.

AnkiiiBot Defends Aadi Over Team SouL Targeting Controversy
items.content:
Nebula Esports, led by former IGL Aditya “Aadi” Dawar, targeted Team SouL in the last match of Battlegrounds Mobile India Showdown 2026 (BMSD 2026). Although he explained his reason behind his actions, the criticism did not seem to stop. BGMI caster Ankit “AnkiiiBOT” Pandey recently shared his two cents on the controversy.
AnkiiiBot Asserts Targeting Is a Part of The Game
In a recent livestream, in the context of Nebula Esports (former roster) targeting Team SouL, AnkiiiBot asserted that there’s nothing wrong with it and that it is a part of the game. “I don’t know, man. Why do people take this stuff so personally? Targeting and all is part of the game, period.”
Further clarifying his stance, AnkiiiBot added that Aadi doesn’t need to explain why he targeted someone. “It’s a game. You felt like doing it, you did it.”
He staunchly added that there is no official rule against targeting another team, and if someone has a problem, they can get a rule written down by Krafton itself saying that you can’t target. However, he was quick to clarify that he was not isolating this event, but he is talking about all the ‘targeting’ controversies that have emerged over the past few years. “I’m not saying this just about this particular matter. There have been plenty of instances like this, whether it was regarding Hector or some other team.”
AnkiiiBot Recalls RevenantXSpark and GodLike Esports Targeting Controversy in BMPS 2026 and BGIS 2026
AnkiiiBot recalled a similar instance that happened with RevenantXSpark and GodLike Esports in BGMI Pro Series 2026 (BMPS 2026) and Battlegrounds Mobile India Series (BGIS 2026). He asserted that it is a sensible thing to do against a strong team because naturally they would want to eliminate the strongest competition from the lobby. “Why wouldn’t they? You’re a strong team. They would want you out of the tournament. They wouldn’t want you to win a trophy.” He added, “So what’s the big deal? In the next tournament (BMPS 2026), you targeted them, you even won, and that was that. The tournament was settled.”
Sharing his personal opinion, AnkiiiBot said, “Everyone should just do whatever they want.”
Targeting another team has always been viewed as an unethical practice in BGMI esports. However, in a competitive tournament, eliminating your biggest opponent can be a sensible decision, especially when that team poses a major threat to your chances of winning. It can even be one of the most strategic moves a team makes during a match. As long as there is no official rule against it, targeting remains a part of the game, and teams are free to make such decisions based on their strategies.

League's current client has been a frequent source of frustration within the community for years, with players regularly reporting bugs, performance issues and stability problems. As a result, a ground-up refresh of the software underpinning the game could end up being one of New Dawn's most impactful changes.

Aadi Reveals Why He Targeted Team SouL in BMSD 2026, Alleges Poaching
items.content:
Vasista Esports’ current BGMI IGL Aditya “Aadi” Dawar explained why he targeted Team SouL in the final match of BGMI Showdown 2026 (BMSD 2026), while he was playing for Nebula Esports. Aadi voiced his frustration over Team SouL’s alleged poaching behaviour following BGMI Pro Series 2026 (BMPS 2026) and his actions stemmed from that. He also revisited the poaching incidents he has faced throughout his career since Team SouL signed Goblin from iNSANE Esports in 2022.
Aadi Expresses His Frustration on Team SouL’s Alleged Poaching Behaviour
Aadi is one of the oldest active players in the BGMI esports scene, having been playing the game professionally from at least 2021. Over the years, as the IGL, he has fostered multiple esports athletes who have been making waves in the esports scene or have won multiple official esports events. However, Aadi himself has only won one A-tier tournament, BGMI Masters Series Season 5.
When Aadi recently went live on his YouTube channel, his viewers started spamming why Nebula Esports, his erstwhile team in BMSD 2026, targeted Team SouL in the last match on Miramar. Responding to this, he stated that there were a lot of things piled up in his mind about Team SouL and it was a reaction to all those things.
Elaborating his earlier remarks, Aadi alleged that, following BMPS 2026, where both teams showcased mediocre performances, one of Team SouL’s players called one of Nebula Esports erstwhile players and talked about signing him. “Now, tell me one thing. Maybe Krafton gave these guys special permission, or I honestly don’t know, because how can you change a player during the lock-in window? Perhaps Krafton gave them permission to make changes even during the lock-in period. I have no idea,” he sarcastically added.
Aadi went on to question Team SouL’s intention behind the call. “What really got to me was if you can’t actually sign the player, why are you calling him in the first place? What is your mindset behind doing that?” Expressing his suspicion, he added, “Personally, I feel they called him for one reason, to mess with the player’s head. They can’t even sign him, so they just want to unsettle him and ruin the good thing we have going. That’s what I think their main goal was.”
Aadi Calls Out Poaching Saga He Has Faced in His Career
Since the start of his career, Aadi has fostered a lot of underdog players and made them a few of the finest in the esports scene. This includes renowned players like Team SouL’s Harsh “Goblin” Paudwal, Gladiator Esports’ Naman “Neyo” Adiani, Team Outrage’s Raghuraj “Slug” Singh, Team Apex Gaming’s Harsh “Harsh” Negi, and a lot more.
Aadi outlined a pattern that he has noticed throughout his career. “Every time, I build a lineup. I develop players from scratch. I pick up underdogs when they’re just starting out, and I build them up. Then you guys come along, looking for already-established players to add to your teams. And in the process, you break up the good lineup I’ve managed to build. Am I an idiot for constantly building teams from scratch?”
Aadi pointed to what he described as a recurring problem, “You guys just always want to be the ones who win. You don’t want the person who puts in the hard work, who builds a player from scratch, to ever win.” He further expressed his frustration, “Think about it. Someone works incredibly hard and puts everything into making a player good and building a strong team. Then, just when that player reaches his peak, you call him and make an offer. Just like that.”
Aadi further shared, “These are the kinds of things that have been bothering me for a long time. They really get on my nerves. And this is another example of that.”
Aadi Shuts Down His Critics
Following the team’s action at BMSD 2026, Aadi faced a lot of criticism. Addressing the criticism, he said, “Isn’t this unethical too? You’re calling our players during the lock-in window and making them offers, saying, ‘We’ll sign you after the lock-in.’ Our player is obviously still going to put in his full effort.”
Following this, Aadi traced the issue back to when Team SouL signed Goblin from iNSANE Esports back in early 2022. “So, if this continues, or if you keep provoking me by calling my players and messing with their heads… then understand this: I targeted you in the last match, and next time I can start targeting you even earlier. I might not win, but I won’t let you win either. That’s my mindset, plain and simple.”
As of now, Team SouL has not issued any response to Aadi’s allegations. While his statements have raised concerns about the team’s alleged poaching practices, these claims remain allegations. Poaching has been a long-standing issue in the BGMI esports industry, which is why Krafton introduced lock-in periods and transfer windows to regulate player transfers and prevent such incidents. However, Aadi’s recent statements raise questions about whether these measures are being followed effectively and whether they are enough to address the issue.

items.title: Communication Score in Dota 2: How to increase and keep it high
items.content:
To increase your Communication Score in Dota 2 and keep it high, you need to be respectful and considerate of other players when using in-game communication tools. Avoid unnecessary chat, arguments with teammates, excessive pinging, and refusing to commend or swap commends with other players after matches.
Communication Score is a metric designed to keep Dota 2 players from misusing its in-game communication features and to promote a more mature and healthier playing environment. If you want to learn more, this post will provide you with all the updated information about Communication Score, especially if you’re having issues with it being too low.
Key Takeaways
Dota 2’s Communication Score measures how players use in-game communication tools, with a maximum of 12,000 points. Low scores progressively restrict access to features such as voice chat, text chat, pings, and chat wheels.
To improve your score, limit unnecessary communication, avoid arguments and toxic interactions, ignore insults, and use chat, voice, and pings only when they help your team.
Playing your assigned role and avoiding behavior that causes unnecessary team conflicts can also help you maintain a healthier in-game environment.
Communication Score updates every 15 matches, and Turbo games count toward that total. To maintain a high score, avoid spam, keep messages short, and treat teammates and opponents respectfully.
Table of contents
Key Takeaways
What is Communication Score in Dota 2?
How to raise my Communication Score in Dota 2
How can I maintain my high Communication Score in Dota 2
FAQs about Dota 2 Communication Scores
What is Communication Score in Dota 2?
A Communication Score of over 10,000 (Image credit: Valve)
Introduced in the 2023 Summer Client Update, the Communication Score is another metric that goes along with the Behavior Score. It has a threshold range of 0-10,000, but the maximum Communication Score that a player can get is 12,000.
Communication Score generally reflects the quality of a player’s in-game chat and speech interactions. If a player uses the game’s communication features to have toxic and unhealthy interactions with other players, the system will likely reduce an amount of Communication Score from that player.
Also read: How to increase Behavior Score in Dota 2
What happens if your communication score is too low?
As your Communication Score drops, Dota 2 gradually restricts your access to certain communication features. Below are the features that become unavailable when your score falls below specific thresholds.
Communication ScoreRestricted features
Less than 10,000Coaching and ping ally abilities
Less than 8,000Voice chat
Less than 7,000In-game tipping and requesting a coach
Less than 6,000Text chat and mini profile
Less than 5,000Map drawing
Less than 3,000All pings, alerts, and chatwheels (still usable, but on a 30-second cooldown)
If your Communication Score falls below 3,000, you’ll have a long way to go before regaining access to all communication features. However, as your score increases and reaches specific thresholds, the corresponding restricted features will gradually become available again.
As you see in the table above, denying yourself of those communication features will make it harder for you to coordinate plays with your teammates, hence making it difficult to win games and gain MMR.
How to raise my Communication Score in Dota 2
Avoid conversations like this (Image credit: Valve)
To increase your Communication Score and regain access to restricted in-game features, keep the following tips in mind. These practices have helped many players improve their scores and get back on track.
1. Disable or limit incoming chat
If you haven’t tried it yet, adjusting your chat settings can make your games much more peaceful. You can avoid much of the toxicity from other players by limiting or disabling the messages you see during a match.
Go to Settings, then select Social. Under the Allowed Chat options, you can either block every message you’ll see (No incoming chat) or limit messages to your friendly and party members only (Friendly players).
No communication means no toxic chat, so it is the easiest way of increasing your Communication Score without doing anything.
2. Communicate only when it matters the most
Communication Score isn’t designed to prevent any players from completely using the in-game chat features. You can still interact with your teammates or the enemy team, but limit it only to announcing ganks, asking for help, or reporting enemy movements.
3. Ignore insults or unhelpful remarks from other players
If another player starts flaming you or someone else, the best response is to ignore them. Let them engage in behavior that negatively affects their Communication Score. In the long run, they are the ones who may face the consequences, not you.
4. Play more Turbo matches to accelerate Dota 2 Communication Score updates
Many players try to increase their Communication Score faster by playing Turbo Mode. Your Communication Score is updated alongside your Behavior Score every 15 matches, and Turbo games count toward that total.
Turbo matches are designed to end much easier than normal matches, so it’s basically a hack that you can try to improve your scores not only in Communication but also in Behavior Score as well.
5. Play your role properly
You might not hear this often from other players, but practices involving not playing your designated role are often the main reasons why players, especially teammates, get into arguments.
In Ranked games, avoid taking every last hit from your core if you’re a support player, or do not pick a squishy support hero if you’re a solo middle, offlane, or carry (unless you can assure your teammates you are pretty good at it).
Since the fate of your MMR is often tied with your teammates, Ranked players expect everyone on the team to understand their hero’s role and how it performs throughout each stage of the game. Knowing what your hero needs to do can help prevent unnecessary arguments in team chat and keep everyone focused on winning.
How can I maintain my high Communication Score in Dota 2
For players with a Communication Score of 10,000 or higher, following these reminders can help maintain their score and potentially reach the 12,000-point cap.
Be friendly to your teammates and enemies to avoid getting reported. Your Communication Score also suffers if you receive multiple reports of Toxic Chat.
Do not spam pings. One or two pings is enough if you want to point something out, like warning an ally of incoming ganks or an enemy hiding in fog.
Don’t send long messages. Limiting your communication to other players also requires you to keep your messages short.
Avoid overusing chat wheels and voice lines. Use them sparingly if you can help it.
Commend everyone after a match. Commending encourages other players to commend you as well, and receiving commends might be a green flag for the system to increase your Communication Score.
FAQs about Dota 2 Communication Scores
Why is my Communication Score too low in Dota 2?
Your Communication Score may drop if other players report you for toxic behavior in text chat or voice chat, including excessive or disruptive communication during matches.
Do commends increase Communication Score in Dota 2
Commends are a positive sign of good conduct, but Valve has not clearly confirmed whether receiving them directly increases your Communication Score.
How long does it take to recover Communication Score?
Your Communication Score is updated every 15 matches, so recovery time depends on how low your score has dropped. Playing Turbo can help you finish the 15 matches faster since games are shorter.
Can you increase your Communication Score without using voice chat?
Yes, it is possible to increase Communication Score without using voice since you can always replace it fully with proper usage of text chats and pings.
What is the highest Communication Score in Dota 2?
The highest Communication Score you can reach in Dota 2 is 12,000. This gives players an extra 2,000 points before they start facing communication feature restrictions below 10,000.

items.content:
Following his departure from Tango Gameworks back in 2023, industry veteran Shinji Mikami went on to form a brand new studio: UNBOUND. After some slight teases, the studio was officially announced to have been acquired by SHIFT UP – the team behind the hit Stellar Blade – in what has been deemed more of a partnership than a pure acquisition. While we still do not know what the team is working on, Mikami has claimed that their first project is planned to release in 2027.
Taking part in an interview with the Japanese YouTube channel ‘TV Asahi’ (and translated by known Twitter user Genki_JPN), studio UNBOUND’s Shinji Mikami claimed that the team’s first project will “probably be released sometime in the middle or second half of next year.”
While Mikami is known best for his work on the massive Resident Evil franchise, the creative has also been responsible for many smaller – more unique – experiences, ranging from God Hand to Vanquish.
According to Mikami, UNBOUND’s first project will be closer to the latter than the former, with the 2027 title said to be “a small game, but it will be quite a fun and new game.”
That said, it appears as though the team have been conceiving a wide range of projects at different scales, having previously announced that they are also working on a AAA project of sorts for PC and consoles.
Either way, with Mikami being responsible for massive gaming franchises alongside smaller, cult hits, whatever UNBOUND is working on will certainly find a dedicated audience of fans. It will be interesting to see what is in store.

The nominees for Best Score Soundtrack for Video Games and Other Interactive Media at the 2027 Grammy Awards have been announced. This year's shortlist includes Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora – From the Ashes, 007: First Light, Ghost of Yotei, Marvel's Wolverine and Star Wars: Zero Company.

Previous winners of the category include Austin Wintory for Sword of the Sea in 2026, Winifred Phillips for Wizardry: Proving Grounds of the Mad Overlord in 2025, and Stephanie Economou for Assassin's Creed Valhalla: Dawn of Ragnarok, which took home the inaugural award in 2023. items.title: PS5 Hacker Gezine Claims Game Dump on Firmware 14.22, the Version GTA 6 Reportedly Needs
items.content:
PlayStation 5 security researcher Gezine has claimed to have dumped a game executable on PS5 system software 14.22. Grand Theft Auto VI reportedly needs that firmware version to run, and the game launches on 19 November. Gezine announced the result on X but did not name the game. He has not shared his method, published any files or released a tool.
A game executable, also called a game binary, is the program code a game needs to run. The PS5 keeps that code encrypted and protected. Dumping it means copying the code out of the console in a readable form. It is one step in examining how a game works, but it does not amount to a full jailbreak of the console.
Why the firmware 14.22 claim matters
Gezine had previously said the established method for dumping games stopped working on firmware 14.00 and later. On 19 October he posted that the “old way to dump executables does not seem to work at 14.xx”. He suggested at the time that a hypervisor exploit might be needed. The new claim suggests he has found another route, although he has not explained it.
In late October, Gezine also shared screenshots that appeared to show access to the debug menu on firmware 14.10. Sony released firmware 14.22 on 2 November. Public exploit tools still stop at firmware 13.60, and no public jailbreak exists for any 14.xx version. On 13 November, another modder, Echo Stretch, warned players not to expect a pirated copy of GTA 6.
A dumped executable is also what emulator developers and modders study when they try to run console games on other hardware. Even so, a single dump on one console does not let other players copy or run games. Running a dumped game on a PS5 would still need a working jailbreak on the same firmware, and none has been shown for 14.22. Gezine has not said whether he plans to go further.
Gezine keeps his PS5 research private
Gezine is known in the console homebrew scene for keeping his findings to himself. He reports vulnerabilities to companies through bug bounty programmes instead of releasing them publicly. He has found security flaws in both Nintendo and PlayStation consoles. That approach means a public tool based on this work may never appear.
Sony has not commented on the claim. It has taken a firmer line on modified consoles this year, cutting PSN access for PS5 systems running jailbreaks. Sony has not said whether firmware 14.22 contains fixes for the issue Gezine used, or whether a further update is planned.
The firmware 14.22 requirement for GTA 6 comes from listings in a PlayStation game size database. Sony and Rockstar Games have not confirmed it. Players can already preload the game, but nobody can start it before launch. Rockstar has not commented on Gezine’s claim.
Security around GTA 6 has drawn attention before launch. Arion Kurtaj, who leaked early footage of the game in 2022, pleaded guilty three days before the game launches. GTA 6 releases on 19 November on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

items.title: BGMI Joins Google Play Arena: Free Registration, MS Dhoni’s Mahi Clutchers and a Mumbai LAN Finale
items.content:
Krafton India has added Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI) and Real Cricket to Google Play Arena, the club-based mobile gaming championship run by Google Play with NODWIN Gaming. BGMI’s open qualifiers are already under way. Registration is free, open to players aged 18 and above, and closes on 27 November. The championship ends with a ticketed LAN finale in Mumbai on 19 and 20 December.
Top performers from the qualifiers will represent one of six clubs at the finale. The clubs are Team S8UL, GodLike Esports, Orangutan Gaming, Revenant XSpark, Team Apex Gaming and Mahi Clutchers. Mahi Clutchers is a new club led by former India cricket captain MS Dhoni. Its roster will be built entirely through the open qualifiers.
How the BGMI qualifiers for Google Play Arena work
The BGMI competition runs on two tracks. Amateur players register online and play through six club qualifiers, one for each club. Professional players enter through a separate closed qualifier. Both tracks meet at the Mumbai finale, where the championship will be decided in front of a live audience.
Google Play Arena has no entry fee and no paid entry routes. Players qualify on results alone. The full schedule is published on the Google Play Arena page. Organisers have not disclosed the prize pool, the Mumbai venue or ticket prices for the finale.
Krafton India and Google comment on the championship
Minu Lee, vice president and head of publishing at Krafton India, said the championship gives players “a door that anyone can walk through”. Lee pointed to the lack of an entry fee or invitation, and said the path ends “on a LAN stage in Mumbai in front of a live crowd”. Kanika Kalra, director of consumer apps and platforms marketing at Google India, said the aim was to “celebrate this talent on a national stage”. She described the event as a merit-led pathway from grassroots play to professional recognition.
BGMI covers the shooter category in the championship, while Real Cricket brings in a cricket title. Krafton India has not yet given dates or a format for the Real Cricket competition. The organisers have also not said which other games are part of Google Play Arena.
BGMI 4.7 runs through the Google Play Arena qualifiers
The qualifiers will be played on the BGMI 4.7 update, which arrives in November and stays live through the finale. The same update brings a Samay Raina collaboration to the game from 9 December. Team Apex Gaming, one of the six clubs, is in talks for a new BGMI line-up after its CEGC campaign.
BGMI has passed 260 million downloads. Krafton India also publishes Real Cricket, Road To Valor: Empires and CookieRun India. It runs the BGMI India Series and BGMI Pro Series, the game’s two main official tournaments.
The post BGMI Joins Google Play Arena: Free Registration, MS Dhoni’s Mahi Clutchers and a Mumbai LAN Finale appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Paper Rex’s something Reportedly Cleared as a Pacific Resident, Freeing an Import Slot
items.content:
Paper Rex may have found the roster loophole every VCT Pacific team wanted. Riot Games has granted Ilia “something” Petrov an exception that lets him count as a Pacific resident in 2027, according to a report by Lion Esports on 16 November. The Russian duelist joined the Singapore club from Japan’s Sengoku Gaming in March 2023. If that holds, something would no longer take up one of Paper Rex’s two import slots, and the club could add a foreign player without breaking up its core. Riot and Paper Rex have not confirmed the ruling, although the club’s X account did little to cool the speculation the next morning.
Robert Pattinson to play under PRX for VCT 2027 pic.twitter.com/p19yPGsqWu
— Paper Rex (@pprxteam) November 17, 2026
Paper Rex’s post on X the morning after the report.
Lion Esports, citing sources close to the matter, said the decision also covers other long-serving Russian players in the region, naming Maksim “Jemkin” Batorov. It added that Riot had not said publicly what threshold it used, whether that was years of residency, years under contract in Asia or a case-by-case review. That gap matters, because the 2027 rules give Riot wide discretion here, and the timing comes weeks after Paper Rex lost Jinggg and d4v41.
What Riot’s 2027 rulebook actually allows
The answer sits in Riot’s VCT Global Policies for 2027, last updated on 28 September. Article 96 says a player can count as a resident of a region if they are a citizen, a lawful permanent resident or hold another special status such as refugee status. The fourth route is the one that matters here, because it covers a player who “was granted an exception to be considered a Resident”, which Riot may accept or reject at its discretion. There is no fixed number of years in the rulebook, so a case like something’s depends entirely on Riot’s judgement.
Article 108 then sets the hard limit on imports. Every team must field at least three residents of its home region in its starting five, which means a maximum of two non-residents. Articles 109 to 112 add a softer route for teams that kept their partnership, such as Paper Rex. These legacy exceptions let a starting lineup carry more than two non-residents, but only if every one of those players holds an exception, and each one ends when that player’s contract with the club expires.
That is why a residency exception is worth far more than a legacy one. A legacy exception protects a player only for the length of his deal and only alongside other protected players. A residency exception, if Riot has granted it, removes something from the import count altogether, so Paper Rex could sign two new non-residents around him instead of none.
Why it matters for Paper Rex’s 2027 roster
Paper Rex needs that room more than most. The club kept its seat among the VCT partner teams for 2027 and 2028, but its 2026 core is already breaking up. Jinggg and d4v41 left on 31 October, and reports since then say f0rsakeN and something will stay while PatMen returns after a season with Global Esports. As we noted after Paper Rex’s exit from Champions Shanghai, most of that roster was out of contract at the end of 2026.
Riot’s new regional map for 2027 adds another layer to this. As our guide to the VCT 2027 format set out, Thailand, Indonesia and Vietnam become their own regions in 2027, while Singapore, Malaysia and the Philippines sit in a Wild Card bracket. Riot assigns each partner team its home region and has not published Paper Rex’s, but if the club is treated as a Wild Card side, Indonesian players like f0rsakeN would also count against the limit. In that case, freeing something’s slot is the difference between keeping f0rsakeN and signing one outside star, or having to choose between them.
Fans have already started naming possible targets for that slot. Thai duelist Primmie is the name mentioned most often in community discussion, although no team or player has confirmed any talks and the club has not commented. Under the 2027 map, a Thai player would count as a non-resident for a Wild Card team, so a lineup with something as a resident could still fit a Thai signing alongside f0rsakeN.
The fairness question for the rest of VCT Pacific
Not everyone is cheering the reported decision, however. Because Article 96 gives Riot full discretion, rival teams have no published standard to measure it against. Some fans have also asked why Russian players should qualify while others from South Asia or Oceania face the import limit. Teams in those markets already reach the global stage mainly through the Wild Card bracket and the Pacific Last Chance Qualifier, so every import slot they spend weighs heavily.
There is also a precedent question for Riot to answer. If long-serving players can earn residency through tenure, other clubs will want the same treatment for their own veterans, and Riot will need to apply it consistently. Riot’s rulebook already allows similar exceptions elsewhere, including Article 113, which treats recent Game Changers players as residents for VCT purposes regardless of nationality.
As things stand, the ruling exists only in Lion Esports’ report and in a joke post from Paper Rex. Partner teams are expected to register compliant rosters before VCT 2027 Kickoff in January, so the first official Paper Rex lineup should show whether something is registered as a resident. Fans can follow every move in our VCT 2027 transfer tracker, while results from the last season are on the TalkEsport wiki.
The post Paper Rex’s something Reportedly Cleared as a Pacific Resident, Freeing an Import Slot appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Microsoft’s 24-Hour Outage Cost Customers About $9 Billion. Microsoft Pays a Fraction
items.content:
For almost 24 hours last week, much of the working world could not open its email. Microsoft’s preliminary incident report puts the Microsoft 365 outage at 23 hours and 50 minutes, from 16:20 UTC on 12 November to 16:10 UTC the next day, with Outlook and Exchange Online hit hardest. By TalkEsport’s estimate, it cost Microsoft’s customers around the world about $9 billion in lost working time, within a plausible range of $2 billion to $27 billion. Microsoft’s own maximum exposure, through the service credits it promises when it misses its uptime target, is less than a billion dollars, and its share price rose on both days of the outage.
That gap is the real story of the outage. The failure was Microsoft’s, the evidence in its own report suggests it was preventable, and yet nearly all of the cost landed on the companies, hospitals, schools and governments that pay for Microsoft 365. We built a simple model to put a number on it, and every step is shown below so readers can swap in any assumption they disagree with.
What Microsoft’s own report says went wrong
Microsoft has been unusually candid about the cause. Its preliminary post-incident report, dated 15 November and shared with administrators under incident IDs EX1550543 and MO1550821, describes a fix it built for the networking gateway that sits in front of many Microsoft 365 services. That fix carried a hidden defect, and it went live across the world from July onwards. For more than three months, it ran without causing any visible problem.
The incident summary in Microsoft's preliminary post-incident report. Screenshot: Microsoft
The defect was lock contention inside an internal Windows process, which meant tasks on the gateway servers waited on each other until processor time and memory ran out. Microsoft’s report admits that its load tests “tended to focus on weaker hardware with fewer cores”, while the bug got worse on newer machines with more cores. On 12 November, a routine Teams failover added load to the same gateway, nearly 14% of its capacity was already offline for an unrelated reason, and US peak traffic did the rest. As we reported while Outlook and Teams were still down, Microsoft spent most of the first night restarting servers that kept failing again.
Microsoft's own account of the root cause, including the testing gap. Screenshot: Microsoft
The report’s own words explain why this one lasted so long. Automated traffic management moved users to healthy servers, which then hit the same bug, and “at its lowest, more than 80% of servers were unresponsive”. Because the faulty change was months old, Microsoft said its “normal rollback, flighting, and feature flags were unable to quickly revert the change”. Engineers had to build a new update instead, and it did not reach the first servers until 07:20 UTC on 13 November, 15 hours after the outage began.
While we're working to mitigate impact, we've confirmed the issue may affect Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region, more information will be provided in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543.
— Microsoft 365 Status (@MSFT365Status) November 12, 2026
Microsoft 365 Status warned on 12 November that the problem could affect users in any region.
About 300 million lost working hours, by our count
The first question is how much of the working day the outage actually took, and that depends on where you were. Using the start time and the regional recovery times in Microsoft’s report, we measured how many hours of a 9am to 5pm day fell inside the outage in nine major business cities. Asia Pacific lost almost an entire day on 13 November, because the failure began overnight there and was only fixed by 11:00 UTC. San Francisco lost all of 12 November, New York and São Paulo lost about six hours, and London and Frankfurt escaped with a lost morning.
From there, the arithmetic is straightforward, even if the inputs are not. Microsoft said in January that Microsoft 365 had more than 450 million paid commercial seats, and it told investors in October that commercial seats were still growing. Not all of those seats are active at once, and Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive kept working for most users, so we assume only a share of seats were working and relying on Outlook. We also assume people lost only part of each hour, since many could still chat, open files and do work that did not need email.
Our central case lands at roughly 297 million lost working hours, which is the equivalent of almost 150,000 people losing an entire 2,000-hour working year. At a blended $30 an hour, that is about $8.9 billion. For comparison, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics puts the average employer cost of a private-sector worker at $46.89 an hour, which is why our high case reaches $26.6 billion. Our low case, which assumes only one hour in ten was really lost, still comes to $2.2 billion.
The only outside estimate we found sits close to the middle of that range. Anderson Economic Group, a Michigan consultancy, put the cost at about $7 billion, according to CNN, which described it as the firm’s high estimate. Its full method has not been published in the coverage we have seen, and it is not clear whether it covers the US alone, so the two figures are not directly comparable. Our estimate, by contrast, covers all 450 million paid seats worldwide. Even so, both land above the $5.4 billion that insurer Parametrix estimated the CrowdStrike outage cost Fortune 500 companies in July 2024, as Fortune reported at the time.
There are real limits to any model like this. Lost hours are not the same as lost output, because some email simply waits until the next day. On the other hand, the model leaves out costs that are harder to count, such as cancelled hospital procedures, delayed court filings, missed trades and the overtime IT teams spent fielding calls. Those costs fall unevenly, and for a small business that runs everything through Outlook, one lost day can matter far more than an average suggests.
Microsoft’s side of the ledger: capped credits and a rising stock
Microsoft’s direct bill is far smaller, and that is by design. Microsoft 365 services carry a 99.9% monthly uptime commitment, and Microsoft’s guide to its SLAs describes credits of 25% of the monthly fee below 99.9%, 50% below 99% and 100% below 95%. A tenant that lost Exchange Online for all 1,430 minutes would sit at about 96.7% uptime for November, inside the 50% band. Those credits only apply to the fee for the affected service, and administrators have to claim them.
That puts a hard ceiling on what Microsoft can owe. Exchange Online Plan 1 costs $4 per user per month, so a 50% credit is worth $2 a seat. Even if every one of 450 million seats claimed at that rate, the total would be about $0.9 billion. That is roughly 1.4% of the $63.9 billion that Microsoft Cloud brought in during the three months to September, according to Microsoft’s latest results. In practice, only a fraction of customers will file, so the real figure should be much lower.
Investors barely noticed any of this, as it turned out. Microsoft shares closed at $523.00 on 12 November, up 0.4% on the day the outage began, and edged up again to $523.88 on 13 November as engineers rolled out the fix. Measured against Microsoft Cloud’s revenue of about $29 million an hour, the outage lasted long enough to cover roughly $690 million of sales, but subscriptions kept billing throughout. Almost nothing about the incident touched Microsoft’s income statement.
That imbalance is what makes outages like this one hard to fix from the outside. The cloud concentrates risk in a few providers, from AWS’s US-EAST-1 failure on 15 November to Google Cloud’s outage in Europe last month, while contracts cap what those providers pay when it goes wrong. Microsoft says it has already added recovery capacity, new monitoring and guardrails against cascading traffic shifts. Its final report, with the full list of repair items, is due around 20 November in the Microsoft 365 admin centre.
The post Microsoft’s 24-Hour Outage Cost Customers About $9 Billion. Microsoft Pays a Fraction appeared first on TalkEsport.

US Breaks Silence on Megaspeed: Probe Began in 2024, Nvidia Cut It Off in June 2025
items.content:
The US government has broken its silence on Megaspeed, and its account puts Nvidia’s own role in a new light. In a rare joint statement dated 16 November, the Department of Commerce and the Department of Justice said they had been investigating the Singapore company since 2024. They also said Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its “no sell” list in June 2025, after Commerce investigators asked the chipmaker for records of its sales. The criminal case is now led by the Justice Department, and the two agencies promised to bring “the full extent of the law” against Megaspeed for any crimes it may have committed.
The agencies said they were speaking because of “inaccurate information circulating in public reporting”, although they did not say which reports they meant. Megaspeed is the cloud company whose former chief executive, Alice Huang, is at the centre of the scandal that ended Jensen Huang’s 33 years as Nvidia’s chief executive on 12 November. No charges against Megaspeed or Alice Huang have been announced, and Megaspeed has denied diverting Nvidia chips to China.
What the Commerce and Justice timeline says about Megaspeed
The statement sets out the clearest official timeline yet. According to the two departments, Commerce opened its investigation in 2024 “after identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring” of possible chip diversion. In May 2025, its investigators asked Nvidia for records of any direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed, and in June 2025 Nvidia added Megaspeed to its “no sell” list. That same month, agents from the Bureau of Industry and Security carried out an on-site end-use check at Megaspeed with Singaporean law enforcement officers. They also interviewed Alice Huang, whom the statement describes as the company’s chief executive.
The full joint statement from the Department of Commerce and the Department of Justice. Image: US Department of Commerce
An end-use check is one of the US government’s main tools for confirming that exported technology is where its buyer says it is, and is being used for the purpose declared. Doing one in person, alongside another country’s police, is a sign that investigators were already treating the case seriously by mid-2025. According to the statement, it was only “following this enforcement action” that the Justice Department took the lead in a criminal investigation, with Commerce’s export enforcement agents still working the case alongside federal prosecutors.
The statement also doubles as a defence of the government’s record. It credits Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whom Senator Tom Cotton had urged to investigate Megaspeed, and Attorney General Todd Blanche. It also says 17 defendants in six separate investigations have been charged under the Trump administration over alleged smuggling of semiconductors worth billions of dollars. Commerce adds that its export control penalties are now 18 times higher than under the Biden administration. One of those prosecutions is a Southern District of New York case against three people accused of diverting US AI technology to China.
The New York Times report the statement does not mention
The timing makes the target of the statement fairly clear. On 9 November, The New York Times reported that the Commerce investigation was handed to the Justice Department after Nvidia’s general counsel, Tim Teter, contacted investigators in August 2025. The Times said Teter told investigators that Jeffrey Kessler, the Commerce under secretary who oversees export controls, had given him permission to reach out. Some agents reportedly worried that the contact could taint the case, and the Times said Commerce paused its own work at the Justice Department’s request.
Commerce told the Times at the time that it had acted “strictly by the book”, and that Kessler did not direct investigators to share anything with Nvidia. The new statement goes further by tying the Justice Department’s lead role to the June 2025 enforcement action, which came before Teter’s reported email. It does not, however, mention Teter, Kessler or the August contact at all, and it gives no date for when the Justice Department took over. Readers are left with two accounts of the same handover, and only one of them names the people involved.
The statement is also silent on the biggest question in Washington. It does not say whether Nvidia, or any of its executives, is a subject of the investigation, and it does not mention Jensen Huang. That gap matters, because Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has demanded answers from Nvidia’s board and its outside counsel within 10 days, as we reported when he called for a “dramatic shakeup” at Nvidia. Nvidia’s board has its own independent investigation under way.
How the US account fits Singapore’s and Megaspeed’s own timelines
The US version lines up closely with what Singapore has already said. In its own statement, Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs said the Bureau of Industry and Security carried out a post-shipment check at Megaspeed on 24 June 2025 with Alice Huang present. Police interviewed her and impounded her passport that same day, as our report on Singapore’s re-entry ban explained. Singapore later concluded that she had given police information she knew to be inaccurate.
The “no sell” date matters for another reason. The Wall Street Journal has reported that Megaspeed arranged nearly $12 billion of advanced chips for Chinese companies between March 2024 and June 2025. We covered that report in our story on the export bills now moving through Congress. That window closes in the same month Nvidia stopped selling to Megaspeed, according to the US statement. Megaspeed, for its part, says Alice Huang left the company on 30 August 2025, as we reported when it launched an internal investigation.
The statement lands on the day Nvidia reports its third-quarter results, its first under interim chief executive Colette Kress. Megaspeed has said it conducts lawful business and has hired outside lawyers to review its conduct, while Beijing has rejected reports that Alice Huang worked for Chinese intelligence. The Justice Department has not said when, or whether, it will bring charges.
The post US Breaks Silence on Megaspeed: Probe Began in 2024, Nvidia Cut It Off in June 2025 appeared first on TalkEsport.

Watching on TV? YouTube Now Counts Everyone on the Sofa
items.content:
YouTube has changed what the view count under every video actually measures. According to a notice on YouTube’s Help Center page on content performance, public view counts on watch pages “incorporate co-views” from November 2026. YouTube defines co-views as an estimate of how many people are watching together on a TV screen. The change was flagged by the creator analytics company vidIQ on 16 November, and it means a single playback on a living room TV can now add more than one view to the public total.
YouTube's notice on its Help Center page about co-views. Screenshot: YouTube Help
The same notice repeats a rule YouTube introduced earlier this year, that views are counted “the moment a video starts to play” across Shorts, long-form videos and live streams. Put together, the two changes mean the number fans see under a video no longer needs anyone to keep watching, and no longer counts only the screens that played it. YouTube says none of this affects the YouTube Partner Program, because earnings remain based on engaged Shorts views and engaged watch hours, while eligibility still depends on qualified Shorts views and qualified watch hours.
How YouTube got here, and how co-views are calculated
The first step came in August, in a Help Community post titled “An update to how we count public views across YouTube”. From 24 August, the company said, a public view would count from the first frame in every format, extending the approach it had already used for Shorts since 2025. YouTube said the aim was a single, consistent measure of exposure that creators could take to brands and sponsors, instead of different rules for Shorts, long videos and streams.
The second step arrived a few weeks later as a private number. In a Creator Insider video published on 2 September, YouTube creator liaison Rene Ritchie introduced Views (Co-Viewed), a metric in the advanced mode of YouTube’s analytics that “estimates the total number of people watching on TVs”. He said that until then “every TV device playback was viewed as a single view”, and described the new figure as platform-backed, so creators could use it when negotiating brand deals. A household of three watching one video together counts as three co-viewed views.
November’s change moves that estimate out of the private dashboard and into the public counter. The Help Center now lists a Co-View Rate metric that shows how much co-viewing lifts a channel’s total, and it explains that dividing total views by that rate gives a “baseline” without co-views. Engaged views and unique viewers still exclude co-viewers, while watch time now includes time from co-views, and the standalone Views (Co-viewed) metric will stay in YouTube Insights advanced mode until May 2027.
How YouTube's Help Center now defines co-views and related metrics. Screenshot: YouTube Help
What YouTube has not explained is how it knows who is on the sofa. The Help Center only says co-views are estimated for shared viewing on TV screens, including the main YouTube app on TV and YouTube TV. YouTube has not published the model, its margin of error or any outside audit of it. Its notice also does not say whether co-views are added to older videos or only to views from November onwards.
Why YouTube wants TV credit, and why the numbers deserve caution
The business case for the change is not hard to see. YouTube took a record 15.8% of all US television viewing time in August, about twice Netflix’s 7.7%, according to Nielsen’s monthly Gauge. Ritchie has also said that viewers watch more than a billion hours of YouTube on TV screens every day. Television audiences have long been sold to advertisers as people rather than devices, so counting one view per TV left YouTube creators reporting smaller audiences than the rooms they were actually reaching.
The problem is that a counted number and an estimated number now sit inside the same figure. Anyone comparing a video uploaded this month with one from last year is no longer comparing like with like, and that matters for the records gaming fans love to track. A trailer’s 24-hour views, a music video milestone or an esports final’s VOD count from November onwards can include modelled viewers that older totals never had, which makes headline comparisons shakier than they look.
Brands paying for sponsored videos face a similar issue. A sponsor paying by public views is now paying partly for viewers YouTube has estimated rather than measured, using a method it has not disclosed. The cleaner figures, engaged views and unique viewers, still exclude co-viewers, but they sit inside a creator’s private dashboard, so a brand has to ask for screenshots and take them on trust. That is a step back from a public counter that anyone could check, even if YouTube’s estimate turns out to be accurate.
Gaming creators sit right in the middle of this. Long VODs, live streams and big events such as YouTube’s 24-hour GTA 6 launch livestream with Total Gaming and Payal Gaming are exactly the kind of content families and friends watch together on a television. That could lift their public totals noticeably, while their Partner Program earnings stay tied to engaged watch hours, so a bigger number on the page will not by itself mean a bigger payout.
Other platforms count differently again, which adds to the confusion. Netflix, for example, reports views as hours watched divided by running time, the figure behind our report on the GTA 6 Extended Look’s 31.1 million Netflix views. YouTube’s own Partner Program rules still require 1,000 subscribers plus either 4,000 qualified watch hours in 12 months or 10 million qualified Shorts views in 90 days. YouTube says the co-view change does not affect either threshold.
The post Watching on TV? YouTube Now Counts Everyone on the Sofa appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: PMGC 2026: Team Soul’s International Tournament History and Past Results
items.content:
Team Soul is set to represent India at the PMGC 2026 in Istanbul, Turkey, starting on 26 November. Notably, Team Soul is the only representative of India in this Global Championship. However, this is not the first time this organisation is playing on the international stage.
Team Soul has already played a total of five international events, including PMCO 2019, PMSC 2019 as Team Spark, PMCO Fall Split Global Finals 2019, PEC 2019, and PMWI 2022. Now the team will play their sixth event in Turkey.
In this article, we are going to cover Team Soul’s international tournament history and results.
From PMCO 2019 to PMGC 2026: Team Soul’s International Journey
Team Soul played four of their five international tournaments in 2019, with their most recent international appearance coming at the PUBG Mobile World Invitational (PMWI) in 2022.
Team Soul, featuring an iconic lineup of Mortal, Viper, Ronak, and Owais, played their first international tournament in 2019 at the PMCO Spring Split Global Finals. The tournament was played from 20 to 28 July in Berlin, Germany, where Team Soul finished in 12th place.
Team Soul played their second international tournament in the same year in the PUBG Mobile Star Challenge (PMSC), as Team Spark. The Team Soul roster paired with Indian YouTuber The RawKnee Games, and together they competed as Team SPARK in this tournament played on 7 and 8 September. The team finished in 13th place in the PMSC 2019.
Read More: SouL Goblin Gives Update on Team SouL’s PMGC 2026 Visa Status
The organisation’s third international appearance came the PUBG Mobile Club Open (PMCO) 2019 Fall Split Global Finals, played in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, Mobile Club Open (PMCO) 2019 Fall Split Global Finals played in Kuala Lumpur in Malaysia from 23 November to 1 December. This time, Regaltos and Clutchgod were added to Team Soul’s roster with Mortal and Viper. However, the result was below average this time too, as they finished 12th at the PMCO 2019 Fall Split Global Finals.
The fourth appearance was special for the team, as they participated in China’s prominent tournament, the Peacekeeper Elite Championship 2019, in Xi’an, China, on 28 and 29 December. This time, Clutchgod joined 8Bit, and Aman played in his place along with Mortal, Viper, and Regaltos. However, the result was still below average, as Team Soul finished in 12th place.
After this tournament, Team Soul had to wait for 2 years for their next international tournament. After winning the BMPS 2022, the team qualified for the PUBG Mobile World Invitational (PMWI) 2026 Main Event, which was played in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, from 11 to 13 August. This was one of Team Soul’s most iconic lineups, featuring Omega, Hector, Goblin, and Akshat. Among these four players, Goblin is the only one set to represent Team Soul at PMGC 2026, marking his second international appearance and the organisation’s sixth international tournament.
The expectations were so high for this lineup of Soul, but the results were still below average, as they finished 11th in the PMWI 2022 Main Event.
Now the team will play their sixth international tournament, the PUBG Mobile Global Championship (PMGC) 2026, from 26 November in Istanbul, Turkey.
The lineup, including IGL Nakul, Legit, Joker, Goblin, and Thunder, won the BMSD 2026 in Hyderabad and qualified for the Gauntlet stage of PMGC 2026. This marks the first international appearance for Nakul, Legit, Thunder, and Joker. However, Goblin already has international experience, having represented Team Soul at the PUBG Mobile World Invitational (PMWI) in 2022.

items.title: How Jensen Huang Turned a $97 Million Side Business Into a $5 Trillion Nvidia
items.content:
Nvidia reports its third-quarter results this week without Jensen Huang for the first time in its history, and the numbers will still be his. In the three months to January 2016, the company’s data centre business brought in $97 million, about 7% of quarterly revenue, according to Nvidia’s own filing. In the three months to July 2026, the same business brought in $89.0 billion out of $96.2 billion. Few chief executives have ever moved a company that far, and almost none did it by betting on a market that did not exist yet.
Huang stepped down on 12 November as president, chief executive and director, and the reasons have been covered in detail elsewhere on this site, including our explainer on the Megaspeed scandal. This piece leaves his private life to that coverage. Even Nvidia’s board, in the statement announcing his exit, thanked him for his “immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry”. The record behind that line is worth setting out on its own.
CUDA, the 20-year bet Wall Street did not ask for
Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, and its first chip, the NV1, nearly sank the company. He has often said Nvidia was “30 days from going out of business” in those early years, a line he kept repeating long after the danger had passed. The RIVA 128 saved it in 1997, and in 1999 the GeForce 256 arrived as what Nvidia marketed as the world’s first GPU. The company went public the same year, and for most of the following decade it was known as a maker of graphics cards for gamers.
The decision that defines his tenure came in 2006 with CUDA. It turned every GeForce card into a programmable parallel computer, which meant spending chip area, engineering time and money on a feature most buyers would never use. Ian Buck, who had built a similar system as a Stanford PhD student, led the work, but it was Huang who kept funding it. Moreover, he kept doing so through the 2008 financial crisis, when investors questioned why a graphics company was building tools for scientists.
The payoff arrived in 2012, when the AlexNet image-recognition model was trained on two GeForce GTX 580 cards and won the ImageNet competition by a wide margin. Researchers had CUDA on their desks already, so deep learning grew up on Nvidia hardware by default. At GTC in March, Huang opened one part of his keynote by noting that “this is the 20th anniversary of CUDA”. By then, millions of developers and thousands of applications were built on it, which is the software moat rivals such as AMD are still trying to cross.
Nvidia’s official highlights from Jensen Huang’s GTC 2026 keynote, where he marked 20 years of CUDA.
Gamers felt those bets too, although they rarely got the credit. The RTX 20 series in 2018 brought real-time ray tracing and DLSS, an AI upscaler that used the same Tensor Cores Nvidia had built for data centres. That loop, with data centre ideas feeding back into GeForce, is one reason PC gamers are watching the succession closely, as our look at the future of GeForce after Huang explains.
Mellanox and the jump from selling chips to building AI factories
By the middle of the last decade, Huang was arguing that the computer of the future was a whole data centre rather than a single box. Nvidia launched the DGX-1 in 2016, an AI supercomputer in one chassis, and the first unit went to a small research lab called OpenAI. A year later, the V100 introduced Tensor Cores, hardware built specifically for the maths behind neural networks. Each step pulled Nvidia further away from being a component supplier and closer to selling complete systems.
The missing piece was the network that ties those systems together. In March 2019, Nvidia agreed to buy Mellanox for $6.9 billion, and it completed the deal on 27 April 2020 at $125 a share, about $7.0 billion in total, according to its filing with the SEC. Mellanox brought InfiniBand, high-speed Ethernet and network cards, the plumbing that lets thousands of GPUs train one model together. Huang summed up the logic at GTC this year: the data centre had to become a single unit of computing, “so Mellanox joined NVIDIA”.
The deal now looks like one of the best acquisitions in the history of the chip industry. Nvidia no longer reports networking separately, but The Next Platform estimates it brought in about $17.5 billion in the quarter to July, roughly a fifth of data centre sales. That means a single quarter of networking revenue is now worth about two and a half times what Nvidia paid for Mellanox. Everything else Nvidia sells, now reported as Edge Computing, made $7.2 billion in the same period, according to Nvidia’s second-quarter results.
Not every one of Huang’s big bets landed, however. Nvidia agreed to buy Arm for $40 billion in September 2020, then abandoned the deal in February 2022 after regulators in the US, UK and EU pushed back. Huang’s response says a lot about how he ran the company. Instead of giving up on CPUs, Nvidia designed its own Arm-based Grace processor, which now sits beside its GPUs in the Grace Blackwell systems that power much of the AI boom.
How Huang’s Nvidia compares with the companies it overtook
The market value tells the story in blunter terms. Nvidia became the first chipmaker worth $1 trillion in 2023, then the first company of any kind to reach $4 trillion in July 2025 and $5 trillion on 29 October 2025. It overtook Apple and Microsoft, two companies that had led tech for decades, while selling a product most consumers never see. Even after the selloff that followed his exit, which our chart of the scandal’s cost tracks day by day, Nvidia remains one of the most valuable companies in the world.
Huang also stayed in charge far longer than most founders do. He ran Nvidia for 33 years, from a booth at a Denny’s restaurant to an AI empire, through the dot-com crash, the 2008 crisis, the crypto mining boom and bust, and the AI wave. Under him, Nvidia went from $5.01 billion of revenue in the whole of fiscal 2016 to $96.2 billion in a single quarter this year. He also ran it with an unusually flat structure, with around 60 direct reports and almost no one-to-one meetings, by his own account.
Colette Kress, who is serving as interim chief executive while the board searches for a permanent successor, has already described her job as “building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years”. The candidates being discussed, which we covered in our report on who could replace Huang, inherit a company whose biggest bets he placed years before anyone else saw them coming. The results Kress presents this week cover the three months to late October, the last full quarter that Huang ran.
The post How Jensen Huang Turned a $97 Million Side Business Into a $5 Trillion Nvidia appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: 30 Years Later, One of the Greatest ‘X-Files’ Episodes is Still a Misunderstood Masterpiece
items.content: For the first three seasons of The X-Files, the writers kept you guessing, not only with regard to the show’s greater mysteries about aliens, but also about its most intriguing character. The Cigarette Smoking Man, played by William B. Davis, begins the series as a shadowy, silent character in the first episode. He looks on as Agent Dana Scully (Gillian Anderson) is given her not-too-subtle orders to undermine Agent Fox Mulder (David Duchovny) and his work on the X-Files. He goes on to appear sparingly, just a few times each season, to stop Mulder and Scully from getting too close to the secrets he’s spent decades covering up.

In the group stage, all 16 teams will be divided into four groups of four teams each. Every team in each group will fight each other to get as many series victories as possible. items.title: Fortnite Server Status: Is Fortnite Down?
items.content:
Fortnite is currently online and operational with no known server or matchmaking issues reported, as of Nov. 16, 2026. This guide covers everything you need to know about Fortnite server issues, including how to troubleshoot the errors and track issues as they persist.
Is Fortnite down right now?
No, Fortnite is currently online and functioning normally. There are no reported outages as of Nov. 16, 2026. The best way to check is to visit the official Epic Games Public Status website. This resource lets you check not only the status of Fortnite, but many other Epic Games-related operations.
The most recent outage occurred as planned on Nov. 11 into 12 as Epic Games took the game offline for a scheduled update. This is typical, as Fortnite updates roll out regularly and require the servers to be offline.
When will Fortnite servers be back up?
🟢 Downtime's a wrap! Jump back in and see what's new:
BR: https://t.co/ME7nUoIsvm
Arenas: https://t.co/921zjNOOz9
— Fortnite Status (@FortniteStatus) November 12, 2026
More often than not, Fortnite servers being offline just means the game is undergoing scheduled maintenance or an incoming patch. In other cases, Fortnite is down because of an unseen issue.
While it doesn’t happen often, it can prevent players from accessing the game for a few minutes to several hours. This is usually due to an issue on Epic Games’ server side that may affect more than just Fortnite.
However, in the more common case of Fortnite updates or scheduled maintenance, Epic Games initiates downtime the night before the new update. The game will then remain inaccessible for up to 8 hours before they return online.
Epic normally informs players when downtime will begin, but rarely announces a specific end time. That is because updates come in all shapes and sizes, and some take longer or shorter than others.
Why are Fortnite servers not responding?
You may see the ‘Fortnite servers not responding’ error for one of two reasons. Either the game is completely offline, or it’s an issue on the player’s side, whether it’s network-related or something else. If it’s the latter, that’s where troubleshooting comes into play.
How to fix the Fortnite server offline or not responding error
(Image via Epic Games)
If you are encountering any of these issues, the first thing you can do is check the server status using one of the resources listed below.
Fortnite server resources
Epic Games status tracker – The most efficient and reliable resource to track Fortnite server status
@FortniteStatus on X – A social media account Fortnite uses to communicate issues, updates, and server situations with players.
Down Detector – Another resource similar to the Epic Games status tracker
Check with friends from Fortnite – Friends will help determine whether Fortnite server issues are affecting multiple people or just you.
Forums such as Reddit – Fortnite players typically congregate and report issues on the r/FortniteBR subreddit.
These are the places you will want to bookmark to check all kinds of Fortnite issues, including server-side problems.
How to fix a client-side connection issue to Fortnite
(Image via Epic Games)
In some cases, Fortnite server issues can be isolated to just your PC or a few select players. If you believe you are in this position, you can run through the following troubleshooting steps:
Restart Fortnite
Simply reboot the game to see if the error disappears.
Verify Game Files
You can do this via the Epic Games Client by clicking the three dots > Manage > Verify Files.
Reboot Router
Go to your internet router/modem and reboot it, then revisit Fortnite to see if you can connect.
Restart Console/PC
Reboot your console and/or PC and then load into Fortnite to confirm.
Check for Game Updates
Confirm whether your Fortnite is updated to the latest version. If it is not, then update it.
DNS/Network Issues
Open Command Prompt and run ipconfig /flushdns.
Firewall and Antivirus
Check any firewall/antivirus settings to see if Fortnite is blocked.
VPN Conflicts
Make sure you are not connected to a VPN, as this can cause issues and, in some cases, even a ban.
Common Fortnite server errors you might experience
Server not responding is one of the most common errors you will experience in Fortnite. However, there are many others you may encounter that can be confusing.
Here are some other common errors and what they usually mean:
ErrorWhat it meansWhat to do
Matchmaking errorUsually related to server issuesRestart your game and check server status resources
Unable to log inUsually a server issue, or it can sometimes indicate you logged into Fortnite on another platformRestart your game and check server status resources
Network connection lostUsually a server issue that can occur while you’re playingRestart your game and check your network connection if the restart doesn’t help
Waiting in queueFortnite servers are experiencing high trafficWait until you load into the lobby
If it’s a Fortnite server issue, you’ll have to wait and check social media and status trackers until servers are back online.
FAQ
Is Fortnite down right now?
No, Fortnite is currently online and operational. There are no known server outages.
When will Fortnite servers be back online?
Fortnite servers are currently online. If they are not, you can track that information using the Epic Games Public Status website.
Why are Fortnite servers not responding?
Either because of an unplanned outage or planned maintenance. It’s normally planned maintenance, but unplanned outages can occur.
How long does Fortnite maintenance usually last?
If it’s planned, it normally lasts anywhere between 5 and 8 hours before an update goes live.
Why is Fortnite not working when servers are online?
Fortnite is exclusively an online game, so it’s impossible to play the game offline.
Is Fortnite down on PS5, Xbox, Switch, or PC?
If Fortnite is offline, it would affect all platforms. However, there are cases where one platform may encounter issues. Currently, Fortnite is operational on all platforms.

items.title: NVIDIA DGX Spark Developer Kit Turns a Desk Into a Supercomputing Lab
items.content:
At SC26, an annual supercomputing conference taking place this week in Chicago, NVIDIA is introducing the DGX Spark HPC Developer Kit for researchers, academics and developers.
The kit is a four-node cluster of NVIDIA DGX Spark systems, each connected directly to its two neighbors in a ring, with an NVIDIA HPC SDK installation playbook coming soon. Researchers get a place at their desk to run multi-node scientific workloads, AI models and agents, instead of waiting for time on a shared GPU cluster. The kit puts the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip on researchers’ desks.
A Supercomputing Lab on Any Desk
The DGX Spark Developer Kit changes how researchers work.
Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26
It scales from one system, or node, to four — linked directly to one another over NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking, with no network switch to buy or set up.
At four nodes, it provides 512GB of combined memory and 20TB of NVMe storage that provides researchers more capacity to distribute models and scientific workloads across the cluster. With NVFP4, researchers can deploy models with up to 700B parameters locally across the four DGX Spark clusters, such as DeepSeek V4.1.
With that much power at the desk, researchers with a fixed compute and server allocation no longer have to wait in a queue for every job. Teams can develop and debug on their own, saving server hours for production runs and keeping unpublished results, and proprietary datasets on premises.
The playbook for NVIDIA HPC SDK is coming soon, bringing GPU-accelerated C, C++ and Fortran compilers, libraries and message passing interface tools to the DGX Spark cluster — the same development tools used on NVIDIA-powered supercomputers. Teams can build and test scientific applications across four nodes, check how computation and data are distributed, and debug communication issues before scaling to larger systems.
The kit brings scientific simulation and AI models and agents to the desktop, with demonstrated four-system workloads including LAMMPS with Kokkos for materials simulation and NAMD for molecular dynamics. The broader DGX Spark community has validated GROMACS for molecular dynamics, OpenFOAM for fluid dynamics, WRF for weather modeling and NVIDIA NIM microservices such as OpenFold3 and Boltz-2 for predicting biomolecular structures.
Running on DGX Spark, new open dataset and post-training recipes for Nemotron 3.5 Super VL help researchers adapt the model for life sciences and chemistry, enabling secure scientific workflows on infrastructure organizations control.
What Researchers Can Do With It
The kit opens up new possibilities for researchers.
Researchers can explore agent-assisted workflows that prepare simulation inputs, launch runs and summarize results, while the scientists validate the setup and conclusions.
Researchers can also train AI models that approximate slow simulations, then use them to refine wing designs toward minimum drag.
Before committing supercomputer time, a team can narrow a 10-million-cell simulation to the 50-500 dimensions that matter.
Kvantify is using NVIDIA cuQuantum, and reports running tensor-network simulations of quantum-chemistry circuits with up to 70 qubits and 975 gates on a single DGX Spark, benchmarking circuits generated for penicillin ground-state energy calculations.
CYRAN AI, an IIT Delhi spin-out, uses DGX Spark and its PixelFlux library to accelerate JPEG 2000 decoding for large satellite images, supporting local geospatial analysis.
OpenFold shows how researchers can fine-tune OpenFold3 on NVIDIA DGX Spark to improve protein-ligand structure predictions for drug discovery.
The Rubin Lab at IGI at University of California, Berkeley is using a DGX Spark and NVIDIA Evo 2 model to predict bacterial traits directly from genome sequences by comparing embeddings from genomic and protein language models against the classical baselines. With no 11-hour cluster queue times, results arrived 15x sooner on DGX Spark.
The Hartwig Group at UC Berkeley is using a DGX Spark to perform LoRA fine-tuning on the Nemotron 3 Super 120B-A12B model for chemistry machine learning, training a prediction head on experimental values. By running locally on the Spark using NVFP4 quantization, the lab successfully fit a 120B-class model on a single device and bypassed multi-day cluster queue times, allowing them to run continuous eight- to 24-hour training fits back-to-back.
Where to Find the Kit
The developer kit is on display at SC26 and available for sale. DGX Spark products and cables can be purchased from top OEM partners and are also available through NVIDIA Marketplace.
Partners include Acer, ASUS, Dell Technologies, GIGABYTE, H3C, HP, Lenovo, MSI and xFusion.
An NVIDIA playbook for building and running the NVIDIA HPC SDK, a software development kit for scientific computing, is coming soon. Once available, it will give scientists and researchers a local platform to develop multi-node GPU applications, explore FP32 and mixed-precision algorithms and run molecular dynamics and materials simulations using LAMMPS with Kokkos before scaling to data center systems.
Learn more about NVIDIA DGX Spark.
