items.title: KRAFTON Hires Samsung’s Former Legal Chief and a Top Finance Ministry Official
items.content:
KRAFTON, the South Korean publisher behind PUBG: Battlegrounds and BGMI, has hired a former senior finance ministry official and a former head of legal at Samsung Electronics. Ahn Sang-yeol, who ran fiscal management at the Ministry of Economy and Finance until 2025, joins as a policy adviser. Kim Jae-hoon, who led Samsung Electronics’ legal team as an executive vice president, becomes KRAFTON’s Head of Legal Affairs and External Relations. The appointments were reported by Korean games outlet Inven on 16 November.
Both men join as unregistered executives, which in Korea means they hold executive titles but do not sit on the company’s board. Ahn’s role is part-time and advisory, while Kim’s is full-time. TalkEsport found no announcement of the hires in KRAFTON’s own newsroom, and neither man has commented publicly. The timing stands out, though, because KRAFTON has spent much of 2026 dealing with legal fights and, more recently, a sharp drop in profit.
Who Ahn Sang-yeol and Kim Jae-hoon are
Ahn is a career economic official who passed the 39th Higher Civil Service Examination. According to Inven, he worked in the presidential secretariat for science and technology in 2013 and directed the finance ministry’s fiscal management division from 2016 to 2018. He was seconded to the National Assembly’s Strategy and Finance Committee in 2019, and he served as the ministry’s fiscal management officer, a Grade 1 post, in 2024 and 2025. The ministry has since become the Ministry of Finance and Economy.
Kim brings about 14 years of senior legal work inside two Samsung companies. He studied law at Seoul National University, where he earned a bachelor’s and a master’s degree, and later took an LL.M. at Georgetown University. At Samsung Electronics, he rose from vice president of legal and compliance in 2012 to executive vice president of legal affairs by 2021. From 2022 until this year he was executive vice president of legal and contracts at Samsung E&A, the group’s engineering and construction arm.
KRAFTON has already tied part of Kim’s pay to its share price. Inven reported that the company granted him 800 restricted stock units on 28 September. Restricted stock units only turn into shares once set conditions are met, usually after a period of service, so the grant gives Kim a reason to stay.
Why KRAFTON needs a stronger legal team in 2026
KRAFTON’s biggest legal problem this year came from Delaware. In March, the Court of Chancery ruled that KRAFTON breached its acquisition agreement with Unknown Worlds by firing the Subnautica 2 studio’s leaders without cause, and it reinstated CEO Ted Gill. The case drew global attention because the ruling described how KRAFTON’s chief executive, Changhan Kim, used ChatGPT while looking for a way out of a $250 million earnout. Our breakdown of the Delaware ruling covers how that plan fell apart.
KRAFTON settled that dispute in July, according to Bloomberg, agreeing to pay bonuses to Unknown Worlds staff while Gill stepped down by mutual agreement. The company has also faced regulators at home before. In 2024, South Korea’s Fair Trade Commission carried out an on-site investigation into KRAFTON over loot box probabilities in PUBG.
The legal role also covers external relations, which suggests Kim will deal with governments and partners as well as lawsuits. That matters for a company now operating far beyond Korea. KRAFTON runs BGMI through KRAFTON India, which is betting on Bengaluru for its next global hit, and it recently registered a holding company in Brazil.
The hires follow a weak third quarter for KRAFTON
The appointments land a week after KRAFTON reported its third-quarter results on 10 November. Revenue rose 11.6% from a year earlier to ₩971.4 billion, but operating profit fell 35.5% to ₩225.0 billion. Currency losses pushed the company to a net loss of ₩68.4 billion, as our report on KRAFTON’s Q3 2026 results set out.
The company is also spending heavily on new areas. It now consolidates ADK, the Japanese advertising and content group it bought, and it has been building its own AI models alongside its games. A former fiscal official could help KRAFTON read Korea’s policy direction as it grows, although the company has not explained what Ahn will advise on.
Inven’s reporter saw the two hires as a sign that KRAFTON is reworking its policy and legal operations together. Neither role has been linked publicly to a specific case or regulator, and KRAFTON has not said when either man started. The company reported record revenue of ₩3.3266 trillion for 2025, and its nine-month revenue for 2026 already stands at ₩3.6 trillion.
The post KRAFTON Hires Samsung’s Former Legal Chief and a Top Finance Ministry Official appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: GTA 6 Hacker Arion Kurtaj Pleads Guilty Three Days Before the Game Launches
items.content:
Arion Kurtaj, the Lapsus$ hacker who leaked early footage of Grand Theft Auto VI in 2022, has pleaded guilty to all the charges against him, three days before the game launches. The 21-year-old from Oxford entered his pleas at Woolwich Crown Court on Monday, 16 November, BBC News reported. They cover the Rockstar Games hack and a string of other offences he committed at 16 and 17 as part of the Lapsus$ group. He will be sentenced at a later date.
The pleas turn a long, unusual case into a criminal conviction for the first time. In 2023, Kurtaj was found unfit to stand trial and was sent to a secure hospital with no release date. Doctors later judged him fit, and he was moved to an ordinary prison in January, according to the BBC. Last month, we reported that he was expected to face a full criminal trial in November, and his guilty pleas mean a trial is no longer needed.
What Arion Kurtaj admitted at Woolwich Crown Court
Kurtaj pleaded guilty to all counts, standing to confirm his name and showing no visible emotion, according to the BBC. The pleas include the 2022 attack on Rockstar, carried out while he was on bail for earlier hacks and staying in a Travelodge in Bicester under police protection. With his laptop confiscated, he used an Amazon Fire Stick, a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse and the hotel television to get into the studio’s internal Slack.
From there, he stole 90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 gameplay and tried to blackmail the company. “If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code,” he wrote. When Rockstar refused, he posted the clips and source code on a forum under the name TeaPotUberHacker. Rockstar said the breach cost $5 million (about £3.79 million) to recover from, along with thousands of staff hours.
He also admitted offences from the wider Lapsus$ spree, which hit BT and EE, Revolut and Uber, causing an estimated £10 million in damage, the BBC reported. Prosecutors described him as a “leading light” of the group and argued that it used stolen data to target cryptocurrency investors, taking at least $300,000 from individuals. Kurtaj also pleaded guilty to assaulting prison staff, including several biting incidents.
From a secure hospital order to guilty pleas
Kurtaj’s first case in 2023 never ended in a conviction. Psychiatrists said his autism meant he could not take part in a normal trial. Instead, a jury at Southwark Crown Court only decided whether he had carried out the acts, and in August 2023 it found that he had. In December 2023, a judge ordered that he be detained in a secure hospital indefinitely, until doctors decided he was no longer a danger.
The law has a route back to court when someone in that position recovers. Under section 5A of the Criminal Procedure (Insanity) Act 1964, the Secretary of State can send a person on a restricted hospital order back to court or to prison once they can properly be tried. That decision follows advice from their clinician, and the hospital order ends as soon as they arrive. Reports have not confirmed exactly which order Kurtaj was under, but the BBC said a routine assessment late last year found him fit, which led to his move to prison in January.
His time in custody has not been quiet either. He was caught with a mobile phone in prison after sending a taunting text to police and posting updates on Snapchat, the BBC reported. In March, screenshots shared online appeared to show him hinting that GTA 6’s source code might already be circulating, a claim that has never been backed up.
The other Lapsus$ teenager is already in prison
Kurtaj was tried in 2023 alongside a 17-year-old Lapsus$ member, who was given an 18-month youth rehabilitation order and banned from using VPNs. That teenager has since been named as Thalha Jubair, according to the BBC. In July, Jubair and Owen Flowers were each jailed for five years and six months for Scattered Spider attacks. One of those attacks hit Transport for London and left it with £29 million in losses and recovery costs, according to the National Crime Agency.
In 2023, the jury found that Kurtaj had committed 12 offences, including unauthorised access to computers under the Computer Misuse Act 1990, blackmail and fraud. The BBC did not list the individual counts he admitted on Monday, and it said only that he will be sentenced at a later date. The game he leaked arrives on Thursday, more than four years after his footage first spread online, at the times in our GTA 6 release time guide.
The 2022 leak also exposed one of Rockstar’s best-kept secrets. The clips showed that GTA 6 would have a playable female character, a detail the studio had been saving for its own marketing, according to the BBC. Rockstar later introduced her as Lucia, and the official Grand Theft Auto VI site lists the game’s launch on 19 November for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
The post GTA 6 Hacker Arion Kurtaj Pleads Guilty Three Days Before the Game Launches appeared first on TalkEsport.

Revenant XSpark Signs World Junior Chess Champion Pranav Venkatesh
items.content:
Revenant XSpark (RNTX) has signed Indian grandmaster Pranav Venkatesh, the 2025 World Junior Chess Champion, as its first chess player. The 20-year-old, who competes as Pranav V, joins an organisation that already fields teams in BGMI, Valorant and EA Sports FC. RNTX has not disclosed the length or terms of the deal. The organisation has not said which online chess events he will play under its name.
The signing makes RNTX the second Indian esports organisation to add a chess grandmaster this month. Team Apex Gaming signed Vidit Gujrathi on 9 November, making him its first chess player. GodLike Esports posted a chess teaser of its own, quoting verses from the Bhagavad Gita that point towards grandmaster Arjun Erigaisi, although the organisation has not named a player.
View this post on Instagram
A post shared by Revenant XSpark (@revenantesports.gg)
Pranav Venkatesh won the World Junior Championship in 2025
Pranav won the FIDE World Junior Championship in Petrovac, Montenegro, in March 2025. He finished unbeaten on 9/11 with a performance rating of 2721, ahead of 156 other players. The title ended a 17-year wait for India, after Abhijeet Gupta won it in 2008. Viswanathan Anand in 1987 and Pentala Harikrishna in 2004 are among the other Indian winners.
Pranav Venkatesh won the 2025 FIDE World Junior Championship in Petrovac
The win gave Pranav three world age-group titles at the same time. He had won the World Youth Under-18 rapid and blitz titles in December 2024. A month earlier he won the Challengers section of the Chennai Grand Masters, which earned him a place in the 2025 Masters event.
Pranav V’s grandmaster title and rating
Pranav became India’s 75th grandmaster in August 2022, at the age of 15. He was born in Bengaluru on 13 October 2006 and grew up in Chennai, where he attended Velammal Vidyalaya. He trains under the WestBridge Anand Chess Academy, Viswanathan Anand’s mentorship programme, with Shyam Sundar M as his coach.
He reached a career-high classical rating of 2670 this year. Since the World Junior title, he has won the Fujairah Global Chess 2025 Superstars event, the Salamanca Masters in 2025 and the KazChess Masters Nauryz in 2026. His online results include a last-round win over Magnus Carlsen in a Chess.com Titled Tuesday in March 2023.
RNTX has added players across several titles in recent weeks. The organisation signed EA Sports FC player Vanshaj Sharma on 4 November, and he went on to win Red Bull Wings Cup India on 15 November. It also announced a new Valorant roster led by Aman “Hoax” Yadav on 12 November. Pranav’s FIDE profile lists him under the Indian federation, where he holds the title of grandmaster.

items.title: nobody and CHICHOO leave EDward Gaming, ending Champions-winning core before Hangzhou
items.content:
A month after Global Esports handed out a beating to EDward Gaming at VALORANT Champions 2026, captain Wang "nobody" Senxu and controller Wan "CHICHOO" Shunzhi have left the Chinese org. Their exits (which were confirmed on Webo) bring to an end a triumphant five years, during which the group won VALORANT Champions 2024 and cemented their position as the most decorated Chinese org ever.
For a VCT China partner team, losing three starters in a week with the January Kickoff approaching is a heavy rebuild, although rumors suggest Daniel "Rossy" Abedrabbo is set to sign. No official replacements, though, have been named.
What EDG are losing
🇨🇳 CHICHOO officially concludes his time with 🇨🇳 EDward Gaming
He joined EDG way back in 2021 and qualified to 12 international tournaments before his departure.
CHICHOO’s tenure with EDG was highlighted by lifting VCT CN’s first ever international trophy at Champions Seoul.
— VALO2ASIA (@VALO2ASIA) November 14, 2026
nobody joined EDG on Sept. 7, 2021, beginning as an initiator before taking over in-game leading duties. Eventually, he was trusted with the captaincy. CHICHOO played controller beside him.
Together, they anchored the roster that beat the field on Aug. 25, 2024, making EDG the first organization from China, and from Asia, to lift the Champions trophy. EDG's total winnings sit at $1,592,287.
Both players were still central this year. At Masters London, each played 12 maps, with CHICHOO averaging a 179 average combat score and nobody a 184. However, in a post-match interview after the org’s defeat to Global Esports last month, CHICHOO seemed highly critical, pinpointing the collapse to a lack of communication. Now, just weeks later, he has left the org, though there is no suggestion of a link between the defeat, the reaction and the controller’s exit.
Masters London 2026Result
EDG finishThird place
Prize money$125,000
Final series0-3 loss to Leviatán, lower bracket final, June 20
Where nobody goes next
Reports say that nobody is expected to join Trace Esports for the 2027 VCT China season, and that CHICHOO may join him. Trace's Kai and deLb are said to be under contract through the end of 2027. If the move happens, nobody and Smoggy would open the new season on different rosters.
The rebuild clock
EDG were named a VCT partner team on Oct. 21, on a two-year contract. That deal now starts with a heavily changed roster. ZmjjKK, Jieni7, and stew are among the players still on the team, although the rumor mill is also linking with a move elsewhere. If true, EDward Gaming’s rebuild will be even heavier.
The China Kickoff in Hangzhou is an S-Tier LAN run by TJ Sports, Hero Esports, and Riot Games. Eight of the 12 slots go to partner teams. The other four are split evenly between visiting teams and open qualifier entrants.
Smoggy's new team, Bilibili Gaming, is one of the sides EDG will have to face in a domestic field that is reshuffling fast.
Writer's take
Losing a captain who has led the same group for five years is harder than replacing a single slot. Whoever steps into the in-game leader role will need quick chemistry with whatever players EDG sign, and it’ll be interesting to see if the Chinese org can continue their run of success.
Their first test with a new roster will be the Kickoff in Hangzhou in January, followed by Cup 1 in Wuhan from April 29 to May 23 and Cup 2 in Shanghai from Aug. 5 to 29. Nobody and CHICHOO’s reported moves to Trace Esports remains unconfirmed until either side makes it official. If they do, Trace Esports could be a team to watch next year.

Bose Recalls 670,000 S1 Pro Speaker Batteries That Can Catch Fire
items.content:
Bose is recalling about 670,000 battery packs for its S1 Pro and S1 Pro+ portable speakers in the United States and Canada, because they can overheat and catch fire. The US Consumer Product Safety Commission announced the recall on 5 November, covering about 634,759 packs sold in the US. Health Canada’s notice adds 35,399 more sold in Canada. Bose has received seven reports of packs melting, smoking or catching fire, six of which involved property damage, and no injuries have been reported.
Owners are being told to stop using the affected packs straight away and to claim a free replacement from Bose. The packs are the removable lithium-ion batteries that let the S1 Pro and S1 Pro+ run without a wall socket. They were sold both inside the speakers and on their own as accessories or replacement parts, so a speaker bought years ago can still hold a recalled pack.
Which Bose S1 Pro and S1 Pro+ battery packs are recalled
According to the CPSC, the recalled packs were sold from December 2017 to July 2026 at Bose, Best Buy and other shops, and online at Amazon, Bose.com, BestBuy.com and Walmart.com. They cost between $100 and $160 on their own, while a speaker system with a pack included sold for about $700. In Canada, Health Canada says S1 Pro packs were sold from April 2020 to May 2024 and S1 Pro+ packs from June 2025 to July 2026.
A pack is affected if the first six digits of its 17-digit serial number match one of seven prefixes. The serial number is printed on a label on the bottom of the battery pack, just below the barcode. Here are the prefixes listed by Bose and the CPSC.
To check a pack that is fitted in a speaker, Bose’s recall page says to switch the speaker off and unplug it first. Then loosen the two screws on the bottom, take off the bottom plate and pull the battery out using its tabs. Bose also notes that some S1 Pro systems were sold without a battery, so owners who added one later should check that pack as well.
Why Bose says the packs can overheat and ignite
The CPSC notice says simply that the battery packs “can overheat and ignite”, which poses a risk of fire and burns. Health Canada gives a little more detail about the cause. It says that continued use as the packs age “exposes the lithium-ion cells to potentially damaging operating conditions”, creating “potential fire and burn hazards”.
None of the seven incidents happened in Canada, according to Health Canada, which counted them as of 5 October. The packs were made in China by TWS Technology (Guangzhou) Ltd, and Bose Corporation of Framingham, Massachusetts, imported them. The CPSC handled the case as a Fast Track recall, which is the regulator’s process for companies that move quickly to fix a product problem.
How to get a free replacement battery from Bose
Bose says owners should remove an affected pack from the speaker and stop using it immediately. The speaker itself is not part of the recall, and it can still be used without the battery while it is plugged into mains power. To claim a replacement, owners enter the pack’s serial number on Bose’s recall page, which works for packs that are fitted in a speaker as well as spare ones.
In the US, Bose takes calls on 800-278-1083 from 9am to 9pm ET on weekdays and from 9am to 7pm ET on Saturdays. Canadian owners can call 1-800-869-2114 during the same hours, and Health Canada asks people to report any incident involving the packs. US owners who have trouble getting a replacement can use the CPSC’s recall complaint form. Bose’s page also says online requests are not available in every region, so owners elsewhere, including India, should contact Bose support directly.
Getting rid of the old pack needs some care, because recalled lithium-ion batteries carry a higher fire risk. The CPSC says they should not go in household rubbish, kerbside recycling or the battery collection boxes found in shops. Instead, owners should call their local household hazardous waste centre first to check whether it accepts recalled lithium-ion batteries.
The same battery chemistry sits inside most of the gadgets gamers carry every day, from phones to controllers, and heat is bad for all of them. Our guides on what actually lowers a phone’s temperature and reducing battery drain while gaming cover the basics, and our hardware section will follow the recall. The CPSC lists it as recall number 27-065, and it covers battery packs sold from December 2017 to July 2026.

LEC in 2027 will have no best-of-ones, only Bo3s and Bo5s
items.content:
The League of Legends EMEA Championship (LEC) is making some changes in 2027, including complete abolition of best-of-ones from the domestic league. All three LEC 2027 splits will only be comprised of best-of-threes and best-of-fives, while familiar mechanics like Fearless Draft and First Selection will return.
LEC 2027: Three splits, more Roadtrips
LEC 2027 will once again have three splits: Winter, Spring, and Summer.
LEC Winter 2027 begins Jan. 15. The top teams from this split will compete in First Stand: All In, although the exact number of teams to qualify are still currently unconfirmed.
Image credit: LEC
Unlike in 2026 where the Winter split had a different format than the rest of the year, all three LEC 2027 splits will have the same format:
Regular Season – 10-team single round robin, best-of-three matches.
Playoffs – Six-team, best-of-five Playoffs bracket.
All matches will feature Fearless Draft and First Selection mechanics, as is the current standard for professional League of Legends play.
“By keeping the focus on longer series, we’re giving teams more opportunities to adapt, develop strategies, and demonstrate their strengths over the course of a match,” outlined the LEC in a press release sent to esports.gg. “The format also provides a competitive environment that more closely mirrors international play, helping teams prepare for the challenges ahead.”
Fans can expect a slight shake-up to the calendar, with more details to be shared as Winter 2027 approaches.
Roadtrips
In 2026, the LEC partnered with MKOI and Karmine Corp to bring LEC matches to Berlin, Barcelona, Madrid, Evry, Paris, and Nice across five roadtrips.
Image credit: LEC
For 2027, the league is looking to scale up and partner with more teams in the third consecutive year of Roadtrips. “We’re excited to build on the momentum, discover new destinations, and create more opportunities for fans to experience the action together.”
The LEC 2027 season begins with the Winter split on Jan. 15, 2027.

The Atlas P7 features four-sided tempered glass panels and a panoramic layout, making full use of its floating chassis design while giving builders an unobstructed view of their hardware. GAMDIAS has also added a dedicated display platform and spotlight within the chassis, allowing builders to showcase figures and collectibles alongside their components. The tool-free side panel can be removed for easier access when changing hardware or rearranging displays.
Three 120mm NOTUS M1 PWM ARGB fans come pre-installed, alongside an 8-port PWM/ARGB fan hub. The Atlas P7 uses a chimney-style cooling layout, drawing cool air in through the bottom of the chassis and exhausting heat through the top. The Atlas P7 also supports radiators up to 360mm in size at the top of the case.
The chassis supports Mini-ITX, Micro-ATX and ATX motherboards, graphics cards up to 425mm long, CPU coolers up to 165mm tall and power supplies up to 200mm in length. Up front, you'll find a USB 3.2 Gen 2×2 Type-C port, two USB 3.0 ports, HD audio and dedicated controls for RGB lighting and the integrated spotlight, while magnetic dust filters on the top, side and bottom help keep the system clean. The Atlas P7 is available in black and white, priced at $139.90.

items.title: God of War: Sons of Sparta update brings new modes alongside PS4 port
items.content:
Last week, we reported that Sony’s PlayStation 5 exclusive God of War: Sons of Sparta appeared to be coming to the last-gen PS4 thanks to an update which went live on Sony’s back-end PSN servers. Sure enough, the side-scrolling metroidvania has now been officially announced to be coming to the PS4. In a welcome surprise however, this back-port will also bring a number of welcome additions for those on PS5 – officially announcing a free major update going live today.
Taking to the PlayStation Blog to make the announcement, Sony’s Santa Monica Studio confirmed that God of War: Sons of Sparta will be coming to the PlayStation 4 – an unsurprising conclusion given that the game is a 2D title with a pixel art aesthetic.
What is somewhat surprising however is the fact that this release will be tied-in with a major free update for those on both PS4 and PS5. Available later today, the update will introduce two new game modes for added replayability:
Hermes Mode
A time trial mode featuring “a dedicated speedrunning toolkit with a split-based timer, persistent scoreboard, and more”
Erebus Mode
A hardcore mode in which both you and your enemies die in one hit
For the uninitiated, God of War: Sons of Sparta was shadow-dropped back in February for the PS5 as part of the franchise’s 20th anniversary celebrations. While a welcome addition to the God of War canon, reception towards the game was somewhat mixed, with critics lamenting its relatively generic position within the wider metroidvania genre.
Considering Sons of Sparta failed to make a splash on the sales charts back when it first launched, it is unlikely that the PS4 version will do much to change this fact. For those who did enjoy the original experience however, the addition of the Hermes and Erebus modes is a nice little bonus.

Why GTA 6 Took 13 Years: Rockstar Says It Refused to Make ‘GTA 5.5’
items.content:
Rockstar has finally explained why Grand Theft Auto VI took so long, and the short answer is that it turned down the quicker option. “They could have made GTA 5.5, and done it faster. Ultimately, that’s not what they wanted,” Rockstar executive Jennifer Kolbe told The Guardian in a feature published on 15 November. Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North, was blunter still. “You have to take big swings,” he said, adding that the sequel “can’t be just more of the same”.
Those lines come from a visit to Rockstar North in Edinburgh by the paper’s games editor, Keza MacDonald, which we covered for what it revealed about empathy and the new Criminal Profile. The same interview also answers the question fans have asked since 2013. GTA 6 launches on 19 November, 13 years and two months after Grand Theft Auto V, and Rockstar’s explanation comes down to how big the game became and how long that takes to build.
Rockstar says people and time now set the limit, not technology
Nelson told the Guardian that hardware is no longer what holds Rockstar back. The question now, he said, is “how much can we physically build?” with the people and the time the studio has. According to the paper, nearly 5,000 people worked on GTA 6, a team roughly four times the size of the one that made GTA 5.
A bigger team does not automatically mean a faster game, though. Rockstar’s leadership told the paper that throwing money at a project is no guarantee of making something good, and Kolbe said the team would never stop working on the game if they had the choice. Many developers had already finished their work weeks before launch, the Guardian reported.
The pressure came from inside the building as much as from fans. “I don’t know that any amount of external pressure could compare with the pressure we put on ourselves as a team,” Nelson told Dazed in September. He added that the pressure “is ultimately a privilege”, which is a long way from how most players have felt about the wait.
From a Miami research trip in 2015 to an 80-hour campaign
The game has been in some form of development for more than a decade. “The game’s been in development since 2015, so the idea is gestating for a long time,” Nelson told Trois Couleurs in August, adding that “we develop on very long cycles”. That date matches the first research trips to Miami, which ran under the codename Project Americas, and Bloomberg reported in October that full production started in 2018.
Rockstar did not confirm the project publicly until February 2022, and the first trailer followed in December 2023, as our GTA 6 timeline sets out. The release then slipped twice, first from autumn 2025 to 26 May 2026, and then to 19 November 2026. Take-Two chief executive Strauss Zelnick has since signalled that the next GTA will not take as long, without naming a date.
The size of the finished game is the other part of the answer. Nelson’s own run through GTA 6 in February took 80 hours and covered the main story plus “some optional goals with narrative ramifications”, according to a New York Times feature republished by The Star. Rockstar has not given an official mission count or story length. A report attributed to Insider Gaming’s sources puts the main story at around 50 hours over close to 100 missions, and Rockstar has not confirmed it.
The 13-year wait still divides GTA fans
Not every player is ready to forgive the wait just because the game is big. This month alone, fans have pushed back on the 30fps reveal, and many are frustrated that GTA 6 arrives only on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, with no PC version announced. A former Rockstar technical director has even argued that AI-made rip-offs could push a PC release forward.
The long development also has a harder side. Days before the Guardian’s visit, Kolbe gave evidence at a Glasgow employment tribunal brought by more than 30 developers Rockstar dismissed in 2025, the paper noted. The Independent Workers’ Union of Great Britain links the firings to union activity, which Rockstar denies, as our coverage of the tribunal explains.
Demand, at least, has not faded during all those years. GTA 6 is estimated to have taken $1.18 billion from digital pre-orders, according to Sensor Tower, and Rockstar opened pre-loading on 10 November. Reviews are due on 18 November, and the game unlocks the next day at the times in our GTA 6 release time guide. The official Grand Theft Auto VI site lists the launch as 19 November on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

items.title: PGL Reveals 7 Conflicts of Interest at the Singapore Major, Including Rival Players Who Have A Lot in Common
items.content:
PGL has published seven declared conflicts of interest among the players and teams heading to the PGL Major Singapore, eight days before the Counter-Strike 2 Major begins on 24 November. The list, posted on PGL’s X account on 16 November with a five-page document, covers five player loans, one minority shareholding and one company owned jointly by players on rival teams. According to the document, “no other conflicts of interest have been disclosed by the participating teams and players”. Valve’s rules for the Major require organisers to collect these declarations and make them public before the event starts.
Four of the seven conflicts link two teams that are both competing in Singapore. The other three involve organisations that are not at the event, namely BIG, paiN Gaming and K27, which PGL says did not submit declarations of their own. None of the disclosures suggests wrongdoing, and the point of publishing them is to show fans exactly where those connections sit before a single map is played.
The seven conflicts PGL disclosed for the Singapore Major
Here is every declared conflict, taken from PGL’s document, with whether the other party is also playing at the Major. Four rows involve two teams that will both be in Singapore, so those are the ones to watch if the draw puts them together. The other three only matter for what happens after the event, when the loans end.
The One is the name 1win is using in Singapore, and BB Team is BetBoom, after PGL confirmed new names for four teams because of Singapore’s gambling rules. That means one of the loans runs between two organisations that are both playing under temporary names at the same event. The One also lists a substitute on an emergency loan from K27, which is not at the Major.
Why HEROIC’s susp and NIP’s adamb stand out
Most of the list is ordinary roster business. Loans have become a common way for organisations to place players who are not in their starting line-up, and a loaned player usually still has a contract with the team that owns him. Five of the seven entries are loans of this kind, and four of them run until the final days of December, well after the Major has finished.
The HEROIC entry is different, because it involves a financial link between players on two rival teams rather than between organisations. PGL’s document says susp co-owns a company called AdamTim Performance AB with adamb of Ninjas in Pyjamas, and that both players receive their salaries and prize money through it. If HEROIC and NIP meet in Singapore, the two players will be on opposite sides of the server while sharing that company.
Legacy’s arT has a smaller link of the same kind, through a shareholding of less than 1% in FURIA. FURIA arrives in good form after beating Team Spirit to win BLAST Rivals Season 2, and Team Spirit is itself on the list because of SYPH0’s loan to Nemiga Gaming. PGL’s document includes extracts from each signed declaration, covering the other party, the nature of the conflict and the planned resolution.
What Valve’s Major rules say about conflicts
The disclosures come from Valve’s Major Supplemental Rulebook, which every Major organiser must include in its own rules. It says that teams and players “should not have any financial interest in the success of any team that they are competing against”. To take part, each player and team must affirm that they have no conflict of interest, including shared management, shared ownership of companies, licensing deals and loans, with any other participating team.
Anyone who does have such a conflict must give details to Valve’s Counter-Strike team, along with a plan for resolving it, and the organiser must collect the declarations and publish them before the event starts. Valve keeps a public repository of its Counter-Strike rules, which includes the declaration form and the wider tournament requirements that organisers must follow. The same rules also govern how teams qualify, as seen in Valve’s exception for s1mple’s BC.Game to qualify through Asia.
The PGL Major Singapore has 32 teams across three stages and begins on 24 November, with the playoffs at the Singapore Indoor Stadium. It is the second Counter-Strike Major of 2026, after IEM Cologne, and the first Major ever held in Singapore. PGL’s full disclosure document is public, and PGL says no other conflicts have been declared by any participating team or player.

GTA 6 Release Date and Time in India: When Can You Play?
items.content:
More than a decade after GTA V and years of delays in development, Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally approaching its global launch. As India prepares to make a return to the highly anticipated Vice City on November 19, 2026, Rockstar has adopted a staggered rollout that will let players access the game exactly at midnight in their respective time zones as opposed to a generalised simultaneous global release.
GTA 6 Release Date and Time in India
Grand Theft Auto 6 will be officially available to play in India at 12:00 AM IST on Thursday, November 19, 2026. This launch date is confirmed to be consistent across both PlayStation and Xbox, which will allow players to dive right into the game, provided they have pre-loaded the game ahead of its release.
Interestingly, India is set to be one of the first countries where the game will launch ahead of the West due to the time zone advantage. Countries like New Zealand, Australia, and Japan will receive it well before India, with western regions like Europe and the Americas receiving it at the very end of the release window.
Platforms and Pre-Load Availability
The November 19th launch is dedicated to Xbox and PlayStation, with no confirmed release date for the PC version of the game. Given the massive 200GB+ file size of GTA 6 on both platforms, Rockstar has allowed players to pre-load the game so they can enjoy it right after its release without having to spend additional time downloading it.
GTA 6 India Pricing
Grand Theft Auto 6 is priced at ₹5,999 for the Standard Edition and ₹7,499 for the Ultimate Edition in India across the PlayStation Store (India) and Xbox Store, making it one of the most expensive games to ever hit the market and for good reason.
While fans have cast doubt on its pre-order figures, the global launch is likely to cause a significant boost to its sales. Despite the staggering upfront price, the game offers considerable appeal, especially since the hype built around it over the past few years is likely to be sufficient to turn it into one of the most profitable video games of all time.
With a release less than a week away, fans should ensure they have pre-loaded the game before the global launch. Given that India would be one of the first countries where Rockstar would make the game playable, fans should waste no time diving right into Vice City and exploring the game that made us wait with anticipation for years.

Can You Actually Play GTA 6 on PS4 or Xbox One?
items.content:
GTA 6 on PS4 or Xbox One has two different answers. Xbox One owners can play Grand Theft Auto VI through Xbox Cloud Gaming from 1 AM ET on November 19, 2026, which is 11:30 AM IST. PS4 owners cannot, because PlayStation says the game is only playable on PS5. Xbox One players must buy the game separately, and the stream uses Xbox Series S graphics settings.
Below, you will find the start time, the steps for Xbox One, the cost, and the options for PS4 players.
Can You Play GTA 6 on PS4 or Xbox One?
Yes, you can play GTA 6 on Xbox One, but only by streaming it. Xbox announced on November 10 that Grand Theft Auto VI will run through Xbox Cloud Gaming on Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar Games confirmed the same plan in its own post.
No, you cannot play GTA 6 on PS4. PlayStation’s game page says Grand Theft Auto VI is only playable on PS5 consoles and is not available for PS4. Rockstar lists PS5 and Xbox Series X|S as the native console platforms.
The GTA 6 release date is November 19, 2026. Native PS5 and Xbox Series X|S versions unlock at midnight in each region’s local time. Xbox Cloud Gaming has its own start time, which is listed below.
GTA 6 Xbox One Cloud Streaming Start Time
Xbox says cloud streaming goes live at 10 PM PT on November 18. That is 1 AM ET on November 19, or 11:30 AM IST in India. The same start time applies to players streaming on Xbox Series X|S.
You stream the game over the internet, so there is nothing to preload on Xbox One.
How to Play GTA 6 on Xbox One
Once streaming goes live, follow these steps:
Sign in to your Xbox One with the account you used to buy GTA 6 digitally.
Open My games & apps.
Go to Full library, then Owned Games.
Select Grand Theft Auto VI.
Choose Play with Cloud Gaming.
You can also start the stream from the game’s Xbox Store page once the cloud option appears.
GTA 6 Cost and Cloud Hours on Xbox One
You need to buy GTA 6 separately to stream it. A Game Pass subscription is not required in supported markets. Xbox says you can buy cloud playtime through the Xbox Store, and that this option has been open since November 11, 2026.
Subscribers get a monthly cloud allowance:
Game Pass Essential: 5 hours
Game Pass Premium: 10 hours
Game Pass Ultimate: 15 hours
These caps limit how long you can stream each month. Xbox also says cloud access, purchase options, and device support can differ by market and device. Check your own Xbox Store before launch day.
GTA 6 Graphics on Xbox Cloud Gaming
Xbox confirmed that the cloud version uses Xbox Series S graphics settings. This applies on Xbox One and on Xbox Series X|S. A player streaming on a Series X also gets the Series S settings.
Xbox has not said what this means for resolution or draw distance. Rockstar adds that connection speed and other technical factors can affect streaming performance in ways local play does not. Rockstar also targets 30 frames per second across its console platforms.
Can You Play GTA 6 on PS4?
The GTA 6 PS4 answer is no. PlayStation’s page limits the game to PS5 consoles. As of November 16, no cloud streaming option for PS4 has been announced.
Rockstar says GTA 6 fully supports Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox. Remote Play streams a game from a console that already runs it to another device. PlayStation lists 5 Mbps as the minimum connection speed and recommends 15 Mbps.
In short, Xbox One is the only last-generation console with an official way to play. It relies on Xbox Cloud Gaming, a separate game purchase, and a stable internet connection. PS4 has no announced route.

items.title: Xi Lai Gaming Reportedly Lands Zeus for VCT 2027 After Dropping xavi8k
items.content:
Xi Lai Gaming have reached a verbal agreement to sign Filipino duelist Jhian “Zeus” Vega for the 2027 VCT season, according to Sheep Esports. The report, by Tanmay and others, landed on 16 November, only half an hour after the same outlet said XLG had backed out of a deal with Xavier “xavi8k” Juan. Zeus spent 2026 with Team Secret in VCT Pacific, and the organization lost its partner slot for the next cycle. Neither XLG nor Zeus has announced the move, and a verbal agreement is not a signed contract.
If it goes through, Zeus would fill the import slot on one of the eight teams Riot has partnered with in China for 2027 and 2028. XLG enters that cycle as a partner for the first time, after two years in the top flight as an Ascension team. The full list of 32 VCT partner teams also explains why so many good Pacific players are suddenly on the market this winter.
Why XLG turned to Zeus after dropping xavi8k
The xavi8k deal had looked settled, because he was the in-game leader who took Global Esports to its first VCT Pacific trophy at Stage 2 in Busan, and then to Masters London and Champions Shanghai. When Global Esports quit Valorant in October and released its roster, Sheep Esports reported that he would join XLG. His former teammates scattered quickly too, with UdoTan signing for Nongshim RedForce in early November.
On Monday morning, the same outlet reported that XLG had backed out of that verbal agreement as part of a wider rebuild. It also said Zeus had been on XLG’s shortlist for the import slot before the club first chose xavi8k. Neither XLG nor xavi8k has explained publicly why the earlier deal fell apart.
The swap changes the shape of the team. XLG loses a proven shotcaller from the Pacific league and gains a younger, aggressive fragger instead. That means the calling will have to come from elsewhere in a lineup that is being rebuilt almost from scratch.
From Oasis Gaming to Team Secret’s top-rated player
Zeus made his professional debut in 2024 with Oasis Gaming in VALORANT Challengers Philippines. According to Sheep Esports, his best results since then include winning the 2026 Predator League Philippines and finishing in the top three at Challengers Southeast Asia Split 3 in 2025. His aggressive style earned him a move to Team Secret ahead of the 2026 VCT season.
He started that year as a substitute and moved into the active lineup before Stage 2. Team Secret had another difficult season and failed to qualify for a single international event. Sheep Esports reported that Zeus was still the team’s highest-rated player during Stage 2, which is a strong line on a young duelist’s record even in a losing side.
Team Secret then missed out when Riot cut each international league from ten partners to eight for 2027. That left Zeus free to look elsewhere at the same time as several other Pacific players, including most of the Global Esports roster. For XLG, that meant a ready-made Pacific option was available at exactly the moment its first plan for the import slot fell apart.
XLG’s 2027 roster is built around d4v41 and ZmjjKK
XLG has already been linked with two of the biggest signings of the offseason. Sheep Esports reported earlier this month that the club would add Khalish “d4v41” Rusyaidee, who won Masters Toronto with Paper Rex, and Zheng “ZmjjKK” Yongkang, who won Champions Seoul with EDward Gaming. Teng “happywei” Min-wei and Huang “WsLeo” Ping-wei complete the five-man list in Sheep’s latest report.
There is one wrinkle in that list, and it concerns WsLeo. Sheep Esports’ earlier report on Monday said XLG had allowed WsLeo and James “NoMan” Man to explore their options, but its Zeus report includes WsLeo in the 2027 lineup. Both players remain under contract, until the end of 2028 and 2027 respectively, according to the official VCT Global Contract Database cited by the outlet. Head coach Aleksandr “hvoya” Eremin has left for Aurora Gaming, it added.
The club has the results to justify the ambition. XLG won VCT China Stage 1 in 2025, finished second at the 2026 China Kickoff and Stage 1, and reached the upper semifinals at Masters London after upsetting G2 Esports. It now joins rivals such as Weibo Gaming, which is reportedly bringing in babybay, in a China league that is rebuilding fast.
Partner status guarantees less than it used to. Under Riot’s new VCT 2027 format, partners are only promised a place at Kickoff, and results decide the rest of their season. Sheep Esports said XLG will be invited directly to VCT China Kickoff, Cup 1 and Cup 2, and the 2027 roster it has reported is ZmjjKK, d4v41, happywei, Zeus and WsLeo.

items.title: GTA 6 Is Already on Millions of Consoles, So Why Can’t Anyone Play It Early?
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto VI is already sitting on millions of PS5 and Xbox Series consoles, and a viral post on X wants to know why nobody has cracked it open. “Surprised that GTA6 has been downloaded locally about a bajillion times and nobody has reverse engineered it to play it earlier,” wrote evan j (@ejcx_) on 16 November. He guessed that each copy uses “some pretty basic per user symmetric key” and asked if anyone knew how the DRM works. The post had passed 368,000 views by Monday afternoon IST, three days before the game unlocks.
The short answer is that a pre-load is not the same as a copy you can run. The game’s files arrive early so that players are not stuck behind a 212 GB download on launch night. The console will not start them, though, until the store issues a licence at the official unlock time. Rockstar has not described the protection on GTA 6, and Sony and Microsoft do not publish how their consoles lock pre-loaded games.
What pre-loading GTA 6 actually gives you
Pre-loading opened on 10 November, nine days before launch. According to Rockstar’s support page, PS5 pre-loads began at midnight local time in each region, while Xbox Series X|S pre-loads began everywhere at 12am GMT. As we reported when pre-loading went live, the download needs up to 212 GB, and everything stays locked until release.
Even the boxed version of GTA 6 works this way, because there is no disc to install from. Rockstar says the physical edition contains only a download code, and “a disc will not be included in the box”, so retail buyers end up with the same locked download as everyone else. That has created its own problem this week, with some buyers saying their boxes arrived without codes or with used ones.
The game unlocks on 19 November at times that vary by region, and our GTA 6 release time guide lists the exact moment for each one. Until then, the 212 GB on a console is of no use to anyone who wants to play, however long ago it finished downloading. Anyone who has not finished pre-loading by then faces a slower download on launch night, as our pre-load guide warned, when millions of players hit the servers at once.
Why console pre-loads are harder to break than PC ones
Several replies under the post pointed out what the original guess skipped. One user wrote that breaking encryption is not as trivial as the post implied, while another joked that “key was 4, already playing it”. A reply claiming that the game checks for a valid licence token on every boot was widely liked, although its author did not give a source and TalkEsport has not verified it.
The bigger reason is the hardware GTA 6 runs on. It is only on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, plus Xbox One through the cloud, as we covered in our report on GTA 6’s Xbox One version, and cloud players get no local files at all. Modern consoles are built so that games only run in a locked-down environment that the console maker controls, and there is no PC version on which anyone could poke at the files freely.
Sony has also been closing the gaps that modified consoles rely on. Since mid-October, PS5 consoles on firmware older than 14.10 have reportedly been unable to sign in to PlayStation Network, as we covered in our story on Sony’s crackdown on jailbroken PS5s. A jailbroken console that cannot reach PSN would also have no way to receive a licence for a pre-ordered game.
When games do leak early, it is usually a PC build
Early leaks of big games do happen, but they tend to come from somewhere other than a console pre-load. In May, a full PC build of Forza Horizon 6 reportedly leaked days before its 19 May launch and was cracked, after early reports blamed an unencrypted upload. Microsoft said at the time that the leak was “not the result of a pre-load issue”, and warned that people accessing the build faced bans.
Rockstar has not announced a PC version of GTA 6, which removes the most common route for a pre-release crack, and its support page lists only PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. TalkEsport found no credible report of anyone playing the game from a pre-load, and no comment from Rockstar on the post. The official Grand Theft Auto VI site still counts down to Thursday, 19 November.
The post GTA 6 Is Already on Millions of Consoles, So Why Can’t Anyone Play It Early? appeared first on TalkEsport.

KFC Is Holding a Funeral on GTA 6 Launch Day So Fans Have an Alibi
items.content:
KFC Australia is holding a funeral on GTA 6 launch day, and the deceased does not exist. The fast food chain announced on Instagram that a fictional woman called Ann Alibi has died, with her service set for 11am on Thursday, 19 November, the day Grand Theft Auto VI unlocks. The joke is in the name, because the stunt hands players a ready-made excuse for skipping work. By Monday afternoon, “kfc gta funeral” was trending on Google Trends in Australia, with more than 2,000 searches.
The announcement is written like a real death notice. “It is with heavy hearts, and a much lighter workload, that we announce Ann finally got her wings,” KFC wrote, according to Mumbrella. The post adds that “by remarkable coincidence”, her service falls on the same day as the biggest game launch of the year.
Where and when the Ann Alibi funeral takes place
The service is planned for KFC Robina, at 118 to 120 Robina Town Centre Drive on the Gold Coast, subject to final site approvals, Mediaweek reported. It starts at 11am on 19 November, and KFC says funeral attire is encouraged. Mourners will find a book of condolences, an order of service and commemorative photos, as if this were a real farewell.
People who turn up in person get free KFC while stocks last, plus documentation showing that they attended. For everyone else, KFC will livestream the service nationally on its Instagram from 11am. It is also offering free delivery through the KFC app on orders over $30 that day, which it calls Ann’s “final wish”, under its usual promotional terms.
KFC has kept a straight face about the timing. Ann’s fictional birthday is listed as 28 November 1997, which Mumbrella notes is the launch date of the original Grand Theft Auto, and KFC says “any resemblance to a certain launch date is purely coincidental”. A KFC spokesperson told Mediaweek that “some occasions are simply too important to miss”. The stunt is part of the brand’s Go Full Chicken platform, and it has no official link to Rockstar Games.
A funeral note won’t get you bereavement leave
There is a catch for anyone hoping to show a manager the paperwork. Mediaweek noted that attending does not automatically qualify an employee for compassionate leave or any other kind of leave. Under the Fair Work rules on compassionate leave, employees get two days when a member of their immediate family or household dies, and a fried chicken mascot does not count.
The Fair Work Ombudsman has been in on the GTA joke for weeks. In October, it posted on Instagram about whether any unpaid leave entitlement covers a game launch, and concluded that none does, although workers can still ask for general unpaid leave that their employer may approve. More recently, it reminded Australians that employers can ask for evidence when staff call in sick on launch day, according to Mumbrella. Not everyone needs an alibi, because some employers have simply given in, such as the Palworld developer that gave its staff a five-day GTA 6 holiday. Workers elsewhere will have to book annual leave the old-fashioned way, and that is the route many Australians appear to be taking.
Australians are already booking 19 November off
The data suggests plenty of people are doing exactly that. Annual leave bookings for 19 November among more than 870,000 Australian workers on Employment Hero’s platform are up 29% on the same day last year, Mumbrella reported. Requests from men aged 18 to 44 rose 84%, which is not hard to explain this week.
That is a real effect, but it is a lot smaller than some of the claims going around. TalkEsport has already checked the viral 12.5 million day-off and $1 billion figures, and they don’t add up. What is clear is that demand for GTA 6 is enormous, with the game estimated to have taken $1.18 billion from digital pre-orders, according to Sensor Tower.
In Australia, GTA 6 unlocks on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S at the times listed in our GTA 6 release time guide. Ann Alibi’s service begins at 11am on Thursday at KFC Robina, and the livestream runs on KFC Australia‘s Instagram at the same time. KFC has not said how many mourners it expects, or how long the free food will last at the Gold Coast store.
The post KFC Is Holding a Funeral on GTA 6 Launch Day So Fans Have an Alibi appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: PMGC 2026 Dates and Format Explained: Check Here
items.content:
KRAFTON and Level Infinite have finally revealed the highly anticipated format of the PMGC 2026. The format is quite similar to the last edition with some changes. The PMGC 2026 format consists of four stages: The Gauntlet, Group Stage, Last Chance, and Grand Finals.
The PMGC 2026 kicks off on 26 November, and the Grand Finals will be played from 11 to 13 December. A total of 39 teams will battle it out for the one trophy in Istanbul, Turkey, including one Indian team, Team Soul.
PMGC 2026 Format Explained
Gauntlet
The Gauntlet stage will take place on 26 and 27 November, featuring 16 teams playing 12 games. The top 6 teams from this stage will qualify for the Grand Finals, while the remaining teams will move to the Group Stage.
Gauntlet Teams: AK Gold Esports, Sharper Esports, 4Thrives Esports, The MongolZ, Aurora Gaming, 4K Esports, iKURD Esports, S2G Esports, Gaming Stars, Hustler Crew, Wolves, RoW Esports, XForce Rejects, All Gamers, Team Soul and NS RedForce.
Group Stage
The group stage will take place on 29-30 November and 2-3 December. 32 teams will be divided into two groups of 16. Each group will play a total of 12 matches, and the top 3 teams from each group will qualify for the Grand Finals, while the 4th to 11th placed teams move to the Last Chance stage. The bottom 5 teams of both groups will be eliminated from the tournament.

items.title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer has officially surpassed 1.5 million players
items.content:
2026 has been a great year for Star Wars fans on the video game front, with the IP based on a galaxy far far away having released two unique and critically praised titles in the form of Star Wars: Zero Company and Galactic Racer. With regards to the latter, the Fuse Games-developed rogue-lite arcade racer has managed to hit a noteworthy milestone – officially amassing over 1.5 million players in its first month on the market.
Taking to Twitter to make the announcement, the official game's page wrote the following: “It's been one month since STAR WARS: Galactic Racer launched on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC […] Thank you to every one of the 1.5m pilots who have joined the Galactic League so far and we can't wait to share more about the future of STAR WARS: Galactic Racer with you.”
As always, it is worth noting that 1.5 million players does not equate to 1.5 million copies sold, especially as the title was added to Amazon’s Luna cloud streaming service back in early October. That said, given that Galactic Racer is a very fast-paced arcadey experience, playing through cloud streaming is unlikely to be the most optimal way to play and so is unlikely to have contributed too much to the 1.5 million figure.
Perhaps the most exciting part of the announcement is the fact that Galactic Racer appears geared to receive new content via future updates – though what this will entail remains to be seen.
All that said, with Galactic Racer and Zero Company both hitting milestone player / sales figures, and Lucasfilm expressing desires to explore “all kinds” of different Star Wars games, the future of the franchise in gaming appears to be bright.

items.content:
Last week, 6 years on from the initial launch of the console, Sony officially announced that the PlayStation 5 had hit a massive sales milestone – officially surpassing 100 million units sold. While Microsoft have shied away from sharing their own console sales for a few generations now, insiders / analysts have offered updated stats for the Xbox Series X|S, claiming that it has managed a little over a 3rd of Sony’s output with 38 million units in total.
Following the official announcement by Sony that the PS5 had sold-in 100 million consoles since its arrival in late 2020, known industry analyst Daniel Ahmad released a chart revealing how many units other consoles had managed to push in their first 6 years on the market:
NDS – 136m
Switch – 122m
PS4 – 103m
PS2 – 103m
PS5 – 100m
Wii – 97m
PS1 – 77m
PS3 – 70m
3DS – 65m
X360 – 60m
XOne – 49m

As mentioned, Microsoft stopped publicly sharing its console sales data back during the Xbox One era, and so its figures are said to be “based on company data and estimates”. That said, Ahmad is generally a reputable source, and so it’s safe to assume the Xbox figures are at the very least close to being accurate.
Though their priorities seem to have shifted recently, Microsoft had for years been pushing its Xbox Play Anywhere scheme, de-prioritising its console in favour of Game Pass and cloud streaming, and so it perhaps makes sense that the Series X|S would fall behind the likes of the 360.
Regardless, it is always interesting to get insight into the sales performance of a console (although assuming these figures to be true, it perhaps makes sense why Microsoft stopped disclosing unit sales).

Sony’s QSSR upscaler is coming to Spider-Man, ARC Raiders, No Man’s Sky and more
items.content:
In a surprise announcement earlier this month, Sony unveiled and subsequently released its Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR) upscaler for the base PS5 – a more streamlined version of the bespoke PSSR developed for PlayStation’s Pro console. Limited to just Marvel’s Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei initially, the upscaler has now been officially announced to be coming to half a dozen other titles, including Marvel’s Spider-Man 2; ARC Raiders; No Man’s Sky and more.
Taking to the PlayStation Blog to make the announcement, Sony confirmed its second batch of PS5 titles which are set to support the console maker’s new QSSR upscaler. Said to be “rolling out over the coming weeks” a total of 6 games have been announced to be receiving improvements, namely:
Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 (Available now)
No Man’s Sky (arriving in the next few weeks)
Control Resonant (coming in December)
The Finals
ARC Raiders
Hell Let Loose: Vietnam
For the uninitiated, QSSR is designed to deliver “sharper details, cleaner edges, and more stable images than traditional upscalers”. Being “built on the same foundation as PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution” for the PS5 Pro, we should hopefully see many more developers / games support the technology in time.
Given that the Pro includes PSSR across well over 100 titles, it is safe to assume that many of these will eventually also offer QSSR for the base PS5.
While not quite as comprehensive as the Pro version, Sony’s QSSR has proven to be a net-benefit so far, with the upscaler helping to get rid of ‘jaggies’ (aka aliasing) in most situations without negatively impacting performance.
Of course, results can vary on an individual basis, and so we will have to wait and see how QSSR holds up across these titles once they have been implemented. So far however, things seem to be trending positively. It will be interesting to see how both PSSR and QSSR evolve over time.

Ubisoft Bans Tubarao and Noor Interaction for Rest of BLAST R6 Major Osaka
items.content:
Ubisoft banned an interaction between Tubarão and Noor in Rainbow Six Siege for the rest of the BLAST R6 Major Osaka on 11 November. The ruling covers the combination of Tubarão’s Zoto Canister and Noor’s Horus Lance against hard breach gadgets. Ubisoft said any confirmed use of the interaction “will result in a round loss”. Both operators stayed available, and their gadgets could still be used separately.
Ubisoft said one Zoto Canister could freeze both a Horus Lance and a hard breach gadget at the same time. When the freeze ended, the Lance disabled the hard breach gadget. Ubisoft said it decided “not to allow this interaction” after monitoring its effect on matches. It applied the ruling under section 4.6 of the Osaka Major rulebook.
Osaka Major teams had already agreed not to use Tubarão and Noor
The official ruling came four days after all 20 teams at the Major agreed among themselves not to use the combination. Team Liquid’s Felipe “FelipoX” Lucia announced the gentlemen’s agreement on 7 November, after the interaction surfaced on the tournament’s opening day. Players first thought the interaction was a bug.
BLAST asked Ubisoft about it, and players were told the interaction was intended. FelipoX said the gadgets “never worked this way” and that no one had been told about the change. The interaction did not appear in the latest patch notes. The agreement had no penalty attached, which left it to each team to honour.
What the BLAST R6 Major Osaka ruling does not cover
The ruling is not retroactive, and Ubisoft said earlier matches would not be reviewed. It applied only until the end of the Osaka Major, the second and final Major of the 2026 season. Ubisoft has not said whether it will change the interaction in a future update, or whether the restriction will carry over to the Six Invitational 2027.
The BLAST R6 Major Osaka ran from 6 to 15 November, with the playoffs at ATC Hall in Osaka. It carried a $600,000 prize pool and Six Invitational 2027 points. It was the first top-level international Rainbow Six Siege LAN in Japan since 2019.

items.title: FFWS 2026 Global Finals Knockout Phase 2: Date, Teams, Format, and More
items.content:
Knockout Stage Phase 2 of the Free Fire World Series (FFWS) 2026 Global Finals runs in Bangkok from 19 to 22 November. Eighteen teams take part, and eight of them will reach the Grand Finals at BITEC LIVE on 28 November. Buriram United Esports enter Phase 2 top of the table after finishing Phase 1 with 647 points. The other 10 teams drop into the Last Chance stage on 27 November.
Phase 2 splits the 18 survivors into four pools based on their Phase 1 rankings. The top 12 teams start on the first day, and the six teams placed 13th to 18th join two at a time over the next three days. Two teams qualify for the Grand Finals each day. The event carries a $1,200,000 prize pool.
FFWS 2026 Global Finals Knockout Phase 2 schedule and format
Each Phase 2 matchday has six matches. The top two teams on each day move to the Grand Finals, and the remaining 10 carry on to the next day. Two new teams from the lower pools enter each day, so every matchday has 12 teams in the lobby.
Matches use the standard FFWS scoring. A win is worth 12 placement points, second place nine and third place eight, with one point for every elimination. The scale drops to one point for 10th place and nothing for 11th and 12th.
Which teams play FFWS 2026 Knockout Phase 2
Buriram United Esports, the defending champions, finished Phase 1 with 647 points, 11 more than LOS in second. Fluxo W7M were third with 633 points, and P Esports fourth with 599. The 12 teams in Pool 1 all play on the opening day, which gives them the most chances to qualify before the Last Chance stage.
Resurrection Esports and GunDynasty both finished on 411 points, and Resurrection took 13th place. GunDynasty reached that total despite a 15-point penalty after the opening day of Phase 1. Garena docked them for deliberately dying in the zone in the sixth match.
India’s Team Apex Gaming and Resurrection Esports in Phase 2
Two of India’s three teams remain in the event. Resurrection Esports enter on 20 November in Pool 2, and Team Apex Gaming enter on 22 November in Pool 4. Team Apex Gaming will play only one Phase 2 matchday before the Last Chance stage if they do not finish in the top two on 22 November.
India’s third team, TSG Pros, finished 21st with 315 points and missed the Last Chance stage by two points. Horaa Esports, 19th on 334, and Stellar Esport, 20th on 317, go straight to the Last Chance stage. ParadoX Gaming, Total Winner Esports and Pirate Esports were also eliminated.
The Grand Finals use the Champion Rush format. A team must first reach 110 points and then win a match to take the title, with no limit on the number of matches. The full Phase 1 table is on the FFWS 2026 Global Finals page on Liquipedia, and Garena has not yet published start times for the Phase 2 matchdays.

items.title: Vanshaj Sharma Interview: “I Was Here for Revenge,” Red Bull Wings Cup India Champion on Miami
items.content:
Vanshaj Sharma will represent India at the Red Bull Wings Cup World Final in Miami after winning the EA Sports FC 27 India National Final at Kettle Studio in Bengaluru on 15 November. The RNTX player beat Saransh Jain 2–0 in the best-of-three final, winning the games 5–1 and 4–1. The title came two days after he returned from the FC Pro Open Global Qualifier in London, and less than two weeks after RNTX signed him for that event.
Minutes after lifting the trophy, Vanshaj spoke to TalkEsport’s Pranav Nalawade in Bengaluru. He talked about beating a close friend in the final, the practice he brought back from London, the Esports Nations Cup qualifier he missed by one game in August, and the part of his game he wants to fix before Miami. The interview was conducted in Hindi and English and has been translated and lightly edited for clarity.
Vanshaj Sharma on winning Red Bull Wings Cup India
TalkEsport: Congratulations. You have your ticket to Miami and the responsibility of representing India. How do you see an opportunity this big?
Vanshaj Sharma: Like I said, I am very overwhelmed with emotions. This is a very big thing for me, and my emotions are overflowing right now. But I am very proud of myself, and as I said, I will make my country very proud when I go there. So yeah, I am really excited.
TalkEsport: Saransh is one of India’s most experienced FC players. What does beating him in the final mean to you?
Vanshaj Sharma: He is a very good friend of mine. We have been competing against each other back to back for many years, so it feels bad to beat him too. But in the end we are opponents. Playing with him is always a good experience. GGs to him.
From the FC Pro qualifier in London to Bengaluru in two days
TalkEsport: Last week you were in London, and today you are winning in Bengaluru. How do you look at these two weeks of your life?
Vanshaj Sharma: London was a very good experience, playing against the best players in the world again. I got very good practice there, and I came back to India very confident. I landed only two days ago, then came here to Bengaluru the day after. I was full of confidence, and I used the momentum to win.
TalkEsport: In August you went out of the Esports Nations Cup qualifier. Is today’s win your answer to that loss?
Vanshaj Sharma: You can say that, because I missed out by one game on representing India again. So I was here for revenge. I want to represent India, and I feel so much pride that I am going to represent India. It was always my dream.
Vanshaj Sharma on RNTX and his plans for Miami
TalkEsport: Revenant XSpark signed you only last month, and now you have a national title. What message would you give the organisation?
Vanshaj Sharma: I would like to say thanks for supporting me and thanks for signing me. In moments like these, in tournaments like this, confidence, momentum and support from an organisation are very important. You feel safe, you feel very confident, and you know who you have to make proud. So I thank RNTX for supporting me.
Vanshaj Sharma won the Red Bull Wings Cup India National Final at Kettle Studio, Bengaluru, on 15 November. (Image: TalkEsport)
TalkEsport: You played the world’s top players in London. What do you want to change in your game for Miami? Where do you think you need to improve?
Vanshaj Sharma: I want to work more on my defence. I did not concede many goals in this tournament, but the players on the world stage are much better, so I will try to work on my defending. I am very satisfied with my attack. Of course I need to improve my overall game, but if you are asking, I will focus more on defending.
The Miami World Final is expected in January 2027. Red Bull has not confirmed the date, and the India National Final was the last stage of the Indian competition.

Over two days at COEX, more than 2,000 attendees converged for AI Day Seoul, bringing together Korea’s industry leaders, startups and developer communities advancing physical AI and AI agents.
At the plenary sessions, Deepu Talla, vice president of robotics and edge AI at NVIDIA, said Korea is “punching above its weight,” with Doosan Robotics, Hyundai Motor Group, LG Electronics and SK Group — as well as startups like Real World and Luda Robotics — using NVIDIA platforms to bring general-purpose robotics into the real world.
Jonathan Cohen, vice president of applied research at NVIDIA, showed how enterprises can build agents they own and control. Breakout sessions featured speakers from Coupang Intelligent Cloud, Doosan Robotics, LG AI Research, LG Electronics, NAVER Cloud, SK Telecom and Upstage.
“It was a genuinely enjoyable time to have candid conversations,” said Hyunho Yang, research engineer for omnimodal foundation models at SK Telecom. “Seeing the passion of fellow AI developers was a real source of inspiration for me.”

The Agentic AI 10x Bootcamp Community Day brought together Pseudo Lab, Python Korea, PyTorchKR, HAERAE, Hugging Face KREW, Graph User Group, Womxn Who Code Korea, Dnol (Datayanolja) and other developer communities. Five finalists from the Hangul Day hackathon, co-hosted with Fastcampus, built agents trained on the Korean language and culture with the OpenShell runtime. More than 500 developers also took part in full-day NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute workshops and NVIDIA Certification exams in Korean. How to check how many Chests you’ve opened in Fortnite
items.content:
Opening Chests has become the primary focus for millions of Fortnite players pursuing the Pirate Shop Access Token. With that in mind, it’s worth it to check how many Chests you’ve opened in Fortnite to see how close you are to finding the rare treasure.
This article outlines a few options you can utilize to track how many Chests you’ve opened on your Fortnite journey.
Key takeaways
There are two options to track Chests opened in Fortnite
An in-game Quest that brings you up to 1,000 Chests
A third-party tool created by a Reddit user
There are no guarantees that you will find the rare Treasures regardless of how many Chests you open
How to check how many Chests you’ve opened in Fortnite
For those just starting their journey, an active Fortnite Quest tracks how many Treasure and Rare Chests you have opened so far. There are five stages in total, taking you up to 1,000 Chests before you’ve completed the Quest.
Unfortunately, the options beyond that are limited. Once you complete that Quest, there is no in-game Chest tracker to show you your overall progress. However, if you are desperate to know, a Reddit user named Gatuno7000 launched a program to help.
The website is called Fortnite Chest Counter, and it uses your Fortnite Replay Files to check how many Chests you’ve opened. This website tracks the following:
Chests opened by you
Chests opened by your teammates
Average per match
Most Chests opened in a match
How many Chests per minute
How to use this tool
Epic Games does not endorse this tool. If you decide to use it, link your Fortnite Replay Folder to the website. The website will then import all that information and give you a comprehensive breakdown.
Other than the base Quest and this tool, there are no readily available options to track how many Chests you’ve opened in Fortnite. Regardless, you may want to keep an eye on how many games you’ve played to see how close you are to the 1-in-137,500 Pirate Token odds.
While there are no guarantees that opening 137,500 Chests will get you the Token, it gives you an idea of how much time you have invested in the process.
