Nvidia Director Mark Stevens Sold $946 Million of Stock Two Months Before Jensen Huang’s Exit
items.content:
Nvidia director Mark Stevens sold about 4.2 million Nvidia shares worth roughly $946 million between 31 August and 18 September, according to three Form 4 filings with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. The sales came about two months before Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive, and before Nvidia’s shares peaked on 6 October. None of the filings marks the trades as made under a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan, the pre-arranged schedules that many insiders use to sell. Stevens still holds about 27.5 million shares, and Nvidia has not commented on the sales.
There is no suggestion in the filings that the sales were linked to the scandal that later engulfed Huang. Stevens is one of Nvidia’s longest-serving directors and has sold large blocks before, and the trades began days after Nvidia reported its second-quarter results in late August, when company trading windows usually open. The timing has still drawn attention because of what followed. Within weeks, press inquiries about Huang’s ties to Megaspeed and Alice Huang were reaching Nvidia’s leadership, and by 12 November he had resigned.
Stevens sold 4.2 million shares in three filings at an average of about $223
The first filing covers sales from 31 August to 2 September, when Stevens sold about 1.85 million shares for roughly $411 million at prices between $220 and $226. A second filing covers 3 and 4 September, adding about 1.02 million shares for around $236 million as the price climbed above $234. The third and largest single block came on 18 September, when he sold 1.366 million shares for about $300 million at close to $220. Across the three filings, TalkEsport’s calculation from the reported weighted average prices gives a total of $946.6 million.
All of the shares came from the Third Millennium Trust, which Stevens and his wife run as co-trustees, according to the filings. The trust’s Nvidia holding fell from about 5.2 million shares to just under one million over those three weeks. Stevens still holds about 11.5 million shares directly and 15 million through a second vehicle, the Envy Trust, of which he is trustee. A lawyer signed each filing on his behalf as attorney-in-fact.
The unticked 10b5-1 box is the detail that stands out. Since 2023, insiders have had to flag on Form 4 whether a trade was made under such a plan, which lets them schedule sales in advance and gives them a defence against insider trading claims. Directors can still sell without one during open trading windows, provided they do not hold material non-public information. Interim chief executive Colette Kress, by contrast, sold about $7.6 million of shares in September under a plan adopted in June, according to a tally of 2026 filings.
Stevens accounts for almost all of Nvidia’s insider selling this year, while Huang sold nothing
Stevens is not a newcomer to the board. He has been a director since 2008, after an earlier spell from 1993 to 2006, according to Nvidia’s 2026 proxy statement. Before that, he spent almost two decades as a managing partner at Sequoia Capital, one of Nvidia’s original backers. He now runs S-Cubed Capital, his family’s investment office, and sits on the board’s compensation committee and its nominating and governance committee.
His selling dwarfs that of every other insider this year. Stevens sold about 6.3 million shares worth roughly $1.39 billion between March and September, out of about $1.42 billion sold by all Nvidia directors and officers in that period, according to the same tally. Huang made no open-market sales in 2026, although shares were withheld to cover tax on his stock awards and he gave away more than 800,000 shares. General counsel Tim Teter, whom Reuters has since reported Huang misled about the relationship, sold about $13 million of stock over the same weeks.
Nvidia’s shares are now far below the prices Stevens received
In hindsight, the sales look very well timed. Nvidia’s shares have fallen more than 30% from their 6 October closing high, wiping out more than $1.8 trillion in market value, according to Reuters. They now trade far below the average of about $223 that Stevens received. The decline has been driven by the scandal around Huang, the push in Congress for tighter export controls and a wider sell-off in chip stocks.
Stevens’s remaining stake keeps him heavily exposed to that fall. His 27.5 million shares are worth billions of dollars, and as a director he has a vote on the company’s response to the Huang affair, including the search for a new chief executive. The board’s independent directors have hired Wachtell Lipton to investigate Huang’s conduct, according to the board’s statement, and two large shareholders have asked it to keep Huang’s return on the table. Nvidia reports its third-quarter results on 17 November.
The post Nvidia Director Mark Stevens Sold $946 Million of Stock Two Months Before Jensen Huang’s Exit appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Lawmakers Push Tighter AI Chip Export Curbs After Report Megaspeed Arranged $12 Billion in Chips for China
items.content:
US lawmakers are moving to tighten controls on AI chip exports after a Wall Street Journal report on Megaspeed, the Singapore-based Nvidia partner at the centre of the Jensen Huang scandal. The company arranged nearly $12 billion worth of advanced chips for Chinese companies, the Journal said.
According to records reviewed by the Journal, the arrangements ran from March 2024 to June 2025, and they have raised fears that US export rules were broken or sidestepped. House Speaker Mike Johnson said there is “a developing consensus in Congress” on limiting chip exports to China, Reuters reported. Megaspeed has denied diverting Nvidia chips to China, and Nvidia has said it complies with US law.
Megaspeed’s former chief executive, Alice Huang, is the businesswoman whose relationship with Huang preceded his resignation from Nvidia on 12 November. Reuters reported on Saturday that Huang told Nvidia’s general counsel that his dealings with her and Megaspeed were standard business. The bills now gaining support in Washington, however, go well beyond one company or one executive. Together, they would change how the US polices where its most advanced chips end up and who can use them.
Chinese demand was served from data centres in Southeast Asia, the Journal reports
The Journal’s figures point to a model that current rules struggle to reach. Megaspeed bought at least $4.8 billion of AI equipment in under two years and installed it in Southeast Asian facilities, mostly in Malaysia, then rented out the computing power remotely, according to the records it reviewed. The newspaper described that structure as legal on its face. US export rules restrict shipping advanced chips to China, but they have not stopped Chinese companies from renting the same chips in data centres abroad.
Separate reporting points to physical diversion as well. A Chinese company linked to Megaspeed put smuggled Nvidia hardware into service at a Shanghai data centre, according to documents reported by Bloomberg. The equipment was worth about 485 million yuan (around $73 million) and included 52 Super Micro servers fitted with H100 or H200 processors. Both chips are barred from sale to China, although TalkEsport has not seen the documents.
Megaspeed has rejected the claims that it rerouted chips. In a statement dated 12 November, chairman and chief executive Tan Yong Pong said the company had cooperated with inspections by the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security. He added that Megaspeed had hired a US law firm to count its GPUs and check its compliance. Senator Tom Cotton had already urged the Commerce Secretary to investigate Megaspeed for skirting export laws.
Four bills would track chips, close the cloud gap and give Congress a veto-style say
Reuters identified four measures in the package now before Congress. The AI Overwatch Act would give Congress more power over exports of advanced AI chips, while the Chip Security Act would require companies to track where those processors are located, to curb smuggling. The Match Act would press US allies to restrict sales and servicing of chipmaking equipment bound for China. The Remote Access Security Act would give the Commerce Department tools to stop Chinese firms renting overseas data centres to reach Nvidia chips, which is the gap the Megaspeed model exposes.
Republicans want to attach new chip restrictions to the National Defense Authorization Act, the annual defence bill that must pass each year, according to a Senate aide quoted by Reuters. Congressional staff have also discussed a date and location for Huang to testify, and he is expected to appear before Thanksgiving. OpenAI has told lawmakers it supports the package, as TalkEsport reported when it examined claims that the AI labs engineered Huang’s exit.
Nvidia has beaten similar efforts in Congress before. In December 2025, Congress dropped a proposal to curb chip exports from the defence bill, in what Bloomberg described as a lobbying win for the company. Huang argued for years that selling to China keeps the country dependent on American technology, and that cutting it off hands the market to domestic rivals such as Huawei. The White House has largely sided with that view on chip sales.
Singapore’s case against Alice Huang has added weight to the push
Singapore’s own investigation has fed the pressure in Washington. Authorities held Alice Huang’s passport for months while they investigated server purchases, and in February the country barred her from re-entering after police concluded she had given them inaccurate information. The Ministry of Home Affairs said she was not investigated for espionage. US authorities have examined whether she gathered information for China, which Beijing denies, and no charges against her have been reported.
For Nvidia, the timing could hardly be more awkward. The company reports third-quarter results on 17 November, its first under interim chief executive Colette Kress, while its independent directors run a separate investigation into Huang’s conduct. Data centre sales made up the large majority of Nvidia’s revenue in its last reported quarter, which is why any new limit on who can buy or rent its chips matters to investors.
The post Lawmakers Push Tighter AI Chip Export Curbs After Report Megaspeed Arranged $12 Billion in Chips for China appeared first on TalkEsport.

Jensen Huang Told Nvidia’s Top Lawyer His Alice Huang Ties Were ‘Standard Business’, Reuters Reports
items.content:
Jensen Huang repeatedly told Nvidia’s most senior executives that his dealings with Alice Huang were ordinary business, according to a Reuters report published on Saturday. Citing two people familiar with the matter and internal correspondence, Reuters said Huang misled general counsel Tim Teter and chief marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld about the relationship before it became public.
The agency also released photos it had verified of the pair together in Taipei in June 2024, adding to images that place them at events since December 2023. Nvidia and a representative for Huang declined to comment, Teter did not respond, and Wagonfeld did not immediately respond.
The report lands two days after Huang resigned as president and chief executive, with chief financial officer Colette Kress taking over on an interim basis, according to Nvidia’s announcement. Alice Huang is a former senior executive of Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer whose dealings in restricted chips are under scrutiny, and Singapore has since barred her from re-entering the country. Despite the shared surname, the two are not related. Huang acknowledged an affair in a statement on 8 November, apologising to his wife, their children and the company without naming her.
Huang called his Alice Huang dealings ‘standard business’ in messages to Nvidia’s leaders
According to Reuters, the questions first reached Nvidia’s leadership through the press. Queries in autumn 2025 and again in October 2026 about Huang’s dealings with Megaspeed and Alice Huang drew the attention of senior executives. On both occasions, Huang described the interactions as appropriate. In two separate messages in October, which Reuters reviewed, he said they reflected “standard business dealings with customers”.
Reuters did not review the 2025 messages, and it did not publish the October exchanges in full. Its sources said that in other messages, Huang also affirmed that his interactions with Megaspeed were routine. The agency did not say whether any executive questioned his account at the time, or when Teter and Wagonfeld learned the true nature of the relationship.
The New York Times’s October 2025 article on the pair’s public meetings drew a sharper response. Huang discussed taking legal action against the paper with Nvidia leaders, according to Reuters’ sources, although neither he nor the company filed a lawsuit. A Times spokesperson told Reuters the paper had received no legal demand. At that stage, Reuters reported, Huang did not describe the relationship as an affair.
Verified photos place Huang and Alice Huang together from December 2023
Reuters said it could not establish when the relationship became intimate. Photos it verified online show the two together in the United States, China and elsewhere from December 2023. One image, confirmed by a Reuters source, was taken in Taipei and released on 7 June 2024, the week of the Computex trade show, where Huang gave the opening keynote. According to The Standard in Hong Kong, the Taipei set shows Alice Huang beside him as he greeted supporters after the keynote, with the pair later posing arm in arm.
Those images follow an earlier set that the Financial Times reported on 9 November. They had been posted on a WeChat account belonging to Alice Huang, who also goes by Huang Le. The images showed the pair at dinners and events in Shanghai, California and Hong Kong, and the account has since been disabled. TalkEsport has not republished any of the photos.
The national security question behind the scandal is still open. US authorities investigated whether Alice Huang was spying for China, and Beijing denies that she is a spy. Reuters said it had not independently verified whether she worked for the Chinese government. Huang told Bloomberg in an interview on 29 October that the US government had not told him about any suspicions. Nvidia’s board has said it has “no reason to believe” national security or the company’s secrets were compromised.
Nvidia’s investigators now have Huang’s own messages to weigh
Nvidia’s independent directors hired Wachtell Lipton and former federal prosecutor Joon Kim on 10 November, according to the board’s own statement. The board has not said what the review covers beyond Huang’s conduct. Reuters’ account adds a specific question for it, because a chief executive’s assurances to the general counsel shape how a company answers the press and regulators.
Reuters’ report is the latest in a run of disclosures since Huang left. The New York Times has reported a relationship with an Nvidia employee, and Reuters reported a separate one with a different employee, as TalkEsport covered in its report on the third relationship. The New York Post has described outbursts at senior executives, including Jay Puri, while two large shareholders have asked the board to keep his return on the table.
Investors have already priced in much of the damage. Nvidia’s shares have fallen more than 30% from their closing high on 6 October, erasing more than $1.8 trillion in market value, according to Reuters. Nvidia reports its third-quarter results on 17 November, the first since Huang’s resignation, and it filed his exit with US regulators in an 8-K.
The post Jensen Huang Told Nvidia’s Top Lawyer His Alice Huang Ties Were ‘Standard Business’, Reuters Reports appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Kronten Files FIR Against TAG Manager, Plays Jonathan’s Father Call and Claims ₹2 Crore Home Help
items.content:
GodLike Esports co-owner Chetan “Kronten” Chandgude has filed an FIR against a Team Apex Gaming (TAG) manager he previously accused of spying on GodLike. He also played two recordings on a live stream that he says back up his account of Jonathan’s exit. In the 72-minute stream on his Kronten Gaming YouTube channel on Saturday evening, he claimed that he gave Jonathan ₹2 crore to buy a home soon after he joined GodLike. He said he also arranged a 4BHK flat in Kharghar, Navi Mumbai, at a below-market rate through a builder. TalkEsport has not seen the FIR, and Jonathan, TAG and the manager have not issued a formal response to the new claims.
The stream follows through on what Kronten promised a week earlier. In his first broadcast on 7 November, he said an FIR had been registered without saying against whom, as TalkEsport reported in its breakdown of that stream. He also called an unnamed manager a “spy” inside GodLike, and said he would play a recording of a Christmas call about a “50-50” split “when the time comes”. Jonathan has since called the earlier allegations “completely wrong”. According to Indian esports insiders, the manager named in the FIR is now part of TAG, as are former GodLike player Hades and creator Sharkshe.
Kronten’s live stream from 14 November. Video: Kronten Gaming/YouTube
Kronten’s Christmas recording centres on a demand for half of GodLike
The longer of the two recordings runs to about 13 minutes and is dated 25 December 2025, in the early hours of the morning in Kharghar. Kronten said he had called Jonathan to wish him a happy Christmas after two to three months without contact. Jonathan’s father returned the call, and Kronten said someone with him recorded it for safety. On the recording, Kronten tells the father that Jonathan’s 33% stake in GodLike is not going anywhere. He then offers to raise it to 50% if he is repaid for the four years of funding he says he put in.
The two men then disagree about who owns the company. According to the recording, Jonathan’s father argues that GodLike would have four partners, while Kronten insists that the partners are Jonathan, co-owner Amar and himself. Kronten also warns that he will make the split public if the dispute escalates. At one point the father defends his son’s value to the organisation. “What Jonathan did, nobody else can do,” he says.
Kronten used the rest of the segment to dispute the idea that Jonathan carried GodLike. He claimed that Jonathan’s salary rose steadily over three years, from the ₹80,000 a month he said Jonathan was paid on joining, and that he also provided the ₹2 crore and the Kharghar flat. He said Jonathan had taken about ₹70 lakh from him in total, including interest, that GodLike is still loss-making, and that he is willing to share bank statements. He dismissed reports of ₹100 crore brand deals, and claimed that Jonathan never followed GodLike or Amar on social media, mentioned the organisation in his bio or wore its jersey at events.
Hades’s recording describes a meeting in Goa and a leaked phone number
The second recording features Hades, and Kronten said it was made with his permission. In it, Hades describes a conversation outside the Marriott hotel in Goa. He claims someone there said, “We have access to everything”, and added that “Johnny is with us too”. The speaker is not named in the clips that have circulated, and TalkEsport cannot verify the conversation.
Hades’s account then turns to his own time abroad. He says that when he was in trouble outside India, he contacted only two people, one of them the manager. The next day, he claims, his phone number reached Sharkshe and then leaked widely. Kronten added that Hades had promised to support him publicly after returning to India, but switched sides once his money problems were settled. Sharkshe has not responded publicly to the claim.
Kronten’s sharpest words were again aimed at the manager. According to Hades, the manager first handled execution work at GodLike, including shoots, stream set-ups and brand data, before being made a manager and introducing himself as Jonathan’s manager. Kronten alleged that the manager stayed with Jonathan around the clock, monitored his plans and checked whether Hades was in contact with him. He also claimed that the manager visited Jonathan’s family every two days, and on one occasion asked them not to tell Kronten about the visit.
Kronten’s evidence has not been tested outside his own stream
An FIR records a complaint and starts a police inquiry, and it is not a finding of wrongdoing. Kronten has not published the FIR itself, and the recordings were played without their full context, so TalkEsport cannot confirm when or how they were made. Clips of Jonathan reacting on his own stream circulated afterwards, although neither he nor TAG has addressed the FIR or the money claims in a statement. GodLike and Team Apex Gaming have not commented on their official accounts.
The same stream has already pulled in a third organisation. Kronten claimed that Scout owns only 2 to 5% of RNTX, which RNTX co-owner Rohit Jagasia rejected, saying Scout owns half of the organisation. The wider row is exactly the kind of livestream-led dispute that TalkEsport argued Indian esports needs a referee for. Claims and counter-claims are being aired on stream long before any of them reach a court or a regulator.
Away from the dispute, Jonathan is still competing. He plays as an assaulter in TAG’s BGMI line-up at the Chennai Esports Global Championship 2026, where Group Stage 2 ends on 16 November. Kronten said on his first stream that more material would become public within about 20 days of 7 November.
The post Kronten Files FIR Against TAG Manager, Plays Jonathan’s Father Call and Claims ₹2 Crore Home Help appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Enthusiast builds a working 486 DX2 retro PC on a breadboard in just 16 days, immediately runs Doom
items.content:
Mark's enthusiasm for computers dampened at an early age by the rubber-keyed Sinclair Spectrum 48K and feelings of Commodore 64 envy. However, in the mid-80s, hope in a digital future was rekindled by the purchase of an Atari 520 STe. Since that time Mark has used a multitude of computers for fun and professional endeavors. He often owned both Macs and PCs but went cold on the former after OS9 was killed off, and warmed to the latter with the introduction of Windows XP.

Early work years were spent in artwork and reprographics but in the late noughties, Mark started to blog about computers, Taiwanese food culture, and guitar design. This activity led to a full-time position writing about breaking PC tech news for HEXUS, for the best part of a decade. When HEXUS was abruptly closed, Mark helped with the foundation of Club386, before finding a new home at Tom's Hardware.

When not wearing through the keycap legends on his PC keyboards, Mark can be found wandering the computer malls of Taiwan's neon-lit conurbations and enjoying local and international cuisine.

items.title: Rainbow Six Y11S4 guide: Operation Vital Signal, events, and ranked changes
items.content:
Rainbow Six Siege (R6 Siege) launches its Year 11 Season 4 (Y11S4) on Dec. 1, and it will run through early March 2027. Ubisoft unveiled new content and gameplay overhauls during the Osaka Major via the traditional reveal panel.
Read on for the full breakdown of R6 Y11S4, including info on Vital Signal, Doc’s operator remaster, returning limited-time event, modernized maps, a DOOM collaboration bundle, and more.
Key takeaways
Year 11 Season 4 in Rainbow Six Siege runs from Dec. 1 to early March 2027. The season is named Operation Vital Signal.
Doc is a remastered operator. He is the final remaster before the game moves to adding four new operators per year.
Bank is a modernized map for this season. It received a strategy update.
The Grand Larceny is a limited-time event returning to R6, bringing items and the atmosphere of the 1920s mafia.
During the winter holidays, you can claim daily rewards in the game, including unique Celebration Packs.
Two playlists are introduced for Ranked matchmaking, focusing on Solo and Duo players so they can compete without five-player teams in the mix.
Thunderbird received an improved Kona Station and a new weapon option, the MBZ-19.
Two shotguns are nerfed: the TCSG12 and ACS12.
A DOOM collaboration comes to Rainbow Six. The details are still a mystery.
A new Social Hub introduces better interactions with in-game friends.
Table of contents
Key takeaways
Operation Vital Signal
Doc remaster
Bank, a modernized R6 Siege map in Year 11 Season 4
DOOM collaboration is coming to R6 Siege
The Grand Larceny: A limited-time event returns to Siege
Winter Daily Rewards event
Half Reinforcements in Testing Grounds
Ranked changes coming in R6 Y11S4
Balancing for Thunderbird
The MBZ-19, a new SMG
Weapon changes
New Social Hub in Rainbow Six Siege
FAQs about Year 11 Season 4 in R6 Siege
Operation Vital Signal
The final content season of 2026 in Rainbow Six Siege is Operation Vital Signal. Here is a list of what’s coming to the game starting on Dec. 1 and up to early March 2027.
Remaster for Doc: New healing gadget for remote activation.
Modernized Bank: Better strategy for attackers on this map.
DOOM collaboration.
Grand Larceny: An iconic event returns.
Winter Daily Rewards with Celebration Packs.
Half Reinforcement: A new gadget for testing.
Ranked changes: Two playlists for Solo / Duo and for mixed teams.
Thunderbird rebalanced: Improved Kona Station.
The MBZ-19: A new SMG for defenders.
Nerfs for shotguns: TCSG12 and ACS12.
New Social Hub.
Y11S4 content in R6 Siege (Image credit: Ubisoft)
The new season traditionally comes with a refreshed Battle Pass track. Here is what to expect from Operation Vital Signal in terms of progression rewards.
Operation Vital Signal Battle Pass in Rainbow Six Siege (Image credit: Ubisoft)
Doc remaster
Doc is the next R6 operator to receive a remastered version for a new season.
E-HEAL Monitor is a new gadget for Doc. With it, you can track the teammates’ health and support them remotely.
If you have a match with Doc, all teammates receive a special patch. When needed, Doc activates healing or reviving through it from a distance.
Self-healing works for Doc, too. The reviving works for a player only once per round.
Additionally, Doc can take a deployable shield to his loadout.
The previous remaster was for Dokkaebi with Operation System Overdrive. However, Doc is the final such update, as starting in 2027, Rainbow Six Siege will get four new operators per year.
Bank, a modernized R6 Siege map in Year 11 Season 4
Following the tradition of refreshing and modernizing maps with each new R6 season, the developers introduce improvements for Bank.
The map has received a targeted update, with a focus on a better-balanced strategic approach for attackers.
DOOM collaboration is coming to R6 Siege
A crossover event with the DOOM franchise will launch in Rainbow Six Siege on Dec. 22. Doom Slayer is coming to the game! He may bring exclusive cosmetics and special missions.
More details will be revealed soon.
The Grand Larceny: A limited-time event returns to Siege
The 1920s mafia-themed event, The Grand Larceny, was part of Year 5 in Rainbow Six Siege. It returns for a new run from Feb. 2 to Feb. 23, 2027.
Only shotguns are in play.
Almost all walls and floors are destructible
Attackers should open a set number of safes to win a match.
Defenders protect stolen goods in their safes.
Event cosmetics during The R6 Grand Larceny (Image credit: Ubisoft)
Winter Daily Rewards event
Starting from Dec. 1 and to Jan. 15, you can receive daily rewards in Rainbow Six Siege. Log in to the game and get various packs with random drops.
Celebration Packs return for this event. The drop pool includes highly hyped Gold Dust and Glacier weapon skins. The T-5 SMG is a new gun with an animated Glacier skin.
T-5 SMG Glacier, a new addition to the R6 skins selection (Image credit: Ubisoft)
Half Reinforcements in Testing Grounds
From Jan. 7 to Jan. 19, the R6 Testing Grounds feature a new gadget, Half Reinforcement. It lets defenders block half of the wall to prevent easy access but still have an open view to shoot approaching attackers.
The gadget takes a spot in your loadout, and the view is an opportunity for attackers as well. These aspects should balance Half Reinforcements.
After the testing period, the gadget may make it to the main game.
Half Reinforcement in Rainbow Six Siege (Image credit: Ubisoft)
Ranked changes coming in R6 Y11S4
Starting from Year 11 Season 4, the ranked mode in Rainbow Six Siege receives some significant adjustments.
Two Ranked playlists: for Solo / Duo players and for everyone, including five-player teams.
Solo / Duo and Flex Ranked playlists in R6 Siege (Image credit: Ubisoft)
This change allows players who join R6 Ranked matchmaking alone or with a friend to avoid facing better-coordinated settled teams of five. It’s a continuation of the Ranked 3.0 development in Rainbow Six Siege.
Players have separate progression in the two new Ranked playlists. As a Solo, you will not be forced into Flex to reduce the queue time, but that may happen with Duos.
This update disables four-player team queues.
Balancing for Thunderbird
The defender operator Thunderbird gets meaningful balance changes in R6 Y11S4.
Her Kona Station can target stunned teammates, remove the effect, and protect them for 1.5 seconds afterwards.
Kona Station will prioritize stunned players over injured ones to bring them to battle quicker.
Thunderbird takes four Kona Stations to a match instead of three. The cooldown between activations has been reduced to 10 seconds instead of 15.
The MBZ-19, a new SMG
This new submachine gun joins the defender arsenal with Y11S4 in R6 Siege. MBZ-19 is available for Thunderbird, Jäger, and Warden.
Damage: 33.
Fire rate: 750 rounds per minute.
Ammo: 64-round magazine.
Weapon changes
Balance adjustments come for the following weapons.
TCSG12 — damage reduced to 50 (from 75).
ACS12 — damage dropped to 45 (from 69); the magazine reduced to 20 rounds (instead of 30). The number of magazines available was increased from 4 to 6.
New Social Hub in Rainbow Six Siege
The game receives an improved Social Hub, with new features for interaction with other players.
See who’s online.
Check who’s available to play.
Send quick invites for a match.
Generate a code and send it to a person you want to be in your squad.
Example of the new R6 Social Hub (Image credit: Ubisoft)
The updated interface also shows random teammates you played with recently. All the Ubisoft Connect and R6 friends will be added to the Social Hub, too.

This phase of the Rainbow Six Siege Major took place in the arena, where the hype is clearly tangible. Witness...

As the season reveals are connected to international R6 Siege esports events, the next panel is scheduled to happen at Invitational 2027 — for Year 12 Season 1. The World Championship takes place in São Paulo, Brazil, from Feb. 1 to Feb. 14.
FAQs about Year 11 Season 4 in R6 Siege
When does Operation Vital Signal start in Rainbow Six Siege?
Operation Vital Signal for Y11S4 starts in Rainbow Six Siege on Dec. 1, 2026. It is scheduled to run up to early March 2027.
What R6 operator receives a remaster for Y11S4?
Doc receives a remaster for Operation Vital Signal Y11S4 in Rainbow Six Siege. His healing gadget has been changed. It’s the E-HEAL Monitor now, with the option for remote healing and revival.
What R6 map was modernized for Y11S4?
Bank received a targeted update for Y11S4 in Rainbow Six Siege. It is focused on improved attacking strategy.
What is the Grand Larceny event?
The Grand Larceny is a limited-time event in Rainbow Six Siege. It is themed around the 1920s mafia and introduces shotgun-only matches with breakable floors and walls, where teams should loot or protect safes.
What R6 operator got balance adjustments for Y11S4?
Thunderbird is the R6 operator rebalanced for Y11S4. She got an improved Kona Station and a new weapon option, the MBZ-19.

items.title: GTA 6 Physical Copies Arriving Without Codes or With Used Ones, Buyers Say
items.content:
Some players who picked up physical copies of Grand Theft Auto VI this week say their boxes arrived with no download code inside, or with a code that had already been redeemed. Because the boxed edition contains no disc, a missing or used code leaves them without a copy of the game four days before its 19 November launch. Reports have come from buyers in the US and Europe, and a fan account that tracks the game says Xbox owners are now affected as well as PlayStation owners. Rockstar Games has not commented publicly on the reports, and nobody knows yet how many copies are involved.
The timing makes the problem harder to ignore. Boxed copies went on sale at retailers on 12 November so that buyers could redeem their codes and start the 212GB pre-load ahead of launch. According to Rockstar’s support page, “codes can be used as soon as they are received”, which means anyone stuck with a dead box is already falling behind players who bought digitally.
Grand Theft Auto VI is now only one week away!
Thank you to everyone in the community for your incredible support.
There’s still time to pre-order and pre-load so you’re ready on launch day.
Code-in-box versions are also available now for pick-up at retailers worldwide. pic.twitter.com/au3uAf6p5w
— Rockstar Games (@RockstarGames) November 12, 2026
Buyers say some sealed boxes held no code, and others held a used one
The complaints from buyers fall into two broad groups so far. Some buyers say they opened a sealed case and found an empty space, or a grey strip, where the code card should have been, according to GSMDome. Others say the code was there but had already been redeemed by someone else when they tried to use it. One social media post claimed that Rockstar support closed a ticket after a player reported a missing code, although that claim has not been verified.
A second theory explains how a sealed code could already be used. According to posts in a Reddit thread cited by TechJuice and GamingHQ, the code is printed on the case cover itself rather than on a separate insert. In PEGI regions such as the UK and Europe it is reportedly left fully exposed, while North American packaging obscures it. A fan account claimed on 13 November that the code could be read through the shrink-wrap with a strong light, which would let someone copy it and leave the box on the shelf. GSMDome notes that there is no evidence this is a common theft method, and none of the reports shows a widespread manufacturing fault.
Several buyers also say retailers refused to swap or refund boxes that turned out to be empty or already used, GamingHQ reported. Rockstar has not announced a separate fix for affected retail copies. Its own pre-order support FAQ sends questions about copies bought elsewhere back to the retailer, while boxed orders from the Rockstar Store are handled by its payment partner, Xsolla.
Without a disc, a missing code means no game at all
Rockstar confirmed months ago that “a disc will not be included in the box”. The standard physical edition holds a single code for the game and the Vintage Vice City Pack, and there is no physical Ultimate Edition. Take-Two chief executive Strauss Zelnick has defended the decision, saying the publisher’s business is “well over 90% digital” and that retail still matters as a marketing channel, which “is why we offer code-in-a-box”.
That reasoning holds up only while the code works. With a disc, a buyer can still install and play the game even if a voucher is lost or damaged. With a code in a box, the code is the game, so any fault in packing, storage or retail handling hits players directly. Region rules add one more catch for anyone buying a box. Rockstar says PlayStation codes must match the country of the player’s account, while Xbox codes are not region-locked, and PlayStation codes sold in Japan expire 170 days after issue.
The problem also lands in the busiest week of the game’s long build-up. Take-Two has put the price at $70 to $80, and reviews are due a day before launch under the 18 November embargo. Players who planned to start the moment the game unlocks in their region now have less time to sort out a faulty box.
Check the box before you leave the store, and redeem the code at once
Rockstar has not issued specific advice for this problem, but its existing support pages point to a few sensible steps. Inspect the case and its shrink-wrap before leaving the store, and open it at the counter if the retailer allows it. Keep the receipt and the packaging, and take photos as soon as you open the box, which GSMDome also recommends. Buying from a retailer in the same country as your PlayStation account avoids region problems, as Rockstar’s support page advises.
Redeem the code straight away rather than leaving it in the case until launch day. On PS5, codes are entered through the PlayStation Store’s Redeem Code option, and Xbox owners can use Microsoft’s redeem page. If a code is missing or already used, contact the retailer first, since Rockstar directs retail purchase problems there, and submit a request through Rockstar Support as well. Boxes sold as “sealed” on resale marketplaces carry the same risk, with less chance of a refund.
Rockstar has given no figure for how many boxed copies have been sold, or how many may be affected. Digital pre-load opened on 10 November, and players who redeemed a working code have been downloading the 212GB install since, a rush big enough to set a broadband record at Virgin Media in the UK. The game launches on 19 November on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
The post GTA 6 Physical Copies Arriving Without Codes or With Used Ones, Buyers Say appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: GTA 6 Has Made $1.18 Billion Before Launch, and It Still May Not Save Console Sales
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto VI has not launched yet, but it is already one of the biggest entertainment releases of 2026. Sensor Tower estimates that the game had taken about 12.1 million digital pre-orders across PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S by the morning of 13 November, worth roughly $1.18 billion. Those figures come from the analytics firm’s public GTA VI sales tracker, and neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has confirmed a pre-order count. Take-Two has, however, said that demand is running well ahead of its own plans.
The game unlocks on 19 November, with the standard edition priced at $80, and the launch times for every region are already set. Pre-loading opened on 10 November, according to Rockstar, and the PS5 download weighs 212GB. That download alone was enough to set a traffic record at Virgin Media in the UK. The size of the launch is now shaping what rival publishers, console makers and players do this month.
Sensor Tower’s GTA 6 estimate has climbed by $430 million in ten days
The pace of the run-up is what stands out. Sensor Tower’s tracker put pre-orders at about 7.71 million copies and $751 million on 3 November, then at 10.31 million copies and roughly $1 billion on 11 November. Two days later, the estimate had reached 12.1 million copies and $1.18 billion. In its recent breakdowns, PS5 accounted for about three quarters of all copies, with Xbox Series X|S taking the rest.
Take-Two’s own language has been just as bullish. Reporting second-quarter results on 9 November, the company said GTA VI pre-orders were “tracking far above our initial expectations”, while chief executive Strauss Zelnick said they were “continuing to reach unprecedented levels”. Take-Two kept its full-year net bookings forecast of $8.0 billion to $8.2 billion, and guided for $3.35 billion to $3.5 billion in the quarter that includes the launch, according to its earnings release. Net bookings in the second quarter itself fell 18% to $1.6 billion, which shows how much of the company’s year now rests on one game.
Fortune noted that $1.18 billion is already more than the roughly $1.01 billion that The Super Mario Galaxy Movie has grossed worldwide this year. Analysts have estimated that Take-Two spent between $1 billion and $1.5 billion developing GTA VI, so pre-orders are already in the same range as that budget. Sensor Tower’s figure is gross consumer spending before platform fees, however, so Take-Two’s own share of that money is smaller.
Rockstar’s official launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI.
Console prices could blunt GTA 6’s boost to hardware sales
The bigger question is whether GTA VI can lift console sales the way earlier blockbusters did, and analysts quoted by Forbes are doubtful. US hardware spending fell 9% to $2.9 billion between January and September, according to Circana data cited in that report, and Xbox Series sales were down 27% year on year as of September. Louise Woolridge of Ampere Analysis said GTA VI will “definitely give console sales a boost, but I don’t think it will be enough to reverse the year-on-year decline”. Circana’s Mat Piscatella called it the “biggest video game launch of all time”, although he expects most new console buyers to come from wealthier households.
Price is the main obstacle for anyone who still needs a console. Sony raised the US price of the PS5 to $649.99 from 2 April, with the Digital Edition at $599.99 and the PS5 Pro at $899.99, citing “continued pressures in the global economic landscape” in its announcement. Microsoft was more direct when it raised Xbox prices again from 1 August. “Console storage and memory prices have increased by more than 2.5x and we expect another doubling by the fall of 2027,” the company said on Xbox Wire.
TalkEsport has tracked the same squeeze across PC hardware, as AI data centres absorb more of the world’s memory supply. AMD has cut Radeon allocations in China by up to 50%, and Nvidia reportedly cancelled a 24GB RTX 5080 over the cost of its memory modules. Valve’s Steam Machine launched at $879 for similar reasons. Rhys Elliot of Alinea Analytics told Forbes that a new console and the game together could cost “$580 to $1,000+”, and he sees no relief in the memory crunch until at least 2029.
Rivals are already fighting GTA 6 for storage space and players’ time
The 212GB install is a problem for every other game on a player’s console. A launch PS5 offers about 667GB of usable storage, so GTA VI alone takes up close to a third of it. EA has clearly noticed, since the official Madden NFL account warned players on 10 November not to “let 210GB get between you and Your League”. Madden NFL 27 is now also showing an in-game “Don’t delete!” message, which teases a “high-stakes run” with a signal due on 17 November, two days before GTA VI unlocks.
Many players are also clearing their calendars for launch day. In a YouGov poll commissioned by PCMag and run in late October, 8% of 2,024 US adults said they planned to take time off work or school, or rearrange their schedules, to play the game. That works out to about 12.5 million people, and the share rose to 13% among Gen Z respondents. Another 7% said they planned to buy a console to play it, while a separate survey of nearly 1,500 users by the key marketplace G2A found that 29% had already asked for time off.
Review scores will land first, with the review embargo lifting on 18 November, a day before launch. Rockstar and Take-Two have not said when they will share official sales figures for GTA VI. Take-Two’s next scheduled results, covering the October to December quarter and the launch itself, are due in early 2027.

items.title: Rockstar Says GTA 6 Is the First GTA to Encourage Empathy, and a Criminal Profile Will Track Your Violence
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto VI will give players ways to show empathy for the first time in the series’ history, according to Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North. “We’ve tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to,” Nelson told The Guardian. The paper’s games editor, Keza MacDonald, visited the studio in Edinburgh ahead of the game’s 19 November launch. Asked directly whether GTA 6 encourages empathy, he tied it to the plot rather than to a rulebook. “I would say that it’s a product of the story we’re trying to tell,” he said.
That story belongs to Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, whom Nelson described as “a younger couple with their backs against the wall”. The systems are optional, and many of them are small. Jason can ask a passer-by for permission before petting their dog, for example, and people on the street react when the player interrupts their conversations. None of this replaces the series’ usual chaos, although it gives players who want a gentler run through Leonida something to work with, a shift that has been building since Rockstar’s first trailer and reveal.
Jason and Lucia’s relationship is the system Rockstar is betting on
The biggest of those mechanics is the relationship itself. When they are apart, Jason and Lucia call and text each other, and when they are together they can go on dates to the gym, a bar or a meditation retreat. A liquor store stick-up also counts as a date, and a dedicated button lets the pair hold hands. “The relationship is yours to nurture or yours to lose,” Nelson said, adding that whether it stays romantic is up to the player.
Neglecting the relationship has consequences, according to the preview, although Rockstar has not said how far they go. Players who have no interest in romance can ignore the system entirely. They can switch between Jason and Lucia for most of the game, while some story moments lock players into one character’s perspective for a stretch. Rockstar’s second trailer leaned heavily on the same partnership, and it remains the clearest official look at the pair together.
Grand Theft Auto VI Trailer 2. Video: Rockstar Games
Jason and Lucia also start out as small-time criminals. Early on, they can only hotwire cheap cars and pick basic locks, and bigger jobs come later in the story. Before a robbery, players can scout the location, find a back door or a safe code, and disable security cameras or take their footage. In the demo Rockstar showed the press, a jewellery store robbery without that preparation ended with a guard opening fire and a police chase across half a district.
Jason and Lucia start out as small-time criminals in Leonida. Image: Rockstar Games
A Criminal Profile tracks players who go beyond what is necessary
Crime, Nelson said, is still “a fundamental part of GTA”, although he added “at least up until now, it has been”. Rockstar is “trying to make sure we’re not punishing people for playing the game they are used to”, he said, while promising that “your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out”. Players can still cause traffic jams, shove pedestrians and flee the scene of an accident.
What changes the picture is a new system called the Criminal Profile. It tracks how violent and malicious a player’s crimes are, in a similar way to the honour system in Red Dead Redemption 2, and it is not a simple good or bad meter. A hit-and-run or an escape before the police arrive is fine, according to Nelson. The problems start “when you go beyond what is necessary on a consistent basis”, he said, and Rockstar has not said whether the profile changes missions, rewards or the ending.
Rockstar chose ‘big swings’ over a quicker GTA 5.5
Rockstar could have released a “GTA 5.5” and done it faster, executive Jennifer Kolbe suggested in the interview, but the studio chose a bigger rebuild. Nelson said the studio had to “take big swings”, because the sequel “can’t be just more of the same”. The research behind Leonida began with trips to Miami in 2015, and Nelson said he visited clubs, spent time in bars in the Florida Keys and rode along with police officers through South Beach. That research shows in how closely Leonida’s streets resemble real Miami.
The same attention to detail reaches the smallest moments of play. In the press demo, Jason ate a doughnut while drinking a beer, and a six-pack he carried sloshed as he ran. Players can also spot birds through binoculars and log them in a wildlife logbook that holds 62 species. MacDonald described the game as “gratuitously, absurdly detailed, from the macro level to the micro”.
Players will be able to test those systems within days. Pre-loading has been open since 10 November and needs about 212GB of free space, while reviews are due on 18 November. Unlock times have been set for every region, and Take-Two has put the price at $70 to $80. Grand Theft Auto VI launches on 19 November on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, 13 years after Grand Theft Auto V.
The post Rockstar Says GTA 6 Is the First GTA to Encourage Empathy, and a Criminal Profile Will Track Your Violence appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Steam Now Shows Real Average FPS for Thousands of Steam Deck Games, and Desktop PCs Are Next
items.content:
Steam store pages now show the average frame rate that players actually get in thousands of games on Steam Deck, and Valve has started asking desktop PC users to share the same data. “With today’s update, you can now see the average framerate players get in games on Steam Deck,” Valve said in its Steam Deck Framerate announcement, which went live late on 9 November. The figure sits in the Steam Deck Compatibility section of each store page, under “Learn more”, with a histogram behind it. Valve calls the Deck rollout “a stepping stone toward providing framerate data for more devices than just Steam Deck”, although it has given no date for desktop PCs.
The feature has been months in the making. TalkEsport reported in April that Steam was testing FPS estimates in its client beta, with Valve saying at the time that it would “focus on devices running SteamOS”. That beta is what now feeds the public numbers. Some posts circulating this weekend suggest Steam already estimates performance for any PC, but the store data so far covers Steam Deck only, and desktop collection is still at the opt-in stage.
Steam’s frame rate numbers come from opted-in players on default settings
The average is “calculated using data from customers who have opted in to providing framerate data,” Valve said. The setting sits under Steam’s account settings, in the Data and Browsing section, as Anonymous Game Framerate Data, and the Steam library prompts players to switch it on. The data comes from the same frame rate reporting tool Valve built for developers, who have been able to see similar figures for their own games in Steamworks for months. A game needs a minimum number of samples before its figure appears.
Valve also limits which players’ numbers count towards the average. Only Decks running the default frame limit contribute, which means 60fps on the LCD model and 90fps on the OLED model, and the data does not account for custom graphics settings or power limits. That sounds like a weakness, but once the effect of vertical sync is taken into account, Valve says it has “found that the framerate data consolidates around relatively narrow ranges”. Every Deck uses the same AMD chip design and a 1280×800 screen, so one game’s numbers from thousands of players can be compared directly.
The histogram matters more than the headline figure. An average of 45fps can hide a game that swings between 60fps in menus and 25fps in combat, while the distribution shows how much time is spent at each frame rate. Stutters and hitches appear as small columns at the low end of the chart. One limit remains, however: an average cannot show whether frames were rendered by the GPU or created by frame generation, and it is not yet clear how Valve treats generated frames.
Deck Verified badges were not enough, Valve admits
Valve’s reason for publishing the data is a candid one. Its Deck Verified programme rates games against fixed criteria, and Valve says that testing “may not match every customer’s bar for acceptable gameplay”. A game can be Verified while running at 30fps, which some players accept and others do not. The new figures cover games rated Verified, Playable and Unsupported, so buyers can now see performance even where Valve’s badge says little.
For buyers, this changes the way people check performance before paying. Until now, the safest test was to buy a game and rely on Steam’s refund policy. That allows refunds within 14 days of purchase, as long as the game has been played for under two hours. Real averages from thousands of players also make poor ports harder to hide. A studio that ships a game running at 20fps on Deck will now see that number on its own store page.
The numbers are only as good as the opt-in rate, however. Valve says a majority of Deck players have already agreed to share data, although smaller games may take time to reach the sample threshold. Thousands of games already have data, Valve says, and that number will grow as more players opt in.
Desktop PCs are much harder to measure than a Steam Deck
The desktop rollout is where the feature gets difficult. A new Steam Client Beta asks desktop users to opt in to sharing anonymised frame rate data, and Valve says the prompt will reach everyone later. Unlike the Steam Deck, desktop PCs come in thousands of processor, graphics card, memory and resolution combinations, with different drivers and settings on top. Valve has not said whether it will group results by graphics card, by processor or by complete systems.
Valve already has a map of that hardware. Its monthly Hardware and Software Survey tracks which graphics cards and processors Steam users own, so the company knows which configurations are common enough to produce reliable averages. An obvious starting point would be the most popular graphics cards, although Valve has not confirmed any plan. It has also not said whether its own Steam Machine, which runs SteamOS on fixed hardware, will be the next device to get its own figures.
Desktop data would land at a useful moment for PC buyers. Memory costs have pushed up hardware prices this year. AMD has cut Radeon supply in China and Nvidia has reportedly cancelled a 24GB RTX 5080, so knowing whether an existing card can run a new game matters more. The data is anonymised and opt-in, a point Valve will need to keep clear after a data breach at one of its logistics partners. Valve is taking feedback in the comments on its announcement, and it has not given a timeline for the wider rollout.
The post Steam Now Shows Real Average FPS for Thousands of Steam Deck Games, and Desktop PCs Are Next appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: League Next Is Now League of Legends: New Dawn, With a New Client and a Rebuilt Summoner’s Rift
items.content:
Riot Games has given the biggest overhaul in League of Legends history a name. The project known until now as League Next will arrive as League of Legends: New Dawn, Riot confirmed in a two-minute teaser shown during the Worlds 2026 grand final. It promises a modernised client, a visually rebuilt Summoner’s Rift, gameplay changes and new ways to play champions. Riot says the full reveal comes in January, with the release itself later in 2027.
The reveal landed during the final itself, which Bilibili Gaming went on to win 3-1 against Gen.G at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, with Knight named Finals MVP. BLG reached the Worlds 2026 grand final by ending T1’s bid for a fourth straight title, and the full bracket is on our Worlds 2026 wiki page. Riot had promised in July that Worlds would include “a little peek” at its plans for 2027 and beyond, according to its dev update at the time.
League of Legends: New Dawn teaser. Video: Riot Games
Riot’s teaser promises a new client, a rebuilt Summoner’s Rift and a 2027 release
The teaser features executive producer Paul “Pabro” Bellezza and Andrei “Meddler” van Roon, head of the League studio. “The client, for one, has to be better,” Bellezza says, before confirming that “next year, we’re releasing a modernised client.” Van Roon then widens the scope. “A client isn’t enough,” he says, adding that Riot is “updating a lot” across the game.
The footage backs that up with a first look at redesigned jungle camps, objectives and environment art on Summoner’s Rift. Ahri, Jhin, Sett, Lux, Blitzcrank, Leona and Volibear all appear across the cinematic and gameplay shots. Riot has not yet explained the gameplay changes behind those visuals, however. Some viewers have read the footage as showing new entrances to the Dragon pit, but Riot has not confirmed any change to objectives.
A few early reports said New Dawn launches in January, but that is not what Riot has announced. The description on the official teaser says the “full reveal” comes in January, with the “release later in 2027”. Players can already sign up for updates on Riot’s New Dawn site, although it currently carries little beyond the name and a subscription form.
New Dawn rebuilds League from the inside instead of replacing it with a sequel
New Dawn is an update to the existing game, not the League of Legends 2 that players have speculated about for years. Bloomberg first reported the project in December 2025, saying most of the League team had moved onto it. Riot responded within a day with a video in which Bellezza and van Roon said the answer to a sequel “remains, no”. They set out the plan instead: retire the current launcher, build the navigation client into the game engine, overhaul Summoner’s Rift and redesign runes and other pre-game systems.
The client change is the most technical item on that list. Today, the client players use to queue, buy skins and pick champions runs as a separate program from the game itself, a design that dates from 2016, when Riot began replacing its old Adobe Air launcher. Building those menus into the engine would remove the hand-off between two programs that players sit through before every match, although Riot has not yet shown it working. A new client was also the first item Riot listed in its January dev update, alongside a revamped Summoner’s Rift and a new player experience.
The scale invites comparison with Riot’s past rebuilds. Summoner’s Rift last received a full visual update in 2014, and runes and masteries were merged into Runes Reforged in 2017. Van Roon put the goal plainly in the teaser. “We want League to stand the test of time and be a game that’s here for many years to come,” he says.
Riot is pulling League in two directions in the same year. In July it launched League of Legends Classic, a Season 3-style Summoner’s Rift with 60 champions on their old kits, built into the current client. New Dawn points the other way, towards a game that looks and plays like a modern release. Riot has not said how Classic will work once the client is rebuilt.
Engine, hardware and skins remain open questions until January
Riot has confirmed far less than the teaser suggests. It has not said whether New Dawn uses a new rendering engine or an upgrade of the existing one, and it has not published minimum PC specifications. That matters for a game whose modest hardware demands have long let it run on older laptops and in internet cafés. Mac support, which League offers today, has not been addressed either.
The other big unknown is what happens to players’ collections and progression. League has more than 170 champions, and Riot has not said how existing skins will be adapted to the new visual style. Because New Dawn is an update and not a new game, players would expect to keep their accounts, but Riot has given no detail on ranked, rune pages or progression. Nothing has been said about Wild Rift, the separate mobile version, either.
The January reveal is where Riot has promised those answers, and the competitive calendar will need them too. Pro teams will have to adjust if a rebuilt Summoner’s Rift lands in the middle of the 2027 season, and Riot has not said where in the year the release falls. League of Legends launched in October 2009, and Bloomberg described New Dawn as the most significant overhaul since then.
The post League Next Is Now League of Legends: New Dawn, With a New Client and a Rebuilt Summoner’s Rift appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Jonathan’s Team Apex Gaming Reportedly in Final Talks for a New BGMI Roster After CEGC 2026
items.content:
Team Apex Gaming (TAG), the organisation founded by Jonathan “Jonathan” Amaral, is in final discussions to sign a new Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI) roster, according to a report shared by Indian esports insiders on 14 November. The Chennai Esports Global Championship (CEGC) 2026 is expected to be the current line-up’s last tournament, with an official announcement to follow once the event is over. TAG itself has not yet commented on the report. If it is confirmed, the change would come only days after one of the organisation’s founders said the current players were signed for a year.
That founder was Shreeman Legend, who dismissed rumours of a disbandment on his stream on 12 November. He said the line-up was “signed for one year” and that he had heard nothing directly suggesting a change. He also said TAG would play CEGC 2026 with the same players, which the new report does not dispute, since it places any change after the tournament. Neither TAG nor Shreeman has explained how a new signing would fit with the one-year deal he described.
TAG has reportedly approached line-ups led by Omega, Saumraj and Punkk
A second report, citing sources, went further and named the players involved. It said TAG was in advanced talks with the line-up led by in-game leader (IGL) Omega, and that the discussions were going well, although Omega had yet to give his final confirmation. Offers had also gone to other line-ups, including Saumraj’s, while a new roster built around Punkk was described as a last-resort option. The same report said the exit of TAG’s current line-up, known as Team Jelly after its IGL, was confirmed for after CEGC 2026.
All three IGLs are playing at CEGC 2026 with their own teams. Omega captains Team Outrage, which finished first in Group Stage 1 with 278 points and went straight to the Upper Bracket. Omega’s main four at the event also includes slug, knightū and ninjaboi, so a deal for the whole line-up would bring in the Group Stage 1 leaders. Saumraj leads K9 Esports and Punkk captains VR1 Esports, and both teams finished outside the top eight. None of the three players or their teams has commented on the reports, and TalkEsport has not independently confirmed any of the talks.
TAG’s current line-up is still fighting for an Upper Bracket place at CEGC 2026
TAG’s current roster is led by IGL Jellly, with Jonathan, Hydrooo and Harsh05 in the main four and KioLmao as a substitute, according to the rosters registered for CEGC 2026. The team finished 15th in Group Stage 1 with 194 points, which sent it into Group Stage 2 instead of straight to the Upper Bracket. Group Stage 2 runs until 16 November, and only its top eight teams join the Upper Bracket, while the rest drop into the Lower Bracket. Partway through the second stage, TAG was sitting close to that top-eight line.
Either way, the current line-up’s run could last for weeks. The Lower Bracket is played on 21 and 22 November, followed by a Last Chance Qualifier from 27 to 29 November. The 16-team Grand Finals take place at a LAN in Chennai from 11 to 13 December. The tournament carries a ₹75 lakh prize pool. If TAG reaches the finals and the announcement waits for the end of the event, the new roster may not be confirmed until mid-December.
Jonathan has expanded TAG quickly since leaving GodLike in April
Jonathan left GodLike Esports in April and launched TAG the same month, with Shreeman among its founding members. This month alone, the organisation has signed EA FC Mobile players DeMYSTeRIO and HaloZeus and grandmaster Vidit Gujrathi, its first chess player. It also fields a team in the PUBG India Challenge 2026. Jonathan, whose YouTube channel has more than 8 million subscribers, still plays in the BGMI line-up as an assaulter.
The roster reports also arrive in the middle of Jonathan’s public dispute with GodLike owner Chetan “Kronten” Chandgude. In early November, Kronten made a series of claims about Jonathan’s time at GodLike, which Jonathan called “completely wrong” in his first spoken response on 12 November. A new roster would be TAG’s biggest BGMI move since its launch. Team Jelly plays its final Group Stage 2 matches on 16 November.

items.title: Razer expands Soma lineup with Soma Pro and Soma Sensa HD Haptics chairs
items.content:
Razer has expanded its Soma gaming chair lineup with the new Soma Pro and Soma Sensa HD Haptics. Following the introduction of the Soma Chroma, both new models add Razer's Sensa HD Haptics technology directly into the seat, while the flagship Soma Pro also includes built-in THX Spatial Audio speakers and Chroma RGB lighting.
Both Soma Pro and Soma Sensa HD Haptics use six haptic actuators that translate in-game action into physical feedback through the chair. Feedback changes based on the distance, direction and intensity of what's happening on screen. The system is managed through Razer Synapse and can also convert audio into haptic feedback for films, music and games without native support.
While the Soma Sensa HD Haptics is built around Razer's haptic technology, the Soma Pro combines haptics with built-in THX Spatial Audio speakers and Razer Chroma RGB lighting. The speakers can be used on their own or as part of a wider audio setup, while Chroma support enables reactive lighting effects across more than 300 compatible games.
Both chairs feature a built-in lumbar arch, dual-density cold-cured foam cushioning and a reclining backrest. An integrated control panel allows users to adjust haptic settings and manage wireless connectivity. The Soma Pro further adds 4D armrests, a magnetic head cushion, a frog tilt mechanism and a powder-coated aluminium alloy wheelbase. Power is supplied through a single USB-C connection, while wireless connectivity is handled via Razer HyperSpeed Wireless (2.4GHz) or Bluetooth LE.
The Razer Soma Sensa HD Haptics is available now for £569.99/$569.99/€589.99, while the Soma Pro retails for £999.99/$999.99/€1029.99.
KitGuru says: Would you want haptic feedback built into your gaming chair, or is audio alone enough to create an immersion?

items.title: FURIA Crushes Spirit to Win BLAST Rivals Season 2
items.content:
FURIA is the winner of BLAST Rivals Season 2 2026, beating Spirit with a 3-0 scoreline as it secured another premier Counter-Strike 2 trophy ahead of the highly anticipated PGL Major. Coming into the event, this FURIA side bested all the top dogs, starting with Vitality in the quarterfinals, followed by Falcons in the semi-finals, and finally a clean sweep of Team Spirit to bag the lion’s share of a million dollars.
With all 8 of the top teams in the world making an appearance, FURIA displayed dominance in all the stages of the tournament as it cruised past all its opponents, dropping a single map throughout the entirety of the tournament. Starting the event with a convincing win over Brazilian side Legacy, the biggest surprise came against Vitality, where it completed a reverse sweep to reach the semi-finals, where it made quick work of Falcons to reach the Grand Finals against Spirit.
FURIA dominates Spirit in the Grand Finals
YOUR BLAST PREMIER RIVALS HONG KONG CHAMPIONS, @FURIA #BLASTPremier #MMarkEvents pic.twitter.com/XrlQAPARRy
— BLAST Premier (@BLASTPremier) November 15, 2026
A closely tied first half saw FURIA and Spirit trade blows, with the first half concluding with a levelled scoreline. FURIA raced ahead in the second half, leaving Spirit to play chase. As Spirit continued to trail with little difference in the scoreline, the Brazilian side managed to edge out a close scoreline.
Taking home the opening map, FURIA let Spirit have the momentum to start Dust 2. Despite the poor start, the FURIA offence recovered late in the half to close with a respectable 7-5 lead. Switching sides at a deficit, FURIA pulled off a perfect defence, winning 6 rounds in a row to close out the second map with a dominant 13-5 scoreline as it hit series point.
With the score at 2-0, Spirit managed to push FURIA to the edge. The first half of the final map failed to separate the two sides. Starting the second half with a 6-0 streak, FURIA hit map point, and while Spirit did pull in a few rounds, the big lead allowed it to drop a few and close out the map with a dominant 3-0 series win.
Molodoy on the AWP proved to be a pivotal figure in FURIA’s conquest. Besting the likes of m0NESY, ZywOo, and finally sh1ro, he is slowly making his name as a star of the professional Counter-Strike landscape, if he isn’t one already. While KSCERATO’s 1.68 IR put him at the top of the chart, molodoy’s performance went beyond statistics to help his side close the game.
With this win, FURIA has made a strong case for itself as it challenges for the title of the best team in the world. Bucharest had several top sides missing, but now that it has beaten everyone in Hong Kong, it will be very hard to argue that FURIA is not the best team coming into the Major later this month.

CachyOS has earned a following among Linux enthusiasts and PC gamers thanks to its focus on performance, but the distro's Arch Linux foundations can still feel intimidating for newcomers. In a preview shared on X, the developers showed off the new Package Installer 2.0 interface. items.title: beyerdynamic launches limited all-black Pro X studio headphones
items.content:
beyerdynamic has announced limited all-black versions of four of its Pro X studio headphones. The DT 770 Pro X, DT 990 Pro X, DT 700 Pro X and DT 900 Pro X are all getting the new look, complete with black velour ear pads, while keeping the same specifications as their standard counterparts.
The all-black design originated from a practical studio requirement rather than a simple cosmetic update. As with the standard models, the closed-back DT 770 Pro X Limited Black Edition and DT 700 Pro X Limited Black Edition are designed for recording, monitoring, production and focused mixing work, while the open-back DT 990 Pro X Limited Black Edition and DT 900 Pro X Limited Black Edition are intended for critical listening, editing, mixing and mastering. Pricing starts at €199 for the DT 770 Pro X and DT 990 Pro X models, while the DT 700 Pro X and DT 900 Pro X carry a €249 MSRP.
All four headphones use beyerdynamic's STELLAR.45 drivers and feature a 48-ohm impedance rating, allowing them to be used with everything from professional audio interfaces to mobile devices. items.title: ESGAMING ZERO MAX targets GPU airflow with an angled bottom intake
items.content:
ESGAMING has detailed its ZERO MAX PC case, which pairs panoramic glass panels with an eight degree bottom air duct designed to direct cool air towards the graphics card. Available in black and white, it supports graphics cards up to 415mm long, up to ten 120mm fans and a 360mm radiator in the roof.
The bottom intake is the main talking point. Three fan mounts sit beneath the hardware, with the angled duct intended to aim incoming air more directly at the GPU. ESGAMING says this provides a more targeted intake path, although the release includes no temperature or noise measurements to show how that translates into performance.
Motherboard support covers ATX, Micro-ATX and Mini-ITX. The 415mm graphics card clearance leaves plenty of length to work with, though builders choosing a tower CPU cooler will need to pay attention to the 160mm height limit.
Cooling provision extends to ten 120mm fan positions across the chassis, with support for a top-mounted 360mm radiator. The release does not specify the supplied fan configuration, so we still need that detail to know what buyers get out of the box.
The power supply mounts vertically on the right side of the case. There are also mounts for two 3.5-inch hard drives and one 2.5-inch SSD, which should accommodate a couple of bulk storage drives alongside an SSD.
Front and left glass panels provide what ESGAMING describes as a 270-degree panoramic view of the build. The left panel uses 4mm tempered glass, while the choice of black or white extends the options for matching the chassis to the rest of the system.
Dust filters cover the top and bottom. Front I/O includes USB 3.0, USB Type-C rated at 20Gbps and HD audio.
ESGAMING may be a less familiar name to some readers, but the company says it has two decades of experience in the PC industry, producing cases, their own power supplies and cooling hardware. It reports that ZERO MAX sales have reached 200,000 units since launch, with exports concentrated in South America, the Middle East and Southeast Asia.
Jack Meng, founder of ESGAMING, said, “At ESGAMING, we have always believed that a great gaming PC case should not only look outstanding but also deliver a great experience in everyday use.
For the ZERO MAX, we set out to rethink how airflow is handled in conventional case designs. We adopted an innovative 8° tilted bottom structure that channels cool air more directly toward the GPU area. At the same time, we combined 270° panoramic tempered glass with strong hardware compatibility, aiming to give esports players and PC building enthusiasts a product that balances cooling flexibility, visual aesthetics, and the demands of high-performance builds.
As ESGAMING continues to expand its global market presence, we will continue to develop more innovative gaming hardware solutions for global clients and partners.”
We hope to get a hands on with this case in 2027 and deliver our own unbiased, indepth technical analysis.
KitGuru says The question for us is how much the angled intake helps GPU cooling at a given noise level. The case has room for large graphics cards and several cooling configurations, but the supplied fans, build quality and price will all influence its appeal. We would want to see those details and some thermal testing before drawing conclusions about the design.

The Fortnite Treasure Hour events give you the best chance to find the elusive Pirate Shop Token, which grants you 14 days of free Item Shop cosmetics. One week has already passed, and only a few Treasure Hours remain before the season ends.
Here is everything you need to know, including the increased odds of finding the rare Pirate Shop Token or the weekly Gold Outfit.
Key takeaways
Fortnite Treasure Hours significantly increase your odds of finding rare Treasures
The odds of finding the Weekly Gold Outfit are as low as 1 in 156,250
The odds of finding the Pirate Shop Access Token are as low as 1 in 68,750
The next two Treasure Hour dates are on Nov. 21 and Nov. 28
Fortnite Treasure Hunters will conclude on Saturday, Dec. 5

Epic Games previously released the full odds of finding the various Treasures available this season. The Weekly Gold Outfit, previously A$AP Rocky and now Lil’ Uzi Vert, has by far the highest odds at over 1 in 1.5 million.
However, the Pirate Shop Access Token has snatched most of the headlines, despite the lower odds. Players of all skill levels have spent thousands of hours searching Chests in hopes of finding it.
That’s where the Fortnite Treasure Hour events come into play, since they cut those odds significantly, from 1 in 137,500 to as low as 1 in 68,750. It’s worth taking advantage of these two-hour time windows to increase your chances.

According to well-known Fortnite leaker, HYPEX, the first Nov. 14 Treasure Hour peaked at over 10 million active players, with 7 million queuing into Battle Royale. While that’s a fraction of the over 44 million players that queued into Fortnite OG in 2023, it’s still a substantial number.
It’s safe to assume the player count will remain around these figures for the remainder of the Treasure Hunters season as the Pirate Token hunt continues.

items.title: League of Legends: New Dawn – New Summoner’s Rift, Client, and more
items.content:
League Next, the long-awaited update to Riot’s flagship MOBA, now has an official name: League of Legends: New Dawn. It will bring a new (likely integrated) client, an overhaul to Summoner’s Rift, updated champion visuals and gameplay, and more. Here’s everything we know about the New Dawn update.
League of Legends: New Dawn release date
Riot hasn’t publicly announced when the massive update is going live. However, we do know that it won’t be the first Season of 2027.
This leaves Seasons Two and Three, which places League of Legends: New Dawn’s release date anywhere between April and August 2027. This section will be updated once Riot reveals more information about New Dawn’s release date.
What is League of Legends: New Dawn?
League of Legends: New Dawn, previously known as “League Next,” is a massive overhaul to the client and game. It was revealed during the Grand Final of Worlds 2026, and we expect it to release sometime around mid-2027.
Preliminary information sent by Riot Games to esports.gg tells us that New Dawn will be an overhaul of League as a product.
New Client
We are finally getting a new client after a decade. The last time the client got an update this big was in 2017.
While Riot did not reiterate it, preliminary information about League Next heavily suggests that the client will be integrated into the game, instead of being a different program. Think more modern games like VALORANT, Overwatch, Dota 2, and Deadlock, whose lobby and party screen are completely unified with the game executable itself.
Hopefully, this brings an end to the seemingly endless amount of bugs we’ve had with the League Client.
New Summoner’s Rift
The map is getting a visual refresh, modernizing the game’s textures and shaking up the geography again.
Of course, Riot couldn’t help themselves and changed the jungle again. This time, though, there’s new terrain and possibly new mechanics.
Most importantly, the Dragon pit is now located along the length of the river (as opposed to the side). This eliminates the differences between the Blue and Red sides when it comes to entering and gaining priority over the Dragon pit.
We don’t know yet if the Baron pit is getting a similar change, which would make it closer to the Roshan pit from Dota 2. Regardless, this is one of the biggest changes to the Epic Monsters we’ve ever seen, possibly having the same or more impact than the Elemental Dragons and Baron Nashor variants.
New Champion and entity visuals
From early sneak peeks provided to esports.gg by Riot Games, we can tell that champions are getting new in-game visuals and models. Some of the champions’ modernized looks seem to be taken from League of Legends: Wild Rift, but it’s unclear whether the new engine supports the direct copy-paste or whether each model had to be ported over.
In the first scenario, then perhaps we can expect some Wild Rift-exclusive skins (like the K/DA HEATBRINGER skinline) to make their way over to League of Legends once New Dawn goes live.
The following champions and entities are confirmed to get new models:
Ashe
Ahri
Blitzcrank
Irelia
Kha’Zix
Master Yi
Morgana
Dragon
Minions
League of Legends: New Dawn, previously known as League Next, goes live in mid-2027.
